name: Lovable.dev
one_line: Lovable's homepage runs a continuously shifting blue-to-pink-to-orange gradient field as its signature hook.
design_notes: Background hex #f7f4ed (parchment cream) replaces the category's cold-white default; cream+coral color pairing vs. typical cool blue/slate; slab-serif display (Copernicus/Tiempos Headline) for h1/h2 against a humanist sans body.
take_what: A single slow-shifting gradient field as hero backdrop gives cheap motion and warmth behind an otherwise typographic hero.

name: Performative-UI
one_line: React library cataloging 27 AI-startup design clichés — aurora gradients, sparkle buttons, prompt heroes — as a knowing satire.
design_notes: Ships components named Aurora Gradient, TokenStream reveal, PromptHero, ChatBubble, sparkle/shimmer buttons, waitlist popovers, logo rows, stat counters — the 2026 AI-website vocabulary, shipped straight-faced as an installable kit.
take_what: A checklist of what to avoid — gradient text, sparkle CTAs, aurora blobs, token-stream loaders — so Astryx's site doesn't default into generic-AI-startup look.

name: ElevenLabs
one_line: ElevenLabs pairs a 15.1M-view launch video with a dark card-based homepage and a scrollable 2023-2026 research timeline as trust proof.
design_notes: Modular homepage split into ElevenCreative/ElevenAgents/ElevenAPI product rails. Embedded audio-player controls inline in marketing copy (playable proof, not screenshots). Animated metric callouts. Client-logo grid. Model-release timeline Aug 2023-May 2026 as credibility device.
take_what: A dated milestone timeline is a compact, scannable maturity signal, reusable for a design system's own release-history section.

name: World Labs (Marble)
one_line: Fei-Fei Li's $1B+ spatial-AI startup site: dark hero, bold sans headline 'Spatial Intelligence,' atmospheric 3D imagery, modular card grid.
design_notes: Dark theme base, white/light-gray text, bold large sans headline, full-width hero, three-column modular card grid (Community/Case Studies/Learn), atmospheric background imagery conveying 3D/spatial concepts, ellipse graphic motif, 'Explore →' hover affordances.
take_what: Atmospheric dark hero + modular 3-card grid pattern for translating an abstract capability (spatial intelligence) into scannable proof sections.

name: OpenAI.com — OpenAI Sans rebrand
one_line: OpenAI's first-ever rebrand: OpenAI Sans typeface, a pulsing 'Emotive Point' mark, Sora-textured imagery — the most-copied AI look of 2026.
design_notes: OpenAI Sans (w/ ABC Dinamo): rounded letterforms on a 'seed of life' grid. Grey/blue 'horizon' palette + lavender/electric-blue accents. 'Emotive Point': pulsing blue disc w/ watercolor swirls, animated across chat, web, docs. Imagery mixes photography w/ Sora textures.
take_what: A single recurring animated glyph (the 'point') as a portable brand anchor across chat, web, and docs, instead of a static logo lockup.

name: Stripe (stripe.com)
one_line: Stripe's first homepage redesign in six years (2026) — bento grid, WebGL wave gradient, GDP counter, docs woven directly into the marketing flow.
design_notes: Bento-box modular cards for product storytelling; animated purple/multi-hue WebGL wave gradient ('minigl'); weight-300 light type; live stat callouts (99.999% uptime, $1.9T, GDP counter); in-page modals instead of doc-site routing; accordion case studies.
take_what: Bento grid as a product-surface pattern; treat docs/technical proof as first-class marketing content via inline modals, not a separate silo.

name: shadcn/ui — Theming docs
one_line: shadcn/ui documents semantic token pairs (background/foreground) in OKLCH, with radius as one --radius var cascading via calc().
design_notes: Two-column docs: left nav by component, right "On This Page" index; tokens shown as OKLCH strings in live code blocks; dark mode redefines same tokens in .dark, toggled live; new "Rhea" style (tighter "Luma") via shadcn/create — denser spacing, smaller controls.
take_what: Single-variable cascading radius scale (--radius x calc) and paired semantic tokens documented as live copyable code, not a static spec page.

name: shadcn/ui
one_line: Category-defining 'copy the code' library — hero is one realistic dashboard mockup that swaps light/dark, not a swatch grid.
design_notes: Clean sans-serif, light/dark toggle in header. Full-width hero: one realistic finance-dashboard mockup (buttons, badges, alerts, dialogs in situ) re-skins light/dark live. Headline: 'The Foundation for your Design System.' Below: settings screens, live streaming chat demo.
take_what: One flagship realistic app-screen mockup as the entire hero visual, plus a small live streaming/typing demo as a motion flourish further down.

name: Cluely
one_line: Undetectable-AI meeting assistant whose dark-gradient site and 'cheat on everything' marketing repeatedly went viral on X.
design_notes: Hero is a full macOS desktop wallpaper mockup (Launchpad/Safari/Zoom/Cluely/Trash icons) under headline '#1 Undetectable AI for Meetings.' Light base with saturated purple/pink/blue gradient feature cards, 'Shimmer' animation, UI chrome demonstrating hiding during screen-share.
take_what: Gradient-washed dark section dividers and animated device-mockup carousels to demo a product across contexts without heavy video.

name: Vercel Geist — Introduction
one_line: Vercel's Geist hub organizes Foundations/Assets/Components/"Markdown for agents" under a monochrome ink-on-fog palette with its own Geist type family.
design_notes: Near-white #fafafa body, near-black #171717 ink, 200-step gray scale; custom Geist Sans/Mono plus new (Feb 2026) Geist Pixel bitmap-grid variant; minimal no-flourish docs hub; dedicated "Markdown for agents" section serves llms.txt-style docs beside human docs.
take_what: "Markdown for agents" docs section serving agent-readable markdown beside human docs — maps directly to an AGENTS.md-driven system.

name: Cursor (cursor.com)
one_line: AI coding agent's marketing site — often cited as "monospace on dark," but live site is a restrained light-mode base, monospace only on code.
design_notes: Bold sans-serif headline on a mostly white/light background (not the dark devtool look its reputation implies); testimonial cards w/ YC/NVIDIA/OpenAI logos; feature timeline 2022-2026; monospace curl-install snippet; minimal gradients, restraint over flash.
take_what: Prove restraint: skip dark/gradient theatrics, reserve monospace for code only, use timeline + logo-testimonial cards as a trust signal.

name: Cardboard
one_line: YC W26 agentic video editor with the batch's highest-upvoted HN launch (131 pts) — site pairs an oversized serif headline with a live embedded editor UI.
design_notes: Dark background, large elegant serif headline 'Edit videos in minutes, not hours' with a hand-drawn wavy underline, floating cropped video-clip thumbnails scattered around the hero, real editor canvas + chat-style 'AI director' panel below the fold.
take_what: Pair a display serif (breaking sans-serif SaaS default) with a real, interactive product screen embedded in the hero, not a static screenshot.

name: Anthropic's frontend-design SKILL.md (via Medium)
one_line: A 30-line Anthropic SKILL.md banning Inter/Space Grotesk/purple-on-white gradients is 2026's most-installed design doc (277k installs in 4 months).
design_notes: Bans specific defaults — Inter/Roboto/Arial/system fonts, especially Space Grotesk; purple gradients on white. Offers 11 selectable aesthetic directions (brutalist, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, editorial, art deco...) and pushes deliberate light/dark/font variation.
take_what: A named font/palette banlist steers an LLM away from generic output better than vague 'be creative' guidance — relevant to Astryx's own AGENTS.md.

name: Wembi
one_line: Virtual-twin device-performance startup; SOTD July 1 2026, lime-green/blue-gray brand with GSAP mouse interactions.
design_notes: High-contrast lime-green (#beff8b) + blue-gray (#9dbbc5) two-color palette, heavy GSAP animation on nav/menu/mouse interactions, smooth-scroll driven hero, otherwise minimal business-corporate layout.
take_what: Lime-on-neutral is an unusual but current tech-startup color signal worth adding to an Astryx example-theme gallery.

name: Mistral AI
one_line: European open-weight lab leans into 'French-engineered minimalism' with a purple-toned identity.
design_notes: Pixelated modular-block 'M' logo hiding a cat face; warm red/orange/yellow palette breaking from rivals' cool blues; dark charcoal/black bg, white type; looping pixel-art cat GIF; bold headline 'Frontier AI. In your hands.'
take_what: Purple/violet can stay premium paired with minimalist restraint rather than heavy gradient/glow — a middle path vs. SSI's austerity or a cosmic orb.

name: Apple Newsroom: Liquid Glass Announcement (June 2025)
one_line: Apple's own press release that coined 'Liquid Glass' — the primary-source definition every startup site now cites.
design_notes: June 2025 press release that coined 'Liquid Glass': translucent, 'behaves like glass,' color adapts to light/dark, specular highlights via real-time rendering. Tab bars shrink/expand on scroll; sidebars refract content; controls 'dynamically morph.' SF Pro type throughout.
take_what: Vocabulary (translucent, refract, specular highlight, adapt to light/dark) startup copy now borrows to describe glassmorphism 2.0.

name: HeroUI v3 (formerly NextUI)
one_line: July-2026 ground-up rewrite (React Aria + Tailwind v4) that moved every animation to pure CSS and shipped a praised OKLCH theme picker.
design_notes: Per InfoQ: built on React Aria Components + Tailwind v4, exposes CSS variables, OKLCH colors, BEM modifiers. 'Every animation moved to CSS, no JS runtime.' Ships 1:1-parity Figma Kit v3 and llms.txt for coding assistants. Reddit praised the themes page as 'pretty.'
take_what: All-CSS animation architecture (zero JS motion runtime) plus a well-received OKLCH theme-picker page and llms.txt for AI-agent doc consumption.

name: PostHog — Pricing
one_line: Usage-based pricing page built around a live cost calculator with sliders per product, plus deliberately irreverent copy and a co-founder trust note.
design_notes: Dark-leaning, modular vertical layout; interactive slider-based calculator (events, replays, flags) showing real-time $ totals; playful microcopy, mascot illustrations, competitor comparison matrix, joke CTA line.
take_what: Real-time usage calculator as an interactive component (slider + live price readout), plus voice-driven trust copy instead of legalese near price.

name: Perplexity AI
one_line: AI answer engine cited repeatedly in 2026 Framer-startup roundups as proof 'AI companies don't need cluttered landing pages.'
design_notes: Hero is a single dominant search bar with minimal surrounding chrome — radical restraint vs. the typical multi-section SaaS hero stack. A Framer-built Ronaldo campaign microsite (perplexity.ai/ronaldo) was a Best Storytelling finalist in the 2025 Framer Awards.
take_what: Single-input hero as the entire above-the-fold — a hero template option worth documenting for AI-product pages.

name: Apple.com — iOS 27 (Liquid Glass refinements)
one_line: Apple's current flagship iOS product page — the live surface using the refined, more-readable second-generation Liquid Glass.
design_notes: Live iOS 27 page: full-bleed multi-device hero on neutral black/white/gray, deep-blue/silver product imagery. Alternating text/image feature blocks. Liquid Glass now reads 'more uniform refraction, improved contrast,' plus a clarity slider from ultraclear to fully tinted.
take_what: Full-bleed device hero plus alternating text/image rhythm; the clarity slider as a pattern for making a bold effect user-configurable, not forced.

name: WWDC25 — 'Meet Liquid Glass' session
one_line: The WWDC talk that operationalized Liquid Glass into build rules: Regular vs Clear variants, nav-only placement, no glass-on-glass.
design_notes: WWDC25 session page, dark chrome, chaptered video hero. Defines 'Lensing' (dynamic light-bending), two variants — Regular (adaptive, everywhere) vs Clear (permanently transparent, media-only) — plus the rule: reserve glass for navigation, never stack glass-on-glass.
take_what: Rule set: reserve translucency for nav layer, never stack glass-on-glass, dim content under the Clear variant — portable to any component library adding glass.

name: Claude (Anthropic product surface)
one_line: Claude's cream/beige, italic-serif, terracotta interface has itself become a copied 'aesthetic' template other AI startups now clone.
design_notes: Design commentary: off-white/beige backgrounds, terracotta accents, large italic serif type, tracked-out subheads, minimal chrome (no shadows/avatars), thin borders fading into the page. DESIGN.md's library now sells a 'Claude Warm Parchment' preset copying the look.
take_what: One italic serif used sparingly on a quiet warm-neutral canvas — proof a light palette can become as recognizable a house style as dark-mode+purple.

name: Awwwards — Startups gallery
one_line: Awwwards' running curated gallery of award-winning startup marketing sites (Site of the Day/Developer Award), live through July 2026.
design_notes: Recent Site of the Day winners: Fauna Robotics (robotics, June 16), Wembi (July 1), EverSwap (June 22), Tresmares Capital (June 12); Honorable Mentions include Ponder AI and Armory AI Agency (June 10) — a real-time signal of which startup aesthetics design judges reward.
take_what: Ongoing sourcing pool for future trend scouting — bookmark /websites/startups/ and /websites/technology/ to catch newly-awarded sites early.

name: Linear
one_line: Repeatedly cited in 2026 write-ups as the standard-setter for product-first startup design, now refreshed toward warmer monochrome.
design_notes: Strict dark canvas: single lavender accent, one negative-tracking display family, no gradients/glassmorphism. Headline weight 300 whispers; hairline borders + surface lift carry hierarchy. Centered headline, two-line subhead, one CTA, no hero image.
take_what: The disciplined 'real product, dark UI, motion equals speed' formula is the sober baseline every gradient/AI-hype site reacts to.

name: Granola rebrand
one_line: AI notetaker Granola's mid-2026 rebrand deliberately roughens its mark to stop 'looking like any other SaaS company.'
design_notes: Pairs Quadrant (mechanical slab serif) with Melange (neutral UI font); hand-drawn, deliberately imperfect new logo instead of a 'committee-produced' mark; green retained but systematized into tokens; goal: 'rough around the edges, but sharp enough to feel serious.'
take_what: Slab-serif display + neutral UI font pairing as an anti-generic move; a deliberately imperfect logo mark as a trust signal against AI sameness.

name: Gumroad (neobrutalist redesign)
one_line: Gumroad's neobrutalist relaunch — thick borders, flat pink/yellow fills, oversized type — is the most-cited counter to polished SaaS gloss in 2026.
design_notes: Thick black outlines, flat pastel fills (hot pink, yellow), hard-edged non-blurred shadows, oversized blocky headline type; company-reported stronger brand recall vs. the prior polished design, per its own user survey.
take_what: Deliberate 'un-polish' as differentiation — hard shadows and flat saturated blocks instead of soft gradients/glassmorphism.

name: shadcn/ui — Accordion doc page
one_line: shadcn/ui's per-component page pairs a live interactive preview with tabbed install/code panels — the reference model for a doc-per-component library.
design_notes: 3-column layout: left component nav, center live demo + install tabs (pnpm/npm/yarn/bun), right TOC. Code blocks have copy + 'view code' toggle. Named variant demos (Basic, Multiple, Disabled, Borders, Card) stack below, each independently live and copyable.
take_what: Per-component page pattern: live demo first, then variant-by-variant live examples each with its own copyable snippet and install tabs.

name: OpenAI (homepage + brand identity)
one_line: OpenAI's first-ever full rebrand (OpenAI Sans typeface, 'blossom' logo, pulsing 'emotive point' disc) now skins openai.com and every ChatGPT surface.
design_notes: Grey/blue palette evoking 'horizons and skies' with accent colors; wordmark built from a perfectly-circular 'O'; grid based on six interlocking circles; black-circle 'point' motif recurs in letterforms/spacing; imagery mixes commissioned photography with Sora-generated textures.
take_what: One geometric primitive (circle/point) echoed in logo, cursor states, loading motion — a cohesion trick for a design system's own brand.

name: Webflow Blog — "8 web design trends to watch in 2026"
one_line: Webflow's 2026 trend report naming 8 patterns, each pinned to a specific live example site.
design_notes: 8 trends w/ exemplars: Springboards (hero anim), Anthropic (illustrative system), Pencil.dev (ASCII art), Rootly (UI in impressionist art), Tesoro (full color system), Dropbox Dash x McLaren (scroll speedometer), Flim (dot-grid canvas).
take_what: TL;DR pitch-deck nav and infinite-canvas patterns fit a docs-heavy design-system site: scannable overview + deep-dive on demand.

name: Web Design Trends 2026 (Muzli)
one_line: Muzli's 2026 roundup: AI in the design-production workflow, retro/brutalism as human fingerprint vs AI-perfect polish, sound design, 'Machine Experience'.
design_notes: Cites Shopify Supply for lightweight, emotionally-responsive 3D (Spline/React Three Fiber) done right; Unicorn Studio for no-code WebGL shaders (liquid distortion, cursor trails); predicts bold saturated gradients returning after years of minimalism.
take_what: 'Machine Experience' — structuring docs/marketing content for AI agents/crawlers, not just humans — relevant to a component-docs site.

name: xAI (Grok)
one_line: Elon Musk's AI lab site — stark monochrome futurism instead of the purple-gradient AI cliché.
design_notes: Black/white/grayscale palette, no color accents, minimal chrome, light/dark toggle; futuristic but restrained — reads as engineering lab, not hype gradient. ($200B+ valuation, 2026.)
take_what: Proves a design-system site can read as serious AI infra without gradient-orb theatrics — monochrome + typographic confidence as the 'AI look.'

name: Resend
one_line: Dev-tool email API site praised for oversized, confident headline typography that tells the story with zero hero imagery.
design_notes: Text-first, docs-focused hierarchy: concise tagline headline, no illustrations, sections organized by plain-language category (CLI, MCP server, docs) with terse copy and links. Oversized plain sans-serif against a neutral backdrop.
take_what: A hero can be a single confident sentence in oversized type with no supporting image — the type IS the visual.

name: Together AI
one_line: AI-native cloud platform; $800M Series C at $8.3B valuation, announced July 1 2026 (TechCrunch).
design_notes: Black/charcoal base, vivid blue-purple-orange accent geometry; hero built from layered translucent circles, hexagons, chevrons suggesting depth/motion; vertical card-grid body, generous whitespace; custom per-feature icon set (inference cloud, batch stack, compute cluster).
take_what: Tabbed hero panel that swaps supporting art per tab — shows multiple product pillars in one hero without a long scroll stack.

name: Framer Awards — 2025 Winners
one_line: Framer's own annual awards page: 2025 winners across storytelling, interactions, animation, visual design, and big-site categories.
design_notes: Winners span dark-minimal SaaS (miro.com) to expressive motion sites (bohdan.design, panton.vitra.com). Judge language repeats: 'light and calm,' 'super smooth motion,' 'bold colors,' 'clear and playful nav.'
take_what: Use winners as a swipe file for motion craft; judges' vocabulary ('light, calm, effortless') as a tone target.

name: Zed
one_line: High-buzz AI-era code editor leading with a text-only headline ("Your last next editor") over a dark, sparse canvas.
design_notes: Text-forward hero: bold sans-serif headline, concise descriptor, dual CTAs, dark bg with white/gray restraint, occasional blue accent. Images appear only as supporting evidence. Flourish: ASCII-style terminal logo, live commit-activity feed.
take_what: A text-only headline plus a live/functional data feed (activity, commits) can replace a decorative hero visual entirely.

name: Adobe Spectrum 2 — Homepage
one_line: Spectrum 2's homepage repeats a giant "The future is Spectrum 2" tagline as its hero, then routes via image cards into icons/implementation/foundations.
design_notes: Neutral, mostly-white background lets colorful component imagery pop. Hero headline echoes itself — 'The future is Spectrum 2Spectrum 2' — over a subtle SVG graphic. Single-column, generous whitespace. Visible 'Reduce motion' control. Six-card grid links deep-dive topics.
take_what: Visible "Reduce motion" toggle as first-class nav control; oversized repeated typographic tagline as hero device instead of illustration.

name: Ploy
one_line: YC W26 AI landing-page and growth-automation startup — meta-relevant, literally selling 'your website should work harder than you are.'
design_notes: Bold blunt headline ('Your website should be working harder than you are'); metric callout cards (+23% Traffic, 6 pages built) in a three-column Web/Grow/Ads layout; timestamped overnight-automation timeline (11:42PM-07:55AM); scrolling logo strip; avatar-based social proof.
take_what: A timestamped activity-log device (a fake overnight feed of the product working) makes an abstract 'automation' claim concrete and visual.

name: Ponder AI
one_line: AI video-editing SaaS; Awwwards Honorable Mention for high-contrast black/white minimalism with WebGL scroll storytelling.
design_notes: Two-tone palette (#f1f1f1 off-white / #020202 near-black) for stark contrast; GSAP+WebGL+Webflow-driven scroll and step animations, mobile-menu and pricing micro-interactions, three embedded product videos in hero/pricing.
take_what: Scroll-triggered 'steps' sections that explain a product visually — a pattern for an Astryx docs/features page.

name: Wembi.ai
one_line: Wembi.ai won Awwwards Site of the Day + Developer Award (Jul 1, 2026), tagged under GSAP animation and clean-design categories.
design_notes: Couldn't render directly (403); per Awwwards categorization it combines GSAP-driven motion with a 'clean' visual language — signals restrained-but-animated is the current award-winning combo, not maximalist WebGL.
take_what: GSAP-class scroll/hover choreography on a clean base, not heavy 3D — matches what StyleX transitions/keyframes can achieve without a WebGL dependency.

name: DESIGN.md Library
one_line: 461 markdown design systems for AI coding agents — incl. 2026-era systems like 'AI Cinematic Creative' and dark-SaaS/glassmorphism patterns.
design_notes: Presets built around this counter-trend: 'Paper & Ink' (literary, paper-and-ink, classic serif), 'Claude Warm Parchment' ('inspired by Claude/Anthropic'), 'Notion Warm Workspace' (warm minimalism), 'Vintage Editorial' (witty serif personality).
take_what: Same species as Astryx's own docs/AGENTS.md — markdown-encoded design systems for LLM consumption is itself a live 2026 pattern worth studying.

name: Onlook
one_line: YC W25 open-source "Cursor for Designers" — #1 GitHub trending above DeepSeek, 8500+ stars, #1 on Hacker News.
design_notes: Dark-background hero, centered text-forward headline with dual CTA (Book a Demo / Sign Up), a full customizable brand-color swatch strip, and an embedded live product mockup using a deliberately funny example project ("Villainterest") for personality.
take_what: Put a genuinely funny custom demo project in the hero product-mockup instead of generic placeholder UI to make an abstract dev tool concrete.

name: Gemini app — 'Neural Expressive' redesign
one_line: Gemini's full redesign: pulsating blue-white gradient homepage, centered oversized greeting, pill-shaped prompt bar, thin rounded icon set.
design_notes: Blue-and-white pulsating gradient homepage intensifies once a chat starts. Centered 'Hi [name], what's on your mind?' greeting above the spark icon. Pill-shaped prompt bar w/ voice input. Thin rounded-outline icons. Model picker moved to a top-left dropdown.
take_what: A centered, oversized conversational greeting as the hero — instead of headline+subhead — worth offering as an 'AI product hero' template.

design_notes: Changelog: Mar 5 2026 added 'Spring' physics to mouse tracking/momentum; Mar 18 added mouse->translate tracking on Transform; Mar 19 added mouse-reactive dynamic outline thickness. Embeds into Framer/Webflow/any site — engine behind agency cursor heroes.
name: Unicorn Studio (no-code WebGL tool)
one_line: No-code WebGL builder ships spring-physics mouse tracking and mouse-reactive outlines — the toolchain behind 2026's cursor-trail wave.
take_what: Spring-physics mouse tracking gives hero CTAs a magnetic hover feel without hand-rolled shader code — evaluate short of a full custom cursor.

name: Apple Developer — Design Gallery (Liquid Glass adopters)
one_line: Apple's self-curated gallery of third-party apps adopting Liquid Glass — the origin's own exemplar showcase.
design_notes: Apple's own curated gallery: card grid (HIG, Resources, Icon Composer, SF Symbols), video rail led by 'Meet Liquid Glass,' Design-Award 'developer stories' with real app-UI thumbnails, plus linked before/after comparisons of third-party apps (Crumbl, CNN) adopting Liquid Glass.
take_what: The before/after (old UI vs Liquid Glass) comparison format as a persuasive device — directly reusable for an Astryx migration/adoption gallery.

name: Mintlify Themes 2.0
one_line: Mintlify ships 10 named, swappable docs themes (Quill, Prism, Venus...) treating documentation visual identity as a first-class product surface.
design_notes: Named theme system: Quill = clean/sharp/uncluttered for content-forward brands; Prism = bold gradient color; Venus = built for API/SDK-heavy nav density. Full Shiki syntax-theme library lets code blocks carry brand color.
take_what: Treat the docs/component-doc theme as a named, swappable design product, not a skin — code blocks should carry brand color too.

name: bolt.new
one_line: AI vibecoding builder whose single-tweet launch clip has 55.6M X views — #1 in Launch Library's tracked set, ahead of 1X's headline robot demo.
design_notes: Light-mode chat-prompt-first hero: 'What will you build today?' input box as primary CTA. Logo wall of design-system integrations (Material, Chakra, shadcn) and brands. Persona-segmented feature sections, stat callouts, infographic illustrations, minimal motion.
take_what: Chat-prompt-box-as-hero-CTA pattern instead of a button, plus persona-segmented feature sections below the fold.

name: studiomeyer.io — Web Design Trends 2026: Reality Check
one_line: Six-month reality-check on 2026 trend predictions: bento/dark-mode won, WebGL/kinetic-type mostly didn't ship.
design_notes: Held: bento (default now, +23% scroll depth); dark mode (82%+ users, +18% sessions). Overpromised: kinetic type (a11y/SEO conflicts); glassmorphism (15-30% FPS drop, mid-tier Android). Surprise: llms.txt now non-negotiable; anti-grid brutalism cited via Browser Company, v0.dev.
take_what: Skip WebGL/kinetic-type hero flourishes (rarely ships, perf/a11y tax); invest in a well-executed bento layout plus dark-mode-default theming instead.

name: Koah
axis: SPC: native ad network for AI
one_line: SPC-seeded, Theory Ventures Series A $20.5M Feb 2026, 'AdSense for AI' embedding contextual ads in AI chat/agent experiences.
design_notes: Custom editorial type: STK Bureau Sans (grotesk) + STK Bureau Serif + Geist Mono. H1 44-69px font-light, tracking -0.04em, serif-italic accent word mid-headline. Cream bg #FAF8F5, ink-blue #105DA8. Mountain-photo hero, publisher-logo strip.
take_what: Grotesk + serif-italic accent word inside one headline for editorial texture; warm cream+ink-blue as alternative to dark-mode-default.

name: Retro and brutalist UI design: a 2026 field guide
one_line: Field guide splitting the 2026 retro wave into three lanes: raw brutalism, Y2K chrome revival, OS-window pastiche; examples Gumroad, Are.na, Vercel.
design_notes: Names Gumroad, Are.na, Vercel as brutalist canon; Poolsuite FM, Cosmos for Y2K; 98.css/system.css for OS revival. Prescribes mono faces (Berkeley Mono), border-radius killed for hard 8px offset shadows, low-easing motion. Flags sub-16px pixel fonts and link-blue as WCAG failures.
take_what: A componentized vocabulary (hard borders, zero radius, link-blue, monospace) for an optional 'raw/technical' theme variant beyond Astryx's polished default.

name: Google Labs DESIGN.md + Meng To (@MengTo) breakdown on X
one_line: Google Labs open-sourced DESIGN.md, a markdown spec letting coding agents generate brand-consistent UI; design-Twitter's Meng To broke down why it matters.
design_notes: Not a visual style but a spec: combines machine-readable tokens with human-readable design reasoning ('what and why') so agents apply brand consistently; portable as plain markdown across Stitch, coding agents, repos, and builders.
take_what: Direct precedent validating Astryx's AGENTS.md-driven component docs as a 2026 category — worth positioning against/cross-referencing explicitly.

name: U.S. Graphics Company (Berkeley Mono)
one_line: Foundry behind Berkeley Mono, the most-coveted paid monospace of 2026, now v2 with 5 widths/12 weights/2 slants; used by Perplexity and Cartesia.
design_notes: Positioned as 'a love letter to the golden era of computing' — engineered for code legibility but reads equally well 'etched on control panels' or on a magazine cover. Variable-font width/weight/slant axes.
take_what: A single well-executed monospace can anchor an entire brand system if given enough weight/width variation to avoid monotony.

name: Vercel — Geist Pixel launch
one_line: Vercel's Feb 2026 Geist Pixel: bitmap-grid typeface (5 variants, 480 glyphs) extending open-source Geist into pixel/terminal territory.
design_notes: Glyphs manually refined on a strict pixel grid to avoid 'visual noise, uneven weight, awkward diagonals' — early-screen inspiration engineered for shipped products. Parent Geist family: 1.5M+ Google Fonts downloads, 2,100+ sites.
take_what: Release a type family as a design-system artifact (Sans/Mono/Pixel variants) to signal serious infra, paired with the component library itself.

name: Safe Superintelligence (SSI)
one_line: Ilya Sutskever's SSI runs the opposite play — an almost bare text page with zero cosmic gradients, zero orbs, zero motion.
design_notes: Minimalist, text-only hierarchy — headline ('Superintelligence is within reach'), body copy, three footer links (Apply/Updates/Contact); no imagery, no dark-gradient hero, no visual flourish at all.
take_what: At the top of AI-lab credibility, restraint reads as confidence — a hero-graphic-free page is a legitimate alternative to gradient/orb spectacle.

name: Google Design — Gemini AI Visual Design system
one_line: Google's own writeup of Gemini's visual grammar: gradients as semantic motion, circles as the foundational shape, blurred ethereal Material forms.
design_notes: Gradients are the core grammar: sharp opaque leading edge diffusing at the tail = 'directional momentum.' Circles (from Google's 4-color dots) concentrate to a point then 'blossom' outward. Motion has defined start/end points signaling active thinking, not decoration.
take_what: Treat gradient motion as a semantic 'system is working' signal, not decorative background noise — apply to async component loading states.

name: Apple Developer — Liquid Glass Technology Overview
one_line: Apple's canonical technical definition of the material — primary source for 'hierarchy through depth' as a design principle.
design_notes: Official tech-overview doc: defines Liquid Glass as a 'digital meta-material' that bends/shapes light, behaves 'organically like a lightweight liquid.' Introduces 'hierarchy through depth' — importance via transparency/refraction/weight, not color contrast or size.
take_what: 'Hierarchy through depth' as an alternative to color-contrast-driven hierarchy — worth testing on component elevation/z-order in a design system.

name: Mintlify
one_line: AI-era docs platform (raised $45M Series B at $500M valuation, Apr 2026) whose own site sells documentation as knowledge infrastructure.
design_notes: Light/dark hero shows paired doc-preview screenshots; animated live stat counters (pages read, search/API requests); monochrome customer-logo strip; card-grid feature sections; clean sans-serif type, blue accent CTAs.
take_what: Live animated usage-stat counters and paired light/dark product screenshots in the hero as instant proof of polish.

name: Perplexity Comet
one_line: Chromium-based AI browser with a persistent sidebar agent that reads and highlights the page it's acting on.
design_notes: Sidebar assistant lives beside the page, not a pop-out; blue outline frames appear over content the AI is reading, as a live transparency cue; replies render as structured, source-cited cards; customizable widget home page. Reviewers call the UI clean, familiar, zippy.
take_what: The 'AI is reading this' highlight-frame affordance and sidebar-as-workspace pattern — reusable transparency device for an AI-assistant surface.

name: Tines — Pricing
one_line: Ditches the 3-column grid for a narrative two-card (Community vs Custom) layout with illustrated hero and a 'Specialized Editions' section.
design_notes: Large colorful abstract-shape hero illustration (purple/teal/orange accents); two asymmetric tier cards with bullet lists instead of a feature grid; G2 badges and customer logos placed near price; extensive FAQ; startup-program callout.
take_what: Alternative to N-column pricing tables — a narrative two-card layout for cases where a feature grid undersells a flexible/enterprise product.

name: Pocket (heypocket.com)
one_line: AI voice note-taking wearable; $11M raised (Accel, YC, ElevenLabs CEO), announced June 29 2026 (TechCrunch).
design_notes: White/off-white minimalist palette with blue accents; bento-style six-box grid of named use-case vignettes ('On the go', 'Client calls'); staggered testimonial cards; arrow-nav carousels; candid lifestyle photography of real professionals rather than glossy stock/renders.
take_what: Bento grid of named use-case vignettes paired with authentic (non-glossy) photography — humanizes a technical hardware product.

name: v0.app (formerly v0.dev)
one_line: v0 (formerly v0.dev) rebranded to v0.app in 2026; homepage leads with a conversational prompt box ('What do you want to create?') over a template grid.
design_notes: Large bold sans-serif headline as literal chat input; light/near-white background, dark text, neutral palette letting template thumbnails carry color; feature cards ('Sync with a repo', 'Integrate with apps'); template grid of user-built projects as social proof.
take_what: Prompt-box-as-hero (input field doubling as headline) plus a 'built with this' gallery as trust-proof — translates to a 'built with Astryx' showcase grid.

name: ElevenLabs Store
one_line: AI voice unicorn ElevenLabs runs a minimal, fashion-brand-style storefront as a design flex, distinct from its core product site.
design_notes: Tagged eCommerce / Minimal / Fashion on Landing.love — stripped-back editorial layout, more Aesop-boutique than SaaS-dashboard, deliberately unlike ElevenLabs' main product marketing site.
take_what: A spin-off microsite with a totally different, more editorial visual voice than the core product — brand extension as design statement.

name: Fauna Robotics (faunarobotics.com)
one_line: Humanoid-robot startup (Sprout) site; Awwwards Site of the Day June 16 2026, 7.39/10.
design_notes: Minimal two-tone palette (#EFEFEF light gray, #D1E3FF soft blue); grid-based feature storytelling; video-led immersive hero introducing the robot's character rather than static product shots; illustration/icon work; micro-interaction-heavy 'wizard' UI components.
take_what: Pastel two-tone palette + illustrated mascot softens a technical product — a model for humanizing a design-system's own illustration/mascot work.

name: Cognition (Devin)
one_line: Devin-maker's site (13x ARR growth in 12mo) uses numbered-section storytelling (01-04) instead of visual spectacle to sell an autonomous coding agent.
design_notes: Numbered progressive sections (01 hero mission, 02 customer logos, 03 recruiting CTA, 04 blog grid), bold display headline, minimal chrome, Next.js image-optimized blog thumbnails, restrained non-decorative layout prioritizing proof over flourish.
take_what: Numbered-section narrative scaffold turns a linear pitch into a scannable proof sequence without relying on 3D/WebGL spectacle.

name: terminal.shop (Charm)
one_line: Coffee company ordered entirely via `ssh terminal.shop` — the site is a plain monospace README that hands off to a TUI checkout.
design_notes: Dark terminal-style page, monospace throughout, `=` ASCII dividers, bracketed nav (terminal/cron/api/readme/faq), hero CTA is literally the `ssh terminal.shop` command, no imagery/gradients — the product IS the interface.
take_what: Make the primary CTA a copy-pasteable command/snippet instead of a button+screenshot; let the hero be literal code.

name: Lando Norris — official site
one_line: OFF+BRAND's F1-driver site won 2026 Awwwards Site of the Year AND Users' Choice — built in Webflow, not custom code.
design_notes: 3D helmet rotation, Rive animations (not just GSAP/Lottie), scroll-driven cinematics choreographed like a highlight reel. Notably shipped on Webflow, proving no-code tooling can win top-tier awards over bespoke builds.
take_what: Rive for lightweight vector animation is a cheaper hero-moment alternative to full WebGL; a no-code stack doesn't cap award-tier polish.

name: Base UI — Accordion doc page
one_line: Base UI's component pages document unstyled primitives via an anatomy diagram, data-attribute state hooks, and CSS-variable reference beside the props table.
design_notes: Left nav (Overview/Handbook/Components/Utils), center content with an Anatomy section, live demo with CSS Modules/StackBlitz tabs, structured Prop/Type/Default table. Documents data-* attributes and CSS vars (e.g. --accordion-panel-height) as styling hooks.
take_what: Document the styling/state contract explicitly — an anatomy section plus a table of data-attributes and CSS variables consumers can hook into, not just props.

name: HF0 Residency
one_line: 12-week SF residency for repeat founders (10 teams/batch, $1M uncapped SAFE) whose W26/S26 2026 cohort produced the startups below.
design_notes: White/off-white bg, minimal nav. Hero is a single animated 'sliced sphere' GIF rotating 25fps — no screenshots, no photography. Tagline 'The residency for repeat founders' in clean sans-serif, understated CTAs. Sparse, confident, near-zero visual noise.
take_what: One abstract looping 3D object as the entire hero visual instead of screenshots — signals confidence with near-zero visual noise.

name: Wispr Flow
one_line: Mac/cross-platform voice-dictation app that recurred across multiple June-July 2026 PH weekly/daily leaderboards.
design_notes: Hero is a dramatic before/after text transformation, not a screenshot; waveform graphics recur; neutral palette lets colorful in-app screenshots pop; pricing hidden behind a dropdown favoring a free-trial CTA; social proof uses named individuals over logos.
take_what: Before/after transformation demo (raw input vs polished output) as the clearest way to prove an AI feature's value.

name: Poke (Interaction Company of California)
one_line: Personal AI agent that texts back like a friend, not a dashboard — TechCrunch-covered 2026 breakout with 10x user growth.
design_notes: Neutral white/light-gray canvas, dark type, vertical modular sections. Conversational voice ('real as a friend'), named AI personalities (Mars, Claudia, Andrew), real Twitter testimonials replace feature bullets, 30+ integration logos, Free-Forever tier.
take_what: Voice-led marketing over feature-bullets; naming the AI personalities turns a utility into a character; testimonial-as-hero instead of a stock feature grid.

name: AI in Design Report 2026 (stateofaidesign.com)
one_line: Second annual report; 900+ designers surveyed, interviews at Anthropic/Stripe/Notion/Shopify/Linear/Framer; site itself is big-type minimal.
design_notes: Report site uses the same Big-Type/Minimal Siteinspire-tagged aesthetic (large display type hero, full-width imagery, generous negative space) as the startup sites it studies — form matches content.
take_what: Half of designers now ship AI-generated code to production — Astryx docs should favor copy-pasteable, agent-ready code over abstract prop tables.

name: 10 Trends Creatives Are So Over in 2026 (Creative Boom)
one_line: Designer-fatigue list naming which mid-2026 clichés (AI slop, liquid glass, gradients, bento grids, empty motion) curdled from fresh to default.
design_notes: Calls out AI slop; Liquid-Glass-triggered glassmorphism backlash; golden-hued default AI-tool gradients; 'lazy minimalism' vs 'lazy maximalism'; Canva/template homogeneity; hollow Y2K nostalgia; bento grids now 'omnipresent'; empty decorative motion.
take_what: Negative checklist for a 2026 site: no gold-gradient hero, no glass-panel cards, no unmotivated motion, no bento-because-everyone-else-did.

name: MadeGoodDesigns — "Font Trends 2026: 12 Type Movements"
one_line: Comprehensive 2026 taxonomy: 12 named type movements (bouba grotesks, retro monospace revival, brutalist display, cyberpunk display, anti-AI handwriting).
design_notes: Describes a shift from stark minimalism to 'quiet luxury': earthy/muted palettes (warm beige, olive, charcoal replacing black/white), custom elegant serif headline fonts, asymmetrical layouts, oversized headlines as design elements themselves.
take_what: Pick ONE movement deliberately (bouba grotesk for warmth, or retro-mono for dev-tool feel) instead of blending signals into one incoherent system.

name: Rive
one_line: Interactive-animation-engine startup (Series A) whose homepage is built entirely from its own live Rive files.
design_notes: Rive-native animations respond live to scroll position and cursor movement, including character animations — every motion element is an actual interactive Rive graphic, not a video/GIF (School of Motion 2026 roundup).
take_what: Homepage IS the product demo — every animation is a live instance of the thing being sold, not a rendered video.

name: getdesign.md
one_line: A catalog of reverse-engineered 'DESIGN.md' style guides scraped from real AI-company sites, built for feeding to AI coding agents.
design_notes: Catalog organized by company category (automotive, fintech, AI platforms, big tech); each entry outputs a spec-style markdown doc of color palette, typography, spacing, component patterns, and design rationale, following a Google-authored DESIGN.md spec format.
take_what: A ready benchmark set for Astryx's identity vs. named AI-lab archetypes, and a model for publishing its own machine-readable design-tokens doc.

name: Basecase Capital (basecase.vc)
one_line: Alana Goyal's seed fund runs a text-first, bracket-notation, theme-togglable site reading like a terminal profile rather than a fund brochure.
design_notes: Linear text-heavy layout, `[website]` `[twitter]` `[blog]` bracket-style nav links (code-editor convention), live "change theme color" toggle implying multiple accent palettes, no hero image — copy IS the hero ("basecase writes the first check...").
take_what: Bracket-notation link styling plus a user-facing accent-color toggle turn theming into a visible interactive feature, not hidden chrome.

name: opencode.ai (SST)
one_line: SST's open-source "AI coding agent built for the terminal" leads with a raw curl-install one-liner instead of a product screenshot.
design_notes: Grayscale-only palette (blacks/whites/mid-grays), bold sans hero headline, monospace `curl -fsSL ... | bash` install block as the primary visual, star/contributor counts as social proof, minimal borders, no gradients.
take_what: Lead the hero with a single monospace install/quickstart command plus a stripped grayscale palette.

name: Wispr Flow (rebrand)
one_line: AI dictation startup's 2026 rebrand trades SaaS-dashboard darkness for a cream, magazine-Sunday editorial system.
design_notes: Cream/soft-neutral palette (Lumen/Pulse), subtle green CTA accents; Figtree sans paired with an editorial serif for headlines; wide margins, two-column 'editorial Sunday' layout; hand-sketched illustrations of people mid-thought; slow-fade microinteractions.
take_what: Dual-typeface contrast (functional sans + expressive serif) and hand-drawn illustration as a warmth signal against generic AI iconography.

name: Apple.com — Apple Vision Pro
one_line: The visionOS product page — the acknowledged design ancestor of Liquid Glass's depth-and-translucency language, still live today.
design_notes: Vision Pro page: minimalist neutral white/gray/black, oversized headline ('seamlessly blends digital content with your physical space'), hero shot of a person wearing the device to sell see-through optics. 'View in your space' AR module; vertical alternating category sections.
take_what: Selling transparency/depth via literal optical product photography, not abstract CSS blur; equal-weight alternating category sections as a feature tour.

name: GitHub Primer — Homepage
one_line: Primer's homepage splits into three offerings — Product UI, Brand toolkit, Brand UI — then a "Shared Foundations" grid, glued by illustration and octicons.
design_notes: Minimal light-mode default with "Switch to dark mode" toggle; bold hero ("The design system for GitHub") with immediate CTA before the three-pillar split; card sections each carry dedicated illustration; "Shared Foundations" grid surfaces cross-cutting tokens at a glance.
take_what: Splitting the docs site into named offering tracks so visitors self-route by what they're building, before shared token foundations.

name: Stripe — Tour of the API
one_line: Stripe's docs use the industry-defining three-column layout (nav / prose / live code) that turns reference material into a guided, copy-paste tutorial.
design_notes: Persistent left nav, center narrative prose with inline cross-links to object types (PaymentIntent, PaymentMethod, Charge, Event), embedded state-transition diagram and video walkthrough; live language-switchable code samples live on adjacent reference pages.
take_what: Three-column doc shell (nav / narrative / live code) with inline cross-linked object/type names — link component prose straight to its own doc page.

name: Baseten
one_line: AI inference platform closed a $1.5B split-priced Series F (June 2026, $13B valuation); inference volume passed 1B calls/day.
design_notes: Black-on-white minimal palette, single blue CTA accent; oversized hero 'Inference is everything'; customer-logo row (Notion, HubSpot, Clay) right under fold; horizontally-scrolling model-library grid with 'Try it' links; rotating testimonial carousel.
take_what: Near-monochrome palette plus one accent keeps a huge feature surface legible; scrollable model-library grid for many discrete offerings.

name: Web Design Trends 2026: What Actually Held Up After Six Months
one_line: Six-month check on 2026 trends: bento + dark-mode-default won, kinetic type and heavy WebGL flopped, anti-grid brutalism emerged as the real surprise.
design_notes: Bento grids now default across Apple/Google/Microsoft/Spotify, ~half of YC W26 demo-day startups (+23% scroll depth vs 12-col); dark-mode-default crossed threshold (82%+ mobile, +18% sessions); kinetic type flopped; counter-trend 'anti-grid brutalism' at Browser Co, v0.dev.
take_what: A named counter-trend (brutalism vs bento) plus a hard new baseline (llms.txt/agents.json/schema) a docs-heavy site should treat as infra, not decor.

name: Fourmula AI
one_line: AI visual-asset generation platform; Awwwards Site of the Day May 2 2026, built by Fourmeta agency.
design_notes: Stark 2-color palette: near-black #020108 background, saturated orange #FF6B02 accent; GSAP-driven scroll/transition animation, Webflow build; typography-forward, high-contrast dark UI — the dominant 2026 AI-product look.
take_what: Single-accent-on-black formula (one saturated hue against near-black) reads premium/technical without gradients — portable to a dark-theme hero.

name: Hallucinate
one_line: A no-login massively multiplayer 3D rave — low-poly club full of live strangers dancing to a synced DJ set — went viral and crashed its own servers.
design_notes: Low-poly 3D WebGL club scene rendered in-browser, real-time multiplayer avatars, dead-reckoning client-authoritative sync for smooth motion at scale; no accounts, no ads, MIT-licensed source.
take_what: Shows real-time collaborative 3D-in-browser is technically approachable now — a reference point for what 'viral' looks like vs. safe SaaS templates.

name: Vercel.com
one_line: Vercel's marketing site is repeatedly cited as the reference bento-grid implementation, with full dark/light adaptive theming.
design_notes: Per trend write-ups: minimalist restrained palette, bento-grid tiles organizing feature set, automatic dark/light matching OS setting, interactive buttons embedded directly in headline copy rather than separate CTAs.
take_what: Bento-tile feature grid + theme-adaptive palette is the most-cited 2026 dev-tool layout — maps directly to an Astryx homepage grid using existing tokens.

name: Mercury
one_line: Startup banking platform cited repeatedly in 2026 fintech-design roundups as the reference for 'banking designed like a tech product.'
design_notes: Agency case study: 'traded the cold, transactional feel of traditional banking for warmth, care, and intention' via refined typography, elevated still-life product photography, and structured grids; identity and web design treated as one unified project.
take_what: Pairing dark-mode chrome with real in-product screenshots made a 'boring' category feel design-forward — applicable to a component library showing live UI.

name: Cartesia AI
one_line: Voice-AI startup's ODA identity leans on Berkeley Mono to fuse 'golden era of computing' nostalgia with ML research credibility.
design_notes: Identity balances 'industrial research, fundamental engineering, and useful products' via Berkeley Mono's UNIX-terminal, control-panel-etched aesthetic — old publishing conventions meeting techy monospace precision.
take_what: Monospace-as-brand-voice: use one premium mono typeface across marketing surfaces, not just code blocks, to signal engineering rigor.

name: Charm (charm.land)
one_line: "We make the command line glamorous" — Charm brands each CLI/TUI library (Bubble Tea, Lip Gloss, Gum, Glow) with a mascot, terminal-native visuals.
design_notes: Dark background, sans headers over monospace product names, per-library mascot illustrations, product photography of physical merch (gum packs, roller skates) alongside 25k+ app adoption stats — playful, zero gradient/glass.
take_what: One consistent mascot/icon per component family turns a library into a legible cast — could mark Astryx component categories similarly.

name: Radix UI Themes — Theme overview docs
one_line: Radix Themes' overview page pairs live component variants with a card grid to per-token pages (Color/Typography/Spacing/Radius/Shadow/Cursor).
design_notes: Neutral base, swappable accent (e.g. mint); classic/solid/soft button variants shown side by side; realistic panels ground props instead of isolated swatches; bottom card grid indexes per-token pages; live Playground link.
take_what: Card-grid token index at page foot routing to per-token deep-dives; grounding props in realistic mini-UI, not isolated swatches.

name: Park UI (Panda CSS / Ark UI) — Homepage
one_line: Park UI markets "Build your own Design System" and demos components as fully functional sign-up forms, payment flows, and product cards, not static mockups.
design_notes: Headline framed as a builder-tool pitch, not a component gallery; banner ("Park UI x Chakra — it's official!") signals headless-UI vendor consolidation; React/Solid toggle previews same components across stacks; every showcase is a working pattern (auth form, payment picker).
take_what: Embedding components in complete functional real-world flows (a whole sign-up form, payment picker) on the homepage rather than isolated swatches.

name: Motion (motion.dev)
one_line: Homepage for the Motion animation library, built as a running demo of its own primitives, with a free MotionScore performance auditor.
design_notes: Modular FIG.01-FIG.08 sections pair a punchy headline ("Independent transforms", "Scroll animation") with inline code + a live demo card (parallax, confetti, typewriter, shimmer); ticker marquee "MOTION▲ 2.4%"; dark code-forward look; free audit tool as lead magnet.
take_what: Site-as-proof pattern: each homepage section is a live instance of the library's own primitives, not a screenshot; a free audit tool doubles as a growth hook.

name: Manus AI invite codes as tradeable social currency
one_line: Manus skipped position numbers and let invite codes circulate on X/Discord as scarce tradeable currency, generating organic UGC around access itself.
design_notes: No visible counter — reporting describes bare invite-code fields shared via Discord 'Referral Megathread' and #ManusIM, codes granting credits to both parties. Fetching manus.im in July 2026 shows the gate is now gone (product folded into Meta).
take_what: Access-as-currency framing: a code with a visible reward split reads as generous, not gatekept.

name: Modal Labs
one_line: Serverless AI compute platform closed a $355M Series C (May 21, 2026, $4.65B valuation) led by General Catalyst and Redpoint.
design_notes: Dark-navy hero fading to white/gray cards, soft light-green accent; bold headline 'AI infra developers love'; alternating text/visual blocks per workload; metric-led testimonial cards (65% latency cut); animated Lottie logomark; thin divider rules between sections.
take_what: Metric-forward testimonial cards, alternating text/visual workload sections — numbers as trust signal, not generic quotes.

name: Rain
one_line: Stablecoin payments platform raised $250M Series C at $1.95B valuation (Jan 2026), third round in under a year.
design_notes: Brand-pink accent on white/neutral base; hero 'Stablecoin payments for the tokenized future' over layered globe imagery; scrolling client-logo carousel; accordion product sections; chip-style icons; compliance badge cluster; pink CTAs with arrow icons.
take_what: Single dominant brand-accent color on neutral base for recognizability; accordion pattern to compress dense product/compliance detail.

name: Fauna Robotics
one_line: Humanoid-robot startup Sprout; $30M seed in 2025, Amazon-acquired March 2026, Awwwards Site-of-the-Day June 16 2026.
design_notes: Predominantly white/gray/black 2-color palette (per Awwwards) letting product video lead; embedded hero video behind 'Request Robot' CTA; trust-badge row (Disney, Boston Dynamics, academic partners); modular use-case cards; UGC carousel. Score 7.39/10, designer O0 PRO.
take_what: Restrained 2-color palette + character illustration makes a technical/scary category (robotics) feel approachable without going full playful-startup cliche.

name: The Browser Company
one_line: Maker of Arc/Dia; named by trend articles as an anti-grid 'brutalist' counter to bento consensus, though its live homepage now reads calm not raw.
design_notes: Deliberately austere: minimal header (logo, theme toggle, nav), no hero image/video, plain statement copy ('We're building better ways to use the internet with Dia and Arc'), no visible motion, sans-serif only, neutral black/white/gray — reads as raw HTML, not a designed page.
take_what: Warm cream + one saturated blue as a calm alternative to bento-polish; italic centered heading with embedded inline product links.

name: Landdding — Bento Grid by Website Category
one_line: Bento-grid usage by category — SaaS (Linear, Vercel, Raycast), AI tools (Perplexity, ElevenLabs) — as dominant 2026 layout.
design_notes: SaaS bento pages: +31% time-on-page. Portfolio bento use +240% 2024-2026 on Webflow/Framer. E-commerce bento attempts: -14% conversion. Framed as feature-card grids replacing single-scroll dev-tool pages.
take_what: A bento tile grid (dominant card + capability cards) is the top-consensus layout for a feature section.

name: "7 Best AI Startup Landing Page Examples in 2026" (ebaqdesign)
one_line: Curated 2026 roundup of AI-startup landing pages (Flow, Sahara AI, Composio, Snowglobe, Meridian, Jupi) with per-site design breakdowns.
design_notes: Spans cream-editorial (Flow/Wispr), grid+3D (Sahara), gradient-refraction+noise (Composio), candy-colored halftone (Snowglobe), sci-fi globe carousel (Meridian) — thesis: 'one strong aesthetic direction beats flashing 3D everything.'
take_what: The curator's own thesis — pick ONE distinctive motif and commit — is directly reusable for narrowing Astryx's homepage redesign options.

name: The Monospace Web (Oskar Wickström)
one_line: A widely-cited experiment proving a whole page — text, diagrams, charts — can run on a strict monospace grid using near-vanilla semantic HTML.
design_notes: Single monospace typeface for everything, content aligns to a fixed character-width grid that steps responsively, box-drawing characters (│─┌┐) used for diagrams instead of SVG, deliberately rejects custom CSS ornamentation.
take_what: Character-grid alignment and box-drawing diagrams as a rigorous constraint model — a good stress test for a plain-HTML fallback mode.

name: Anti-AI Design — the backlash to the gradient-orb look
one_line: The counter-trend to OpenAI/Gemini's polished gradient-orb look: hand-drawn marks, grain, and deliberate imperfection read as 'human-made' now.
design_notes: Names the reaction against glossy, noise-free AI interfaces (the OpenAI/Gemini look): hand-drawn marks, ink bleed, grain, deliberate asymmetry — polish now reads as 'corporate filler.' Anti-laziness not anti-tech: AI generates roughs, a human hand-finishes the imperfection in.
take_what: A deliberate imperfection pass (grain, slight misalignment, hand-touched texture) to differentiate from the now-generic AI-gradient-orb hero.

design_notes: Names Typography Principles (gray circle cursor for contrast), Komnata Agency (draw-with-fluorescent-light cursor), CQQL Records (pixelated analogue cursor), Waaarhol (circle cursor inverts underlying color), Lux Expression (small yellow dot).
name: Awwwards — Customize your mouse cursor guide
one_line: Awwwards field guide catalogs 5+ live sites' custom cursors with an explicit 'use sparingly, disable on mobile' design rule.
take_what: Adopt its restraint rule: custom cursor effects belong on portfolio/editorial surfaces, not corporate/B2B flows like Astryx docs.

name: Apple.com — macOS 27 'Golden Gate'
one_line: Apple's macOS page treats Liquid Glass as a literal textured material in close-up product photography, not just a CSS effect.
design_notes: macOS 27 'Golden Gate' page: welcome/endframe hero carousel spanning the whole device lineup, warm gold accent on neutral white base, card layout with alternating text/image rhythm, close-up Mail-app screenshot showing glass buttons with visible surface 'texture.'
take_what: Macro close-up shots of UI chrome used as hero imagery — sells the material/texture directly instead of a flat screenshot.

name: Linear — Pricing
one_line: The most-cited 2026 pricing-page exemplar: four flat tiers, 5-7 bullets per tier, then a category-grouped full comparison table below.
design_notes: Clean horizontal tier-card row at top with per-seat pricing ($0/$10/$16/Custom); detailed comparison table grouped into labeled sections (Members, Issues, AI & agent workflows, Security) rather than one long undifferentiated list; single CTA per card.
take_what: Section-grouped comparison table (group rows under labeled categories) as a reusable Astryx table pattern — scans faster than one flat feature list.

name: Sazabi
one_line: YC W26 AI-native observability startup whose site opens inside a full-bleed 3D mech cockpit overlooking a neon cyberpunk skyline.
design_notes: Full-viewport WebGL scene: dark cockpit HUD frames a night skyline in blue/red neon, bold condensed all-caps display type 'OBSERVABILITY ON AUTOPILOT,' sound toggle top-left, numbered scroll sections (01 Alerts/02 Chat/03 Agents), red accent CTA.
take_what: A full-bleed animated 3D/WebGL scene with one bold condensed headline and an ambient sound toggle turns a routine dev-tool pitch into a game-like moment.

name: Rivet
one_line: YC-backed visual editor letting product designers ship precise UI changes straight into production code — 'own every detail in your live product.'
design_notes: Tagline 'The visual editor built for design'; per YC/X posts the product shows designers editing live components with pixel-level control that commits straight to code, positioning itself as the bridge between Figma-style editing and a real component tree.
take_what: The core narrative — precise visual control mapped 1:1 to real components, not a mockup — echoes how Astryx could demo its swizzle/eject workflow.

name: Acti (openacti.com)
one_line: Singapore agentic-keyboard startup, raised $5.3M, TechCrunch-covered, PH-badged; keyboard that takes actions from typed intent.
design_notes: Dark tech aesthetic, glowing neon key-glow effects (key-glow-tight/diffuse), animated halo rings behind phone mockup, pill-shaped gradient UI chips, creator avatar carousel, bold sans headline 'Think it. ACTI on.' over full-bleed sections.
take_what: Glow/halo motif around a hero product shot to make an abstract 'agent' concept feel tangible; pill-chip micro-components as recurring visual language.

name: Framer 3.0
one_line: Framer's major June 2026 release adding on-canvas AI Agents, Community, and a redesign; charted top-10 on PH multiple weeks.
design_notes: Modular card-based feature showcase, live 'Thinking...' agent-generation states shown inline as UI demo, community grid of user-made sites as social proof, earthy/organic color-palette direction, real-time stat counters (uptime, sites shipped).
take_what: Showing the AI agent literally 'thinking' inline in a hero demo (live-state UI) rather than a static screenshot.

name: Runway
one_line: Runway's dark, cinematic interface puts AI-generated video output front and center as the hero content, per design-survey coverage.
design_notes: Dark interface throughout, cinematic full-bleed video demonstrations as hero content, product output (not screenshots) is the visual centerpiece, targets creative/filmmaker audience.
take_what: Let the product's literal output (rendered media, not chrome/UI screenshots) BE the hero visual — output-as-hero over abstract illustration.

name: "Aesthetics in the AI Era: Visual + Web Design Trends for 2026" (Teleanu)
one_line: Names 11 emerging 2026 aesthetics (Technical Mono, Surveillance, Frutiger Aero, Y3K, Immersive 3D) as pushback against generative-AI visual sameness.
design_notes: Frames the moment as 'recombination': skeuomorphism over surveillance UI, brutalism softened with botanical gradients, vapor-gloss pixel collage. Three throughlines: embrace of imperfection, mixed-media maximalism, neo-nostalgia as critique of algorithmic sterility.
take_what: A vocabulary (Technical Mono, Surveillance Aesthetic, Frutiger Aero) for naming dark-AI clichés to deliberately avoid in Astryx's docs/marketing voice.

name: Neko Health
one_line: Daniel Ek's body-scanning health startup; Note Design Studio's pale-yellow/dark-green futurist palette for its scan rooms carries into the brand.
design_notes: Unconventional healthcare palette — high-gloss pale yellow paired with dark green, brushed metal, diffused reeded glass — built to feel futuristic yet human, not clinical-white; second-gen scan-room platform launched 2026.
take_what: Breaking category-color convention (healthcare = white/blue) with an unexpected warm/dark duo reads premium and future-facing, not sterile.

name: Base UI
one_line: Headless primitives from the combined Radix+MUI+Floating UI team, now shadcn's official second engine — site is deliberately undecorated.
design_notes: Text-first, no gradients or motion flourishes, matching its 'unstyled' positioning. Hero: 'Unstyled UI components for building accessible user interfaces.' Adopter-logo roster, team/contributor credits, FAQ addressing why headless/unstyled is the right call.
take_what: An adopter-logo wall plus an explicit FAQ pre-answering 'why this unconventional approach' — useful for justifying a foundational choice like StyleX.

name: Google Gemini app — 'Neural Expressive' redesign
one_line: Google's ground-up Gemini redesign: a named design language, 'Neural Expressive,' with glowing gradients, a pill-shaped prompt box, and structured responses.
design_notes: Blue-and-white ombre gradient homepage; top half glows through the Gemini icon colors while 'thinking'; pill-shaped input and Live waveform; responses lead with bolded key info plus inline images/timelines instead of text blocks; fullscreen nav drawer.
take_what: 'Glow reflects system state' pattern — ambient gradient pulse during processing, a strong micro-interaction for loading/skeleton states.

name: ClickHouse — Pricing
one_line: Leads with a 'pricing philosophy' essay (pay-for-what-you-use, transparency) before any tier/number, using icon-paired statements instead of a table.
design_notes: Dark, icon-led sections (currency icon for 'pay only for what you use', control icon for 'transparency') ahead of the Development/Production/Dedicated tier breakdown; hybrid subscription+usage+capacity model shown as prose, not a grid.
take_what: Lead with a short values/philosophy statement above the price grid to justify a usage-based model before showing numbers — reduces sticker-shock framing.

name: 925studios — AI Slop Web Design Guide
one_line: 2026 guide naming the 'AI slop' aesthetic (Inter font, purple-blue gradients, generic rounded cards) and prescribing five fixes to look distinctive.
design_notes: AI-slop signature named: default Inter type, purple-to-blue gradient, rounded-corner cards, stock imagery, generic AI-toned copy. Cites 38% of visitors bouncing from poor design. Fixes: distinctive type, real photography, voice-matched copy, intentional micro-interactions.
take_what: Explicit checklist to avoid: default Inter font, purple-blue gradient, generic rounded cards, vague copy — replace with custom type, real screenshots

name: Vestwell
one_line: Digital savings/retirement platform raised a $385M Series D (2026), one of the year's largest fintech rounds.
design_notes: Soft pastel palette (pink, blue, sage, orange) on cream neutrals; bold headline with italic emphasis; custom 3D illustrated mascots (bear, chess-piece horse, coin, lighthouse); three-persona hero split (Employers/Advisors/Individuals); video-thumbnail hero.
take_what: Pastel-on-neutral palette plus custom illustrated mascots humanizes an institutional fintech category without sacrificing credibility.

name: Featherless.ai
one_line: Featherless.ai built its whole visual system around an origami-style geometric 'F' isotype in a signature yellow, with a real-time-typed logo animation.
design_notes: Origami/geometric-fold visual language; 'Solar Feather' yellow as sole signature accent against neutral base; Geist Mono for developer-audience credibility; logotype 'typed' in real time above the fold; auto light/dark adaptation.
take_what: One geometric mark + one accent color as the whole brand system, plus monospace type signaling developer audience — cheap, high-leverage for a docs mark.

name: prg.sh — Why Your AI Keeps Building the Same Purple Gradient Website
one_line: Traces the ubiquitous purple-gradient/Inter/card-grid 'AI website' look to Tailwind's old bg-indigo-500 default propagating through LLM training data.
design_notes: Names purple/indigo gradient-on-white, Inter/Roboto type, predictable 3-card grids as the LLM 'statistical average.' Prescribes distinctive type (Playfair Display, Space Grotesk, Fraunces), layered atmospheric gradients, and orchestrated (not scattered) animation as the fix.
take_what: Gives an explicit anti-pattern checklist (no purple/Inter/white-card-grid) usable as QA before shipping any Astryx-generated marketing page.

name: Jeton
one_line: eWallet fintech site that won Awwwards SOTD, Developer Award, FWA and CSSDA SOTD for its scroll-based finance UX.
design_notes: Black-and-white base, single signature orange accent drives all CTAs; custom wordmark typeface built around the 'O' counter, extended into a 3D animated brand universe; scroll-triggered motion; layout morphs desktop-to-mobile; repetition used as a brand device.
take_what: One disciplined accent color on near-mono base + a repeated custom-lettered wordmark motif reads more premium than multi-gradient hero art.

name: "Why Every AI-Built Website Looks the Same" (dev.to)
one_line: Traces the 'every AI-built site looks the same' purple-gradient cliché to Tailwind UI's default bg-indigo-500 and a training-data feedback loop.
design_notes: Names the formula explicitly: indigo-500→purple-600 gradient text, Inter/system-ui only, 0.5rem rounded corners, low-opacity shadows, 3-column icon feature grid, white/light-gray base.
take_what: A literal checklist of what to deliberately avoid if Astryx's site wants to read as designed-by-humans rather than templated-by-AI.

name: PostHog
one_line: Product analytics unicorn trading the purple-gradient SaaS look for a cream background and hand-drawn hedgehog mascots, called "insane" on LinkedIn in 2026.
design_notes: Warm cream/light background (not white), no gradients on the marketing surface, hand-drawn hedgehog illustrations scattered like sketchbook marginalia, flat CTA buttons. Note: PostHog's logo itself picked up a gradient in a 2026 refresh — a small crack in the flat system.
take_what: A warm off-white/cream base plus a consistent hand-drawn mascot motif — color without gradient, an alternative to stark black/white brutalism.

name: ChatGPT Atlas
one_line: OpenAI's browser, natively rendered (SwiftUI/AppKit/Metal, not a Chromium reskin) to give Agent Mode its own rich motion layer.
design_notes: Clean minimal chrome (search bar, tabs, bookmarks kept plain); built with native UI specifically so Agent Mode carries richer animation than a bolted-on extension could; omnipresent 'Ask ChatGPT' action; 2026 update added tab groups + an 'Auto' mode.
take_what: Reserve real motion budget for the single 'thinking/acting' moment; keep surrounding baseline chrome deliberately plain rather than spreading novelty evenly.

name: Fireart Studio — Brutalist UX & Invisible Logic
one_line: 2026 trend piece: raw/tactile brutalism as proof of human authorship vs. AI-homogenized design, plus 'Machine Experience'.
design_notes: Pairs deep-black-plus-neon chromatic extremes with lightweight CSS noise/gradient texture instead of heavy 3D; variable fonts tie weight/width to scroll position ('typography as architecture'); true-black #000000 OLED dark-first framed as battery-saving, not just aesthetic.
take_what: 'Machine Experience' — structuring semantic HTML so AI agents can parse and recommend the product — is a new docs-presentation checklist item.

name: Superset
one_line: YC-backed (Spring 2026) terminal-first IDE for 10-100+ parallel coding agents; 11.5k GitHub stars, named a standout of June 2026 demo day.
design_notes: Dark-theme, monospace-forward UI mirroring its own product; hero 'The Code Editor for AI Agents' with dual macOS-download CTA; live product chrome as marketing art — animated terminal spinners, color-coded git-diff view, worktree metaphors, agent-icon row.
take_what: Literal, live-feeling product screenshots (git diffs, terminal state) as hero art instead of illustration.

name: Daydream
one_line: Chat-based AI shopping agent for fashion built around iOS 26's Liquid Glass visual language; $50M Forerunner-led seed, Time Best Inventions 2025.
design_notes: Embraces Apple's Liquid Glass system — translucency, softened dimensionality, layered surfaces — applied to chat input, nav, and full-bleed product displays; screenshot-to-search lets users shop from a photo. Press calls it 'minimal but rich, clean but expressive.'
take_what: Translucent, layered glass-surface treatment for cards/nav to add depth without visual heaviness

name: Mirendil
one_line: Frontier AI lab, $200M a16z/Kleiner seed, runs an ultra-minimalist text-first site.
design_notes: Minimalist, text-heavy layout; numbered nav sections (1.0-4.0); neutral monochrome palette with light/dark toggle; no hero imagery, just declarative typographic statements; transparency-driven structure (mission, team, funding, contact).
take_what: Numbered-section nav and headline-only hero that trusts typography alone to carry credibility, no decorative imagery needed.

name: 21st.dev
one_line: YC W26 team building UI building blocks for the agentic internet — a React component registry used by 2M devs, the closest direct comp to Astryx's own site.
design_notes: Light background, high-contrast black-on-white type, italicized 'beautiful' emphasis in headline 'Build something beautiful,' equal-weight top nav (Components/Templates/MCP/Themes), filterable search as the primary hero CTA.
take_what: Frame the whole marketing site as a searchable, filterable catalog rather than a persuasion funnel — search-as-hero fits a component-library product directly.

name: SaaSFrame — 10 SaaS Landing Page Trends for 2026
one_line: Trend roundup naming Notion, Linear, Framer, Figma, Amplitude and Zendesk as SaaS landing-page exemplars for 2026.
design_notes: Story-driven heroes (Notion, Linear, Framer); personalized CTAs (Figma); purposeful micro-animation (Peec AI); interactive product previews (Amplitude, Zendesk); real UI screenshots over abstract art (Coherence); split-screen comparisons (Decipad); modular design systems.
take_what: The 'real UI screenshots over abstract art' trend argues for Astryx docs showing live component demos, not decorative illustration.

name: vibecon.ai (Replit)
one_line: Replit-backed 'code meets culture' AI conference site frames itself as an art/culture event, not a dev conference.
design_notes: Tagged Event / AI / Art / Technology on Landing.love; structured around named zones — Main Stage, Forum, Lab, Installations — mixing talks with AI-art exhibits.
take_what: Zone-based information architecture (stage / lab / installations) to present a multi-track program visually instead of a flat agenda list.

name: Siteinspire — Big Type category
one_line: Shared Siteinspire tag across 2026 startup/finance adds (Daylight, Semaloop, Mammoth Brands, AI Report): one move — huge display type as the hero.
design_notes: Not one site but a pattern: hero built from a single oversized headline (often 8-15vw type), minimal chrome, restrained 1-2 color palettes, whitespace instead of imagery to establish a premium/confident tone.
take_what: Market has moved past bento-grid/glassmorphism toward type-as-hero; Astryx's site should lead with an oversized headline, not a feature grid.

name: "Best AI Startup Website Design Examples (2026)" (Veza Digital)
one_line: Surveys 9 AI leaders and names 2026's shared grammar: dark-mode default, single electric accent, WebGL shaders, bento grids, kinetic variable-font headlines.
design_notes: Covers Anthropic, Jasper, Runway, Perplexity, Midjourney, Hugging Face, Harvey, Cohere, Stability AI. Notes the 'marketing site collapsed into the product surface' (Perplexity's search box IS the homepage) and that top sites prioritize product proof over visual spectacle.
take_what: The 'product-as-homepage' collapse and single-accent-on-dark discipline are the most portable, non-gimmicky takeaways for a component-system site.

name: Stan Vision — "SaaS website design in 2026"
one_line: Design studio's journal breakdown of what's converting on 2026 SaaS homepages, company by company.
design_notes: Named: Superhuman (single value-prop hero), Clay (tactile 3D shapes, avoids 'AI-robot' look), Ramp (real UI, no floating dashboards), Databricks (orange on dark bg), Brex (people on orange backdrops). Pattern: UI before copy, dark bg + one accent, micro-animation.
take_what: 'Product UI before copy, micro-animation over cinematic' is a testable heuristic for sequencing Astryx's own component demos.

name: WorkOS
one_line: Enterprise-auth site leaning on a feature checklist and code-tab showcase instead of illustration; a black-and-white minimal-site standard.
design_notes: Bold headline + concise value prop, dark-text-on-light restraint, minimal decorative patterns. Uses functional artifacts (language-toggle code samples, ready/enabled checklist) instead of illustration or photography for visual interest.
take_what: Replace decorative hero art with functional artifacts (code samples, status checklists) that double as proof-of-product and visual texture.

name: Gucci: Mystery Unfolds
one_line: MONOGRID-built Gucci storytelling microsite, Awwwards SOTD June 17 2026, app-style narrative interaction.
design_notes: Minimal 2-color palette (#FEF1E1 cream, #CAB588 gold-tan). App-style UI with gesture-driven storytelling, GSAP animation, GraphQL-backed content. Scored 7.69/10 creativity over 7/10 usability — narrative-first, not conversion-first.
take_what: A 2-color palette carries luxury weight better than a busy gradient system; scroll-as-narrative-device over static hero copy.

name: Material Design 3 — Design tokens overview
one_line: Material Design 3's token page codifies a three-tier ref/sys/comp naming hierarchy so design and code share one token vocabulary.
design_notes: Token names = system + class + role (e.g. md-sys-color-primary); reference=raw values, system=semantic roles, component=per-element; site pushes "M3 Expressive" and "hero moments" — spend expressive motion on 1-2 interactions only; dynamic color extracts theme from wallpaper.
take_what: Three-tier token naming (reference -> system -> component) as explicit tokens-page IA; "hero moments" restraint principle for where to spend expressive motion.

name: Mantine
one_line: React library (120+ components, 70 hooks) whose homepage doubles as a live interactive demo gallery.
design_notes: Clean sans-serif, seamless light/dark toggle, Ctrl+K search. Hero: '120+ components, 70 hooks.' Live embedded demos that actually work, code blocks with 'Expand code' toggles, sponsor logos. 2026 banner markets docs as LLM-optimized, built for Claude Code/Cursor.
take_what: Live actually-interactive demo blocks (not screenshots) plus expandable code toggles and explicit 'agent-readable docs' hero positioning.

name: Chakra UI v3
one_line: Component-system homepage pairs a vivid green/red accent duo with a Tokens/Typography/Recipes breakdown of the system layer.
design_notes: Bold headlines on neutral bg, bright green/red accents. Hero: npm snippet, CTA, 'component system for building products with speed.' Below fold: live previews (Slider, Pin Input, Tabs, Menu, Switch). Three-column Tokens/Typography/Recipes section. Downloads stat, Pro upsell.
take_what: A live component-preview strip right below the fold, and an explicit Tokens/Typography/Recipes three-column structure.

name: Figma
one_line: Figma's 2026 launch video pulled 35.9M X views — #2 in Launch Library; Figma has three videos in the top 20, most launch-video volume of any tracked company.
