design_notes: Light-mode, white background, purple/lavender accents in live UI demos. Headline 'The intelligent canvas for infinite creativity.' Large real product screenshots as hero imagery, feature-card grids, testimonial + Fortune-500 logo carousel below fold.
take_what: Real product-screenshot-as-hero-image on a white base with a single restrained accent color, rather than illustration.

name: SaaSFrame — Pricing Page category
one_line: 211-example library of real SaaS pricing pages with light/dark variants and downloadable Figma files for premium subscribers.
design_notes: Card-thumbnail grid showing desktop + mobile crops per company (Linear, Figma, Asana, Intercom, Buffer, Raycast, GitBook); filters by category, brand, and light/dark theme.
take_what: Bulk reference for how PLG tools pair pricing cards with light/dark theme parity — useful for auditing Astryx's own pricing-template theme tokens.

name: Humans& (humansand.ai)
one_line: Human-centric AI research lab that raised the 2nd-largest seed round in VC history ($480M) days into 2026.
design_notes: Copy-forward, minimalist positioning site; hero line: 'AI should serve as a deeper connective tissue.' Direct fetch blocked (403); no verified color/type specifics — treat as messaging-led, not visually maximalist, per public coverage.
take_what: How a huge-buzz raise still ships spare, text-led copy — proof that manifesto voice can out-signal visual maximalism in AI-lab positioning.

name: Landdding: State of Landing Pages 2026
one_line: Data-driven survey of 2026 startup landing pages: custom type, dark near-black palettes, 'surgical' gradients, and live product demos replacing screenshots.
design_notes: Custom type (PP Neue Montreal, Aeonik, GT Super) beat generic sans; dark near-black dominates AI/dev tools; gradients reduced to a single hero-blob/CTA accent; glassmorphism and stock illustration abandoned; motion shifted to restrained selective reveals (GSAP/Framer Motion).
take_what: The 'surgical gradient' rule (one hero blob/CTA, not a full-bleed wash) and 'live demo beats screenshot' apply directly to how to show component previews.

name: 1X NEO home robot
one_line: 1X's $20K humanoid NEO launched with a warm, textile-soft aesthetic and a launch video that hit 68.7M views on X.
design_notes: Neutral warm palette (tan/gray/dark-brown) instead of tech-brand colors; bold single-column headlines; full-width lifestyle photography of the robot folding laundry/navigating rooms; generous whitespace; deliberately residential, not tech-forward.
take_what: Staging the product in real domestic settings with a warm neutral palette instead of studio-tech renders signals trust and safety.

name: basement.studio (Daylight Computer showcase)
one_line: The studio behind Vercel, Linear, Cursor, Daylight Computer, Harvey and Krea's most-praised web work; the tastemaker for 'internet-native' sites.
design_notes: Portfolio spans dark developer-tool aesthetics (Vercel, Linear, Cursor) to quiet minimal hardware sites (Daylight); coverage calls the house style 'clear, bold, polished, slightly playful.'
take_what: One studio's client roster is a live trend map; scan new case studies periodically to see what 'good' means to startup Twitter next.

name: EverSwap
one_line: DeFi protocol EverSwap (Awwwards Site of the Day, Jun 22 2026, studio Lusion) leads with illustrated WebGL storytelling over a stark 2-tone palette.
design_notes: Near-white (#FBFFF4) + deep forest green (#203727) two-color scheme; WebGL/3D animated intro built in Blender runs before any product info; illustration-driven narrative over text-heavy sections; jury scored animation/transitions 8.0/10.
take_what: An illustrated brand-world intro sequence before the pitch makes a technical/finance product feel crafted rather than templated.

name: Daylight (godaylight.com)
one_line: Energy-tech startup site by studio Numbered; oversized type, generous whitespace, added to Siteinspire May 2026.
design_notes: Big-type minimal hero: bold display headline dominates, expansive negative space, restrained near-monochrome palette, subtle animated transitions across desktop/mobile builds; full branding+motion package by Numbered.
take_what: Oversized single-statement hero type paired with heavy whitespace reads confident/enterprise without needing color or imagery to do the work.

name: Miro
one_line: Trueform's Framer rebuild of miro.com won Best Big Site (2025 Framer Awards) — proof Framer now handles large, many-page marketing sites.
design_notes: Judges described a 'light' experience across multiple pages with 'clear and playful' navigation. Notable because Miro is a large, high-traffic company, showing Framer scaling past single-studio-portfolio use.
take_what: A design-system-scale, many-page site can keep nav light/playful instead of defaulting to dense enterprise chrome.

name: GitHub — Mona Sans & Hubot Sans launch
one_line: GitHub's open-source variable font is now cited as the 'bouba grotesk' archetype — soft, rounded, friendly, replacing colder tech sans-serifs in 2026 branding.
design_notes: Three-axis variable font (weight, width, slant) built to stay expressive across product, web, and print from one file — cited with Stripe/Notion as the dominant 2026 warmth-in-tech-type movement.
take_what: One variable font serving product UI, marketing, and print via weight/width/slant axes, shrinking the type-system surface area to maintain.

name: Trillion (Hello Trillion) — "cosmic orb UI"
one_line: Indie-built 'voice-first AI co-founder' demo makes the cosmic-orb aesthetic literal: a breathing, voice-reactive wireframe orb in a nebula.
design_notes: Full-screen procedural deep-space nebula backdrop, central wireframe orb that breathes/deforms with voice input and shifts color by conversational state, sub-agent avatars orbiting as a 'constellation,' trail beams/pulse rings on dispatch.
take_what: The purest distillation of the 'canonical AI orb' — an extreme reference point to design against, or knowingly quote, not copy wholesale.

name: Legora
one_line: Swedish legal-AI startup, tripled to $5.6B valuation in 2026 (Accel, Atlassian, Nvidia), runs a dense modular enterprise site.
design_notes: Modular sections: expandable 'aOS' capability categories, practice-area cards (M&A, Litigation, Banking), ROI metric tiles, founder-quote block, security-badge row (SOC2/ISO/GDPR/HIPAA); arrow (↳) affordances driving deeper exploration.
take_what: Trust-signal density (compliance badges + metrics + founder voice) packed into a still-scannable grid for enterprise B2B.

name: Jeton (by Bürocratik)
one_line: Fintech app site that won Awwwards Site of the Day plus the Mobile Excellence Award for a 'morphing' desktop-to-mobile scroll experience.
design_notes: Burnt-orange palette with soft pastels, black nearly eliminated from CSS; coin-shaped wordmark always in motion; Rive scroll-indexed animation morphs the hero between desktop/mobile/physical-card; GSAP + Matter.js + Lenis; 'storyscrolling' avoids autoplay.
take_what: A single scroll-driven hero object that morphs desktop to mobile to physical form shows 'works on your phone' without three separate mockup sections.

name: Remotion
one_line: Open-source React video library whose launch clip drew 14.8M X views — outranking xAI's and Cluely's videos despite being a dev tool, not a consumer app.
design_notes: CLI-command hero ($ npx create-video@latest) under tagline 'Create real MP4 videos with React.' Interactive drag-drop demo re-renders video live. Light mode with dark-mode toggle that live-updates preview. GitHub-star/npm-install counts replace enterprise logos.
take_what: CLI-command-as-hero-CTA for devs, and star/install counters as social proof — directly analogous to a component-library site.

name: Opera Neon
one_line: Opera's $19.90/mo 'concept browser' — dark neon UI with a desktop-metaphor start page and three explicit AI modes (Chat/Do/Make).
design_notes: Dark charcoal/black bg, bright cyan neon accents; bold sans headline 'built to act' repeated for reinforcement; start page renders open tabs as circular icons over the user's own wallpaper; three-column cards explain Chat/Do/Make. 2026 reviews: striking but confusing.
take_what: Neon-on-black palette and circular-icon 'desktop as browser home' hero motif; three-mode modular cards as a template for explaining a multi-capability product.

name: Polymarket invite-code waitlist bypass
one_line: Prediction-market breakout Polymarket gated its 2026 app behind a waitlist with an 'I have an invite code' link that routes straight around the queue.
design_notes: Reported UI: default path leads to a static 'Thank you, we'll email you' screen; a secondary 'Enter Invite Code' link bypasses it entirely — code functions as VIP credential, not a rank number.
take_what: Dual-path signup: a form for the masses plus a quiet 'have a code?' link that feels like insider reward.

name: Pricing Pages (pricingpages.design)
one_line: Curated gallery of best-in-class SaaS pricing pages tagged by structure (tier cards, comparison tables, usage calculators, contact-sales).
design_notes: Card grid of company favicons + full-page screenshots; filterable by component (tier cards, comparison tables, FAQs, monthly/annual switches, usage calculators) and content density (long vs short). Features ChatGPT, Figma, Calendly, n8n, Ramp, Vanta, Mux.
take_what: Component taxonomy for pricing UI: tier-card, comparison-table, calculator, contact-sales-card as first-class Astryx primitives.

name: Context.dev
one_line: YC S26 web-context API's hero lets visitors paste any URL into a tabbed live-extraction widget before they sign up.
design_notes: Deep-charcoal dark mode, cyan/electric-blue accents, glassmorphic translucent overlay panels, gradient text on headline with a literal '{API}' curly-brace glyph as brand mark, customer-logo carousel under hero, modular feature cards, accordion FAQ.
take_what: A try-before-signup widget embedded in the hero converts skeptics fast; dashed vertical rails cheaply frame a component gallery page.

name: Espa (Espa Labs)
one_line: Neo-backed AI executive assistant (founder ex-Forethought), publicly launched May 2026, backed by Village Global/SV Angel/Neo.
design_notes: Framer-built. Warm palette from CSS: near-black, brown text #2d251e, teal #5bb9b9, coral #f96e6b, tan #eed1b3, cream #fcfaf9 — human/warm not AI-blue. H1 'What Espa does for you' centered. Cards scroll-reveal via Framer transform (opacity+translateY150→0+scale0.9→1).
take_what: Multi-hue warm palette (teal+coral+tan+brown) as alternative to default AI blue/purple; soft scroll-reveal card entrance for feature grids.

name: FablePool
one_line: Pools small credits from many builders so an AI agent can build ambitious open software in public, with live spend/logs shown.
design_notes: Light, clean, corporate-approachable palette; hero uses a literal 'pool fill' progress metaphor; numeric stats (480 builders, 7 shipped builds) and structured project cards create a transparent, data-driven feel rather than flashy motion.
take_what: The 'fill/progress as hero visual' metaphor and stat-driven trust-building (real counters, not vague claims) — good for a docs/adoption-metrics section.

name: Imprint — Hebbia Design Studio
one_line: Landing page for AI enterprise-search unicorn Hebbia's design studio; nominee for custom-type shader-driven 3D.
design_notes: Custom typeface from Schick Toikka, Three.js + custom shaders, WebGL rendering, interactive filters/effects. Community scores 6.0-9.9 with multiple perfect 10s.
take_what: Bespoke type + shader 3D on an AI-startup microsite shows typography-as-brand-differentiator is now expected — a cue for Astryx's type system.

name: Framer Site of the Month — June 2026
one_line: Monthly Framer Awards post: June 2026 winner plus three runners-up, each with a short craft critique.
design_notes: Winner Disco Dungeon: scroll-driven dungeon crawl as hero. Runners-up: Melnūdens ('stunning scroll, top typography'), Artboard ('bright palette, energetic illustrations'), Carbonable ('dark scheme, fantastic scroll'). Scroll-as-narrative is the throughline.
take_what: Scroll-scrubbed narrative sequences (not static feature grids) as the current top-tier Framer pattern.

name: Peec AI
one_line: Berlin AI-search-visibility analytics startup, $21M Series A, $10M ARR in 16 months, negotiating a raise near $200M valuation.
design_notes: Named by SaaSFrame for 'micro animations with purpose' — minimal hover reveals, scroll fades, animated form feedback demonstrating function not decoration; screenshots favor a narrow guided-workflow view over a dense feature-everything dashboard.
take_what: Restraint as differentiation — a narrow guided-workflow hero screenshot reads more confident than showing every feature.

name: Michal Malewicz — 'Vibe Coding is OVER'
one_line: Prominent product-design voice argues AI-assisted 'vibe coding' has commoditized startup sites into interchangeable, personality-free landing pages.
design_notes: Compares the sameness to an IKEA LACK coffee table — 'functional but soulless': flat feature-block layouts, vague copy ('seamless streamlined effortless automation'), no distinguishing color/type. Argues intentional differentiation is now the actual differentiator.
take_what: Warns against template-flat feature grids and vague AI-toned copy — visible craft/differentiation is now the credibility signal.

name: Paste — Framer Stories case study
one_line: Presentation-tool startup Paste tore out a custom Next.js+GSAP+Sanity stack and rebuilt entirely in Framer for design-team velocity.
design_notes: Case study: homepage rebuilt with interactive animations reflecting brand concepts, blog + help center moved to Framer CMS, custom React-powered components — the reverse of the usual "outgrow the builder" narrative.
take_what: Evidence some funded startups move a marketing site OFF custom code ONTO a visual builder for velocity — cite when scoping non-engineer control.

name: Composio
one_line: Agent-integration infra startup mixes a dark gradient-refraction hero with ASCII-art section headers for a terminal-native feel.
design_notes: Dark bg, gradient-refraction hero with subtle noise grain, monospace/ASCII-art section headers ('CLAUDE CODE' style), holographic PNG accents, smooth fade-out on scroll, numbered 01-04 sections.
take_what: ASCII/monospace section markers + numbered-section pattern signal 'built by engineers, for engineers' cheaply — good fit for docs-heavy pages.

name: Sahara AI
one_line: "AI workforce" platform pairs a technical grid backdrop with a subtle interactive 3D hero element.
design_notes: Dark theme, structural grid-line background, subtle interactive 3D object in hero users can manipulate, hover states that rotate/slide elements, numbered 01-06 modular sections.
take_what: Grid-line backdrop is a cheap CSS way to add 'technical' texture behind a hero without full particle/WebGL cost — worth a quick prototype.

name: Apple Developer — Design Resources (Icon Composer)
one_line: Apple ships a literal builder tool (Icon Composer) for Liquid Glass icons — the material as a design-tool primitive, not a CSS trick.
design_notes: Design Resources hub: modular grid by platform tab (iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS). Icon Composer section shows before/after parallax screenshots and 'create layered icons out of Liquid Glass from a single design' copy; file-format badges, generous whitespace.
take_what: Precedent for a design system shipping its own asset-authoring tool for a signature visual effect, not just docs describing it.

name: Agentic Browsers Are Here: What Web Development Teams Need to Know
one_line: Prescriptive piece: marketing sites must adopt semantic HTML, structured data, and keyboard operability so AI browser agents can act on them.
design_notes: No visual commentary — build-requirements piece: replace generic divs with semantic tags (nav/main/form/button), add JSON-LD + OpenGraph, visible labels on every input, ARIA where semantics fall short, full keyboard operability, optionally a lightweight agent-facing API.
take_what: Non-visual checklist (semantic markup, ARIA, structured data, keyboard-first) for making a site legible to Comet/Atlas-style agents — a new requirement.

name: Chargebee — Anchors Away (Subscription Toggle Anchor Trap)
one_line: Counter-trend piece: the standard 'default-to-annual' toggle backfires — the low anchor makes the true monthly price feel like a 300% penalty.
design_notes: No visuals; argues for defaulting the toggle to monthly and minimizing the monthly/annual price gap instead, citing practitioner reports that leading with monthly price tested better and that no-card trials lifted annual conversion 2-4x.
take_what: Before defaulting an Astryx pricing-toggle to annual, note the documented anchor-trap risk — default state should be deliberate, not copied convention.

name: Nyne.ai
one_line: SPC/Wischoff-backed, $5.3M seed, TechCrunch-covered Mar 2026, resolves 250M+ web sources into verified person profiles for AI agents.
design_notes: Svelte-built. Dark forest-green (#1a3a2a-#315e3c) with neon-mint accent (#4ade80,#9ff0bb) on cream — unusual vs navy/purple data-infra norm. H1 stacks: 'The people / data API / for AI agents.' with 'data API' italic. Pulsing 'live-dot' badge beside real-time sourcing copy.
take_what: Dark-green + neon-mint accent pairing; italic-emphasis word inside stacked headline; small pulsing live-status dot for real-time copy.

name: Uncovr
one_line: EF/Index Ventures-backed surgical-AI startup, $7M seed, emerged from stealth June 2026, turns OR video into clinical reports.
design_notes: Framer-built. Dark navy/near-black (#1a1a1a,#1d2732) with electric-cyan accent #00d9ff and ice-blue tints. Hero headline animates character-by-character: each letter starts blurred+offset (blur, translate, scale, rotate, skew) and resolves sharp — staggered kinetic-type reveal.
take_what: Per-character blur/skew/rotate text-reveal for a premium hero-load moment; near-black + single electric-cyan accent for a precision feel.

name: 10 Web Design Trends Dominating Award Galleries in 2026
one_line: Trend-gallery synthesis of 2026 award-winning sites: 3D worlds, cinematic dark mode, kinetic typography, refined glassmorphism.
design_notes: Names ten trends: floating/3D hero imagery, layered motion, animation-as-brand-personality, huge scroll-reactive typography, mature restrained glassmorphism, luminous-accent dark mode, pinned 'movie-like' scroll storytelling, organic asymmetry replacing sterile grids.
take_what: Oversized kinetic typography as the primary hero element, plus restrained glassmorphic card panels over a cinematic dark base.

name: The Vibe Coding Crisis (Web Designer Depot)
one_line: Argues AI builders train on their own AI-generated output, tightening the aesthetic mean into named clichés — names the human-mess rebellion as the exit.
design_notes: Names vibe-coded clichés: 'SaaS Blue' (trust), 'Brutalist Red' (edge), safe emerald+glassmorphism fintech default, Swiss-grid 'Modern Minimalist'. Counter-move: intentional messiness, hand-drawn marks, layouts that 'scream a human was here'.
take_what: The named-cliché list is a direct audit checklist — if a demo screen matches one exactly, that's the tell to break from it.

name: Dark Design (curated gallery)
one_line: Hand-picked dark-themed site gallery whose AI/tech section anchors the current canon: xAI, Cursor, Modal, Langbase, Gemini, Grok.
design_notes: Featured sites share near-black/charcoal backgrounds, minimal accent colors (white/gray/subtle brand hue), clean sans typography, generous whitespace, simplified nav, full-width product imagery — 'modern restraint over decorative elements.'
take_what: A living reference set of what counts as 'dark AI-startup canon' right now — useful to benchmark Astryx's own dark theme against, avoid sameness.

name: Design Trends | July 2026, Startup Edition (mean.ceo)
one_line: Monthly startup trend roundup arguing design is becoming 'a promptable operating system' — code-first mockups replacing Figma-first workflows.
design_notes: Documents design.md files (markdown brand tokens, component rules, a11y checks) for keeping AI-generated pages on-brand; warns against 'generic gradients' and 'purple gradient startup pages' as the AI-slop tell; describes section-by-section generation with Claude/Codex.
take_what: A design.md-style brand contract (tokens, spacing, a11y minimums) is what a StyleX system could ship alongside AGENTS.md to prevent gradient drift.

design_notes: Duotone palette #FE494A red / #0800FF electric blue, GSAP-driven pixel-trail mouse follower, built on Webflow. Motion-forward production-studio portfolio — cursor trail as brand signature over a saturated two-color ground.
name: Pixel Melbourne — 'Pixel trail' mouse follower
one_line: Awwwards Honorable Mention (Apr 2026): pixel-trail custom mouse follower on a bold red/electric-blue creative-studio site.
take_what: Bold two-color palette plus one signature cursor flourish reads premium without heavy WebGL — worth sketching for a campaign page.

name: Radix UI Primitives docs
one_line: Radix Primitives docs anchor every component page in WAI-ARIA pattern compliance, making the accessibility contract core content, not a footnote.
design_notes: Standard left-nav/content/TOC 3-column doc shell; per-component pages cite the specific WAI-ARIA design pattern followed and internally enumerate keyboard interactions and ARIA attributes handled by the primitive.
take_what: Cite the accessibility spec/pattern a component follows directly on its doc page, and list keyboard interactions as a first-class documented table.

name: Figma — Top Web Design Trends 2026
one_line: Figma's 2026 trend resource: oversized/custom/kinetic typography, variable fonts, and bento-grid layouts as the dominant startup homepage vocabulary.
design_notes: Names oversized headlines, custom letterforms, kinetic scroll-triggered text, and layered type as 2026's primary branding tool, plus variable fonts; flags bento grids as the default dense-info layout, now with exaggerated corner rounding and per-tile micro-interactions.
take_what: Variable-font-driven oversized/kinetic headline type as brand signal; bento tiles with per-tile micro-interaction for dense doc/component listings

name: Crusoe
one_line: Vertically-integrated AI-infra/energy company raised $1.375B Series E above $10B valuation, still driving buzz into 2026.
design_notes: Dark navy/black base, white text, yellow/gold accents for an enterprise-industrial feel; hero 'Build AI faster with Crusoe Cloud'; isometric data-center/energy-to-compute illustrations; customer-logo and testimonial carousels; chronological news timeline.
take_what: Dark-mode default plus one warm accent color reads premium/technical; isometric illustration to make infra concepts legible.

name: 2026 Landing Pages: 110 Examples — Lapa Ninja
one_line: Curated gallery of 110 landing pages from 2026 launches, used industry-wide as a reference set for current startup marketing design.
design_notes: Curators flag serif type ('those little feet') returning to hero headlines for elegance, displacing grotesk-only default; parallel rise of strict black-and-white minimalist landing pages pitched as 'chic sophistication meets conversion power.'
take_what: A volume sample to spot-check trend-article claims against 110 real current examples rather than trusting summaries at face value.

name: machine0
one_line: YC S26 CLI-VM startup's homepage is a near-black terminal window hero with a lime-green CTA and a live-typed command.
design_notes: Near-black bg, oversized white grotesk H1, monospace subhead, centered 3-dot terminal card with blinking cursor, lime-green pill 'DASHBOARD' CTA — single-neon-accent dev-tool contrast.
take_what: Terminal-chrome hero as a 'live code' device fits Astryx's CLI/docs story; one neon accent on near-black reads 'built for engineers' fast.

name: Framer 3.0 — Agents, Branching, Community
one_line: June 16, 2026 Framer release: AI Agents design pages on canvas, Branching adds git-like review, plus a new Community — #1 on Product Hunt that day.
design_notes: Not one site's visual design but the infrastructure shift explaining why 2026 startup sites reach award-level polish fast: AI-agent-assisted design plus safe branching lowers the cost of the high-craft scroll/motion work seen across the winners above.
take_what: The 'agent designs, human reviews via branch' workflow is a process trend worth watching for how a site gets iterated.

name: Deepgram
one_line: Funded AI speech-recognition API company; site repeatedly cited across 2026 startup-site roundups as the dark-theme dev-tool reference.
design_notes: Dark theme with blue/white accents, prominent "Try for Free" CTA, interactive in-page playground for testing the speech API live rather than just describing it.
take_what: A live, actually-runnable API/component playground (not a screenshot) is the strongest dev-tool converter pattern — portable to a "try it live" section.

name: "AI Company Websites: 25+ Examples" (SiteBuilderReport)
one_line: 25+ AI-company gallery: dark-neon (Together AI), deep-purple gradient (Lambda/Synthesia), dark-glow dev tools (PlayerZero), bright outliers (Reclaim).
design_notes: Explicitly catalogs the purple-gradient default (Synthesia 'bold purple gradient,' Lambda 'deep-purple gradient and futuristic UI') alongside deliberate departures like Reclaim's 'bright, confident' cheerful palette.
take_what: Confirms deep-purple gradient is now the median AI look — evidence for picking a non-purple accent to avoid reading as generic-AI.

name: Snowglobe (Guardrails AI)
one_line: LLM-testing tool 'Snowglobe' breaks from dark-cosmic AI norms with a candy-colored palette and halftone illustration style.
design_notes: Candy-colored (bright, non-dark) palette, halftone-dot illustrations evoking data/simulation, technical grid backdrop for structure, scroll-hijacked tabbed sections forcing sequential story, before/after comparison as hero proof.
take_what: Playful halftone illustration + bright palette makes technical/infra products feel approachable rather than ominous — fits playful doc sections.

design_notes: Curated inspiration collection spanning trail effects with blend/invert modes, 3D typography cursor followers, animated-eyes followers, circle cursor-follow-on-move — breadth evidence cursor-as-canvas is now a recognized category.
name: Awwwards — Hovers, Cursors and Cute Interactions
one_line: 466-item curated Awwwards collection dedicated to cursor/hover micro-interactions — depth evidence of a recognized category.
take_what: Reference set for picking restrained, professional-safe cursor patterns before committing Astryx to any signature cursor flourish.

name: Utopia Fluid Type & Space Calculator
one_line: Interactive fluid type/space scale calculator with live CSS clamp() output and step visualizer, from Clearleft.
design_notes: Light neutral palette, dark on white; sticky top nav (Type/Space/Grid/Clamp/Blog/Showcase); min/max viewport + ratio inputs (1.067-2, named ratios); toggles Table/Graph/Visualiser output; monospace code block with copy-to-clipboard for generated clamp() CSS vars.
take_what: Live parameter-to-output preview (inputs re-render a visual scale + generated code) proves a token page can be a working tool, not a static table.

name: How Stripe Built Their New Website (YC Design Review recap)
one_line: Recap of a YC Design Review interview with Stripe's Head of Design Katie Dill on building the 2026 homepage redesign.
design_notes: Confirms bento-box storytelling, in-page modals instead of page navigation, extensive iteration on the wave animation to avoid distraction, and early experiments generating brand imagery with AI tools alongside traditional design process.
take_what: Modal deep-dives keep visitors on one page instead of fragmenting into subpages — Astryx component/template pages could borrow this for "see it live."

name: 925 Studios — 27 SaaS Pricing Pages That Actually Convert (2026)
one_line: Agency roundup citing a real before/after: 5→3 tiers plus a 'Most Popular' badge took one team's conversion from 1.2% to 3.1% (158% lift), no price change.
design_notes: Names dollar-based (vs percentage) annual-savings framing, 8-10 feature cap per tier, single CTA per plan, and social proof placed directly under the pricing cards (not a separate section) as the recurring winning patterns.
take_what: Tier-count reduction + 'Most Popular' badge + proximate social proof as a documented conversion lift — informs Astryx pricing template defaults.

name: Patronus AI
one_line: AI agent stress-testing via 'digital world models'; $50M Series B, announced June 25 2026 (TechCrunch).
design_notes: Dark bg, bold display headline 'Simulating the World's Intelligence'; asymmetric flowing layout with a bento-like grid of research-paper cards; layered translucent SVG overlays and gradient accent imagery for depth; animated chevron icons signaling scroll/expand.
take_what: Research-paper bento grid doubling as credibility proof — reusable for a case-study or changelog section.

name: WriterDock — 7 UI Trends Dominating 2026
one_line: Roundup naming 7 UI trends dominating 2026 web design, led by interactive 'Active Grid' bento layouts.
design_notes: Describes 'Active Grid' bento tiles that expand/play video/reveal data on hover, vs static 2024 bento; Vision-Pro-style glassmorphism/parallax depth; text-as-hero kinetic type; single-page scrollytelling; soft brutalism with sage/yellow pastels; dark-mode sustainability.
take_what: 'Active grid' — a bento tile that plays video or reveals data on hover rather than just tinting — upgrade for a feature-grid section.

name: Status AI
one_line: Gamified 'Sims but social' network where users role-play characters in shared fandom worlds; $17M raise, 2.5M users.
design_notes: Dark near-black background, high-contrast white sans-serif type, bold single-statement headline 'Be anyone in your own world', centered minimal layout, app-store badges + Discord/X icons in footer — no heavy motion, all focus on the one-line value prop.
take_what: Single oversized value-prop headline centered on a high-contrast dark canvas, stripped of secondary clutter

name: Best Tech Startup Websites of 2025: What's Next for 2026
one_line: Design-agency roundup naming specific 2025-2026 startup sites (Featherless, Vercel, Lovable, Jeton, Diamo, Formless) and the trends they represent.
design_notes: Featherless: origami F-shaped feather icon, 'Solar Feather' yellow, live-typing wordmark. Lovable: fluid blue-to-pink gradient hero. Jeton: pink-orange gradient + 3D coin illustration. Diamo: arch/door motif. Formless: generative 3D scroll/hover art but only 35 Pagespeed score.
take_what: The marketing site's visual system should be the same system the product uses, not a separate skin — branding flows into UI.

name: gitdot (args.io, YC S25)
one_line: YC-backed open-source 'better GitHub' (Rust) whose landing page rejects web-app norms for a keyboard-driven, CLI-style ~100ms-FCP aesthetic.
design_notes: Explicitly designed like a CLI, not a webapp — keyboard-driven instant navigation, minimal chrome, extreme speed (100ms FCP target) prioritized over conventional visual polish; design rationale documented openly in a public /designs folder.
take_what: A counter-example to decorative marketing sites — proof raw speed + keyboard-first interaction can itself be the 'design' for a technical audience.

name: Launch Library
one_line: A 160+ entry, engagement-ranked directory of 2026's most-viral startup launch videos on X, filterable by category and sortable by views.
design_notes: Function-over-form data directory: sortable table (Startup/category/Likes/Views/Bookmarks/Watch) with emoji-icon metrics. Horizontal category filter bar (Agents, Hardware, Design, Vibecoding, YC, Fundraising). Emoji wordmark, minimal color styling.
take_what: A ready-made leaderboard for sourcing which startup launches are actually breaking through on X right now.

name: The AI Design Aesthetic (Kompozy guide)
one_line: 2026 guide naming the recognizable 'AI look' (oversaturated color, perfect symmetry, zero grain) and the swing toward real material and brand identity.
design_notes: Diagnoses the 'AI look': oversaturated color, glossy even lighting, near-symmetrical composition, zero film grain, identical gradients/glassmorphism, centered layouts, generic 'competent, balanced' copy tone. Cites Canva's 2026 'Imperfect by Design' framing as the counter-move.
take_what: A checklist of visual defaults that now read as 'AI-generated' (symmetry, zero grain, glassmorphism) — a via-negativa spec for what demo screens should avoid.

name: Siteinspire
one_line: Long-running curated gallery; Tech Start-ups + Big Type + Minimal + Typography categories are the active hunting ground for 2026 startup-site trends.
design_notes: Site itself: dense grid of thumbnails, tag/category filters (Minimal, Big Type, Typographic, Black & White), date-stamped submissions — a working taxonomy of what's currently 'in'.
take_what: Category taxonomy (Minimal/Big Type/Typographic/Unusual Layout) is a ready-made checklist for auditing if Astryx's site reads current.

name: Disco Dungeon
one_line: June 2026 Framer Site of the Month: a turn-based puzzle RPG's marketing site where scrolling walks a character through a dungeon.
design_notes: Retro pixel/disco visual language paired with modern scroll-linked animation; vertical scroll literally traverses the game level; repeated modular feature blocks (tile-matching, exploration, arsenal) under a sticky nav.
take_what: Scroll-scrubbed 'walk-through' hero as a way to demo a product's core loop instead of static screenshots.

name: Framer Blog — "15 best tech website designs in 2026"
one_line: Framer's curated roundup of 15 tech/startup sites, each with a one-line design callout.
design_notes: Named w/ callouts: Crayo AI (interactive graphics, hover interactions), Portal (sleek transitions, scroll storytelling), Visual Electric (AI imagery as product demo), Flighty (mobile-first simplicity), Basedash (dev-focused copy w/ docs).
take_what: Ready-made shortlist of fresh (non-Stripe/Linear-tier) startup sites to spot-check for emerging patterns before committing to a direction.

name: AthenaHQ
one_line: GEO startup (Google Search/DeepMind alumni founders) cited as the model for shipping a 3D hero without wrecking Core Web Vitals.
design_notes: Per Utsubo's 2026 guide: keeps an impactful 3D intro but hydrates canvas after the load event, moves shader compilation to a Web Worker/OffscreenCanvas, swaps to a static image on mobile — best-in-class Core Web Vitals despite the 3D hero.
take_what: DOM-first headline/CTA as real HTML; 3D canvas as deferred progressive enhancement (load-after-paint, worker compile, static mobile fallback).

name: neobrutalism.dev (component library)
one_line: Free shadcn/ui-based React + Tailwind library packaging the hard-shadow, thick-border neobrutalist look as drop-in component primitives.
design_notes: Bold flat colors, thick black borders, hard offset drop-shadows on buttons/cards/inputs (no blur), MIT-licensed, positions itself as the anti-default-shadcn-theme for builders who want visible structure.
take_what: A concrete token set (border-width, hard-shadow offsets, flat accent palette) worth sampling for an optional Astryx brutalist theme.

name: Flashtype
one_line: Fresh July 2026 Show HN launch (markdown editor for Claude/Codex) showing the Linear-descendant look on a brand-new startup.
design_notes: Text-first: large sans-serif headline pairing product name with AI-partner logos, terse tagline, no hero illustration. Feature sections use functional screenshots (diff views, agent chat) as evidence. Neutral palette, partner-brand accents only.
take_what: Proof the pattern survives into brand-new 2026 launches, not just legacy dev-tool incumbents — restraint as default for a solo/small-team ship.

name: n8n
one_line: Berlin automation platform, valuation doubled to $5.2B in May 2026 after SAP investment, with a dark particle-heavy enterprise-AI look.
design_notes: Navy/charcoal dark-mode hero with star/particle-field background suggesting parallax depth; purple/lavender accents; alternating text-left/right blocks; illustrated workflow-node diagrams; 2x2 enterprise-feature grid; grayscale logo wall.
take_what: Dark enterprise-AI palette softened with an ambient particle-field hero rather than flat black adds depth without full WebGL cost.

name: Z.ai (Zhipu AI)
one_line: China's Zhipu AI (HKEX-listed Jan 2026), maker of GLM-5.2 (MIT-licensed, 1M-token context, undercuts GPT/Gemini on price); site fronts its AutoClaw agent.
design_notes: Neutral white/dark-gray base, bold "Hi I'm AutoClaw" hero headline with animated SVG mascot, single-column stacked sections (Models/MaaS/Products/News), carousel sliders for product and news cards, accent color reserved for CTA buttons only.
take_what: Personifying an agent product with a name + animated mascot in the hero as a friendlier alternative to a feature-list headline.

name: Fluent 2 Design System site
one_line: Microsoft's public, token-driven design-system site — the styling source of truth shared verbatim between Copilot and all of Microsoft 365.
design_notes: Motion-led hero with cycling text on mostly white background, colorful product screenshots carry the color story; platform-segmented showcase grid with layered UI previews; "Newsworthy" section uses real shipped redesigns (Teams, Outlook, Windows) as proof of system credibility.
take_what: A public token-documentation site as the format for a single-source-of-truth styling doc — a close structural comparison for Astryx's own docs.

name: The strategy behind Dia's design
one_line: Browser Company's own postmortem on Dia's design: keep 95% of the UI calm and hide the 'novelty budget' inside the AI chat surface.
design_notes: Chrome elements (bookmark button, site settings, profile switcher) hidden until hover; active tab's page color bleeds into the tab strip to reinforce continuity; restraint everywhere except the Assistant/Chat sidebar, where brand animation and color 'swell into view.'
take_what: Named concept of a 'novelty budget' — spend expressive motion/color on one AI-moment surface, keep the rest of the system quiet.

name: The Agentic Browser Landscape in 2026: A Complete Guide
one_line: Survey of the UI shift across AI browsers: URL bar replaced by a prompt composer, persistent AI side panels, inspect-before-run transparency.
design_notes: Docs the URL bar replaced by 'a prompt composer' (Google Disco), Chrome's persistent Gemini side panel, Opera Neon's auto-routing 'Intelligent Mode', Fellou's inspect-before-execution transparency, Edge redesigned Copilot-first; notes MCP convergence by June 2026.
take_what: Two dominant patterns worth citing in an AI-integration doc: persistent sidebar-as-workspace, and 'show the agent's plan before it runs.'

name: LaunchList — AI Waitlist Software for AI startups
one_line: A waitlist tool page targeted at AI launches, claiming an in-product reward ('refer 3 friends, skip 500 spots') beats gift cards 5-10x for this audience.
design_notes: Landing page built around a single positioning claim rather than a broad feature list — reward-inside-the-product framing (spot-skip, not cash) as the differentiator for AI-agent-category launches.
take_what: Audience-specific reward framing: for devs, an in-product unlock beats a generic discount.

name: Phia
one_line: Phoebe Gates & Sophia Kianni's AI shopping assistant finding best prices across 350M items; $35M Series A at $185M valuation, celeb-backed.
design_notes: Press describes the product as editorial in feel — 'Vogue meets Glossier' — with clean fonts, calming muted color palettes, and elevated, uncluttered product photography rather than busy e-commerce grids; UI praised as sleek and intuitive.
take_what: Editorial magazine-style calm palette + elevated photography treatment to make a utilitarian tool feel premium

name: Cyera
one_line: AI-data-security unicorn ($12B Series G) leans into purple/teal gradients and crystalline geometry for 'the trust layer for enterprise AI.'
design_notes: Deep purple-to-blue gradient backgrounds; floating crystal/diamond shapes as a recurring data-fragmentation motif; glassmorphic product screenshots; punchy paired tagline ('AI launches your data into orbit. Cyera secures every landing.'); generous whitespace.
take_what: A single recurring abstract shape motif (crystal facets) used system-wide as a security metaphor instead of generic gradient blobs.

name: Isengard Industries
one_line: YC S26 counter-drone/munitions startup's site channels a military HUD: targeting-reticle brackets, a classified-doc ticker, a jet-runway photo.
design_notes: Full-bleed grayscale runway/jet photo; massive tight-tracked uppercase H1 overlaps the image edge; viewfinder corner-brackets on nav/buttons; monospace ticker bar ('PRE-SEED CLOSED...UNCLASSIFIED//CUI'); allied-flag nav icons; deadpan cookie copy ('Decline theatrically').
take_what: Corner-bracket 'reticle' chrome and a monospace status ticker are distinctive framing devices; the deadpan cookie-banner copy is a voice trick worth stealing.

name: Tenkara
one_line: AI ops-agent platform for US manufacturers, tagged '(W26)' by HF0's own account; raised $7M led by True Ventures weeks after demo day.
design_notes: Large display headlines ('Give Your Operators Superpowers'). Hero shows a live agent-simulation panel (Analyzing Market Conditions / Sourcing Suppliers). Modular 9-function grid. Neutral white/gray palette, accent CTAs, hard metric badges (20% cost cut, 3x faster sourcing).
take_what: A live 'agent-at-work' hero panel dramatizing the product acting in real time, paired with hard metric badges as instant proof.

name: Hamilton AI
one_line: 'World's most intelligent private aviation platform' — HF0 grad that compressed a year of product work into 90 days, then raised $7.5M seed.
design_notes: Mesh-gradient hero bg in blues/purples behind a bold single-claim headline. Card grid of 5 features, each with dashboard-screenshot proof (heatmaps, treemaps, demand maps). Interactive revenue calculator embedded in-page; embedded product video.
take_what: Mesh-gradient atmosphere behind a feature-card grid, plus an interactive ROI calculator embedded in the marketing page as a trust device.

name: Fulcrum (withfulcrum.com)
one_line: SPC/CRV-backed insurance-broker AI platform, $25M combined seed+Series A Jan 2026, used by ~1/3 of top-50 US brokerages.
design_notes: Framer-built. Custom variable serif 'Albra Text Flex Light' weight 300, tracking -2px, white on near-black/navy. Electric-blue accent #1668fc paired with warm gold #fac261 — institutional not generic-SaaS. Hero mixes inline sizes: 52px base, 64px emphasis span.
take_what: Light-weight custom serif display type for a trust register instead of another grotesk; navy+electric-blue+gold as institutional-tech palette.

name: Refero.design
one_line: 135k+ screens / 10k+ flows, updated weekly, now ships an MCP endpoint so AI coding agents can query patterns directly.
design_notes: Organizes designs into thematic collections (SaaS dashboards, e-commerce PDPs, onboarding flows); filterable by industry, platform, visual style (dark mode, neumorphism, minimalist).
take_what: The MCP-for-agents distribution model is itself worth stealing for Astryx's own pattern index.

name: Pangram Pangram Foundry
one_line: Montreal foundry's 2026 redesign puts its own typefaces (Neue Montreal, Migra) center stage via Rams-minimal, editorial/gallery layout.
design_notes: Modernist grid blended with editorial magazine rhythm; subtle micro-animations for warmth without clutter; described as 'pared back and elegant, yet distinctly Pangram Pangram.' Motto: 'let the fonts speak.'
take_what: A restrained, gallery-like grid for showcasing a design system's own type/token specimens — let the artifact be the visual, minimal chrome around it.

name: School of Motion — 10 Websites with Great Animation in 2026
one_line: Motion-design educator's ranked list of the 10 best-animated sites of 2026: WebGL agencies, Rive, Apple's cinematic scroll-3D.
design_notes: Names Lusion and Active Theory as the bar for full-screen WebGL abstract-art scenes with cursor-reactive morphing geometry and theatrical scroll transitions; also cites Rive's live state-machine animations and Apple's scroll-locked 3D product rotation.
take_what: A ranked swipe-file of which motion techniques (cursor-reactive WebGL, character-driven Rive, scroll-locked 3D) are currently best-in-class.

name: Utsubo — WebGL & Three.js Site SEO: Make 3D Sites Rankable
one_line: Practical guide to shipping a WebGL/Three.js hero without losing SEO or Core Web Vitals, using AthenaHQ as the worked example.
design_notes: Recommends hero copy/CTA as real DOM text, canvas slot reserved via aspect-ratio, 3D bundle lazy-loaded after `load`, shader compile moved to a Web Worker/OffscreenCanvas, static-image fallback on mobile. WebGL justified only when 'brand IS the experience.'
take_what: Engineering checklist for any WebGL demo: DOM-first content, deferred canvas hydration, off-main-thread compile, static mobile fallback.

name: Scoring Show HN submissions for AI design patterns (Krebs)
one_line: Analysis of ~1,590 Show HN launches scoring shared 'AI slop' visual patterns (22% high density) — quantifies what text-first design reacts against.
design_notes: N/A, data/editorial piece not a site. Systematizes AI-generated-site conventions across fonts/colors/layout/CSS into a pattern-density score.
take_what: Concrete evidence generic AI-slop visual patterns are now common enough to be measured — avoiding all of them measurably differentiates a marketing site.

name: Tomasz "ITom" Szmajda — creative portfolio
one_line: A paper-tear transition opens into a hand-drawn 3D museum corridor of pencil-sketch WebGL shader portraits.
design_notes: Flat paper canvas physically tears via GSAP-driven SVG, revealing a 3D world. Camera glides through a hand-sketched infinite corridor; picture frames self-paint via custom WebGL shader on interaction. Built with React Three Fiber + Three.js + GSAP.
take_what: The 2D-flat-to-3D-world transition mirrors 'a flat mockup becomes a living component' — one bespoke transition, not a whole 3D site, carries the wow.

name: Milkshake
one_line: Link-in-bio app (5M+ downloads) whose marketing site uses swipeable Instagram-Stories-style card carousels to demo its own card-based product.
design_notes: Vertical mobile-optimized stacked sections; horizontal swipe carousels of 'Card' templates and real creator sites; neutral white bg with red accent CTAs; hero pairs headline with dual store badges and '5M+ Downloads, 4.9 Stars' stat block.
take_what: Marketing-site nav can mirror the product's own interaction model — a swipeable-card demo for a swipeable-card product, not a static screenshot grid.

name: Maya Research
one_line: SPC-backed Bengaluru voice-AI startup; open Maya-1 model ranks #2 globally on Artificial Analysis, 440K+ HF downloads, 3M+ installs.
design_notes: Astro-built. Hero h1 huge: 82px, font-normal, tracking -4px (very tight) but word-spacing +8px (unusually wide) — tight-letters/loose-words rhythm reads almost 'spoken.' White text, fades/slides up on load. Brand blue #0351AF.
take_what: Combine extreme negative letter-tracking with positive word-spacing for a rhythmic, voice-like cadence on oversized display headlines.

name: Godly.website (now recent.design)
one_line: Godly.website (now redirects to recent.design) is a curated feed of standout marketing/product sites for layout, motion, and typography study.
design_notes: Positions above Awwwards' cadence with a much higher curation bar — 'more like a fashion magazine than corporate pages' per secondary coverage. The live 301 redirect to recent.design is itself a small 2026 datapoint: design-gallery consolidation/rebranding.
take_what: Use as recurring scouting source for what's winning attention; typography-forward tagging convention worth mirroring in doc site's own examples index.

name: Semaloop (semaloop.com)
one_line: Dev-tooling/tech startup site, big-type minimal, added to Siteinspire May 15 2026.
design_notes: Large-scale display typography as the primary hero element, clean spacious grid, neutral black/white/gray palette with a selective accent, responsive desktop+mobile hero variants, no visual clutter.
take_what: Confirms 'big type + near-empty canvas' as a repeatable pattern for a dev-tooling landing hero — type carries brand voice, not illustration.

name: Land-book
one_line: Daily-updated landing-page gallery with dedicated 'AI' category and 'Dark Colors' style filter across 200k+ categorized page sections.
design_notes: Filters by color, typography, style, industry, and platform (Framer/Webflow/etc.); reviewers rate it stronger for real conversion-oriented startup/SaaS patterns than art-directed galleries like Awwwards — what funded startups actually ship.
take_what: Filter to AI x Dark-Colors intersection for a fast snapshot of hero/pricing/footer conventions instead of eyeballing one-off sites.

name: Mobbin
one_line: Curated library of 200k+ real product UI screens, filterable by flow, incl. SaaS marketing sites, dashboards, onboarding.
design_notes: Aggregates real production screens (not concepts); organized by flow (onboarding, pricing, dashboard) not aesthetic category; treated as ground-truth over Dribbble-style concept art.
take_what: Ground-truth reference for how live SaaS hero/pricing/nav patterns actually ship, not idealized mockups.

name: IVRESS — Spin a Tale
one_line: Nine-chapter painterly WebGL narrative microsite by Laugh Mind Co., FWA People's Choice Top 100 winner.
design_notes: Particle-effect painterly WebGL scenes, strong dark/light contrast for a menacing-yet-optimistic tone. Story structured as numbered chapters ending in a spiral-of-light transition into the parent brand site; ambient soundtrack accompanies scroll.
take_what: Chaptered, scroll-gated storytelling (numbered acts vs one long scroll) is a transferable pattern for a docs/onboarding narrative.

name: Gemini Neural Expressive hands-on
one_line: Hands-on calls Neural Expressive 'the best Gemini has ever looked' but says the polish papers over cluttered navigation underneath.
design_notes: Cycling gradient (cycles through the Gemini icon's colors) replaces the old spinner during processing. Larger centered greeting. Headings now break up long responses into article-like layout. Reviewer verdict: 'the old app was uglier, but more useful.'
take_what: Caution against polishing the hero while nav/IA debt lingers — a reminder for docs sites where the landing page shines but component nav lags.

design_notes: Drop-in npm package creates a mouse-following spotlight over a darkened page (true 'flashlight' dark mode), distinct from magnetic/trail effects — the reveal-on-hover cursor pattern also cited across 2026 dark-mode hero writeups.
name: real-dark-mode — flashlight cursor npm package
one_line: Show HN npm package: cursor becomes a flashlight, spotlighting content while the rest of the page darkens — the reveal-cursor pattern.
take_what: Spotlight/reveal cursor (page darkens, mouse is a flashlight) — candidate for a dark-mode Astryx hero wanting a guided-reveal moment.

name: Vurt (myvurtpro.com)
one_line: Mobile-first vertical streaming platform for indie filmmakers' micro-series, funded/launched March 2026, covered by TechCrunch.
design_notes: High-contrast black-and-white photography, bold sans headline 'Vertical Cinema. Vertical Stories. Uncompromised.', numbered feature callouts (01-04), full-width vertical image galleries, app-store badges in footer — no landscape imagery anywhere.
take_what: Prove a vertical-video product's identity by never cropping hero imagery to landscape — commit the whole grid to portrait framing.

name: Supabase Docs homepage
one_line: Supabase's docs homepage opens with a framework icon-grid (React, Next.js, Vue, Flutter) for one-click quickstarts, in its signature dark/emerald theme.
design_notes: Dark-mode-first with dedicated light/dark logo assets; icon-based framework cards for progressive-disclosure quickstarts; modular product cards (Database, Auth, Storage, Realtime, Edge Functions) with icons; migration-guide section with provider icons (AWS, Firebase, Heroku).
take_what: Icon-grid quickstart cards as the very first content on a docs landing page — sorts visitors to their framework/component before any prose.

name: OpenAI's rebrand, explained
one_line: Wallpaper* deep-dive on OpenAI's rebrand: OpenAI Sans (with ABC Dinamo), the blossom logo's 'seed of life' grid, the coded 'emotive point' animation.
design_notes: Explains the emotive point is not a canned motion file but a live-coded, input-responsive pulsing disc with a watercolour-style swirl background — OpenAI's presence indicator across every product surface at every scale.
take_what: A single branded 'presence indicator' component (one glyph, many states/sizes, coded not baked) as a reusable AI/status avatar primitive.

name: Flowjam — 25 waitlist landing page examples that convert
one_line: A 2026 roundup citing ChatGPT, Robinhood, Arc as conversion benchmarks (8-20%): single headline, single-field form above fold, mobile-first signup.
design_notes: Prescribes: no nav/'learn more' on hero, one email field only, live signup counter or referral position directly under the form, mobile-first since most prelaunch traffic is X/Reddit/Indie Hackers.
take_what: Radical hero minimalism for a 'request early access' page: strip nav, one field, one proof point.

name: Mida — A/B Testing Pricing Pages
one_line: Practitioner framework: pricing tests have outsized effect (2-3% landing moves → 8-15% on pricing); a decoy top tier lifts mid-tier conversion 10-20%.
design_notes: No screenshots — a text framework (May 2026) on what to test: plan count/structure, billing-toggle default, highlighted-plan treatment, feature-list format, social-proof placement; explicitly flags 2-4 week minimum test runtime.
take_what: Decoy-tier anchoring logic (add a higher tier to lift mid-tier 10-20%) as rationale for a 3-4-tier default Astryx pricing template, not just 2.

name: Coralogix
one_line: Observability platform betting 'someone needs to watch the AI agents' raised $200M (June 3, 2026).
design_notes: Dark navy-to-charcoal gradient sections, bright cyan/blue CTAs; provocative hero line 'You can't observe the future with yesterday's architecture' instead of a feature list; named in-product AI assistant ('Olly') as recurring brand device; compliance badges in footer.
take_what: A provocative problem-statement headline, not a feature summary, plus a named in-product AI persona as a recurring brand device.

name: The 11 standout startups from YC's Demo Day, according to VCs
one_line: TechCrunch's VC-sourced list of standout YC Spring 2026 startups; several are agent-orchestration/testing dev tools (Superset, Arga Labs, Sazabi).
design_notes: No single shared visual system — these are days-old sites on default dark/monospace dev-tool templates; the real signal is category concentration: agent-orchestration, agent-testing/sandboxing, and agent-driven bug-fixing dominate new dev-tool sites right now.
take_what: Confirms which product category is minting the most new dev-tool marketing sites right now — a lens for which competitor sites to watch next.

name: Sesame
one_line: Conversational voice-AI app from Oculus founders with distinct AI personas (Maya, Miles, Simone, Charlie); $250M Series B, iOS launch in 39 countries.
design_notes: Grayscale/monochrome palette, heavy whitespace, oversized headline ('Curiosity, met') over full-width hero photo; single-column scroll, symmetrical nav; repeated lifestyle photography sections build an aspirational, premium feel ahead of a 2027 eyewear device.
take_what: Monochrome restraint + generous negative space + one oversized emotive headline to signal premium confidence

name: Nitra
one_line: Financial operating system for healthcare practices raised $187M combined Series A/B (2026) from NEA, Pantera and others.
design_notes: Clean modular card layout, light neutral background, accent-color CTAs ('Get Started', 'Book a Demo'); hero targets practice-owner pain point; AI-avatar 'Trina' with live task-notification feed; specialty sub-pages; SOC2/HIPAA badges near fold.
take_what: A named AI-agent avatar with a live notification feed shows an AI feature doing work rather than describing it abstractly.

name: Fomo
one_line: Social crypto trading app ($75M Series B, $550M valuation) styled as dark space-opera with astronaut hero and neon.
design_notes: Deep navy/black space-themed background with neon accents; astronaut illustration as hero mascot; bold headline 'where traders become legends'; device mockups showing leaderboard/social-feed UI; circular gradient footer imagery; gaming-adjacent visual language.
take_what: Narrative mascot illustration (astronaut/legend framing) turns a utilitarian trading product into an aspirational identity.

name: Oryzo AI
one_line: Lusion-built product microsite turning a cork coaster into a cinematic 3D showcase; SOTD, black/orange palette.
design_notes: Black #100904 + orange #FF8539, two colors. WebGL sketches, Three.js+GSAP, 3D-to-2D transforms, particle footer. Overall 7.86, creativity 8.35, animation 8.60, community 9.33.
take_what: Tight 2-color palette plus one standout motion moment (particle footer) beats a fuller palette on creativity scores.

name: Landing.love — WebGL collection
one_line: Landing.love's WebGL collection catalogs the current default 'prestige' launch aesthetic: full-viewport 3D hero canvases and agency-grade motion.
design_notes: 15+ surveyed sites skew Portfolio/Agency/3D-Website tags; recurring pattern of full-viewport 3D-canvas heroes and minimal color; the gallery's own taxonomy (Dark Mode / Gradient / Retro / GSAP / WebGL / ThreeJS) doubles as a trend checklist.
take_what: Use the gallery's tag taxonomy as a checklist of aesthetic buckets to opt into or out of — e.g. a restrained scroll reveal without full WebGL.

name: "Anti-AI Design Trends 2026" (Crea8ive Solution)
one_line: Documents 'tactile brutalism' and intentional friction (scanned textures, ink bleeds, asymmetry) as deliberate rejection of AI-polish homogenization.
design_notes: Raw geometry, aggressive color contrast, simulated physical texture, '1px solid' stark borders against dark backgrounds, messy layered layouts — positioned as proof-of-human-authorship signals against beige/glossy AI sameness.
take_what: A deliberate-imperfection lever (grain, texture, asymmetry) to keep a component-driven design system from reading as generically AI-polished.

name: Framerbite — 20 Beautiful Framer Websites (2026)
one_line: Blog roundup of 20 startup/product/portfolio sites built in Framer, explicitly framed as '2026 inspiration.'
design_notes: Cross-site patterns repeat: dark-mode + minimalist type (Superhuman), horizontal-scroll portfolios (diana.lu), monochromatic + bold type (darkroomagency.com), bright/playful gamified sections (Donutshop, Yuna, FEASTIE) — split between restrained SaaS and maximalist consumer play.
take_what: Sortable reference set for picking a hero pattern (search-bar, horizontal-scroll, modular scroll) per page type.

name: EverSwap (design by Lusion)
one_line: DeFi liquidity protocol site by 3D studio Lusion, Awwwards SOTD June 22 2026, scored 7.58/10.
design_notes: Minimal cream/dark-green palette (#fbfff4 / #203727), built with WebGL, Blender, Figma; video-driven intro/nav, full 3D interactive scenes — maximalist motion for a category that usually defaults to flat dashboards.
take_what: Shows agencies pushing 3D/WebGL even into finance products to differentiate from flat SaaS dashboards — a ceiling data point for motion investment.

name: OH no Type Co.
one_line: Indie foundry (Degular, Cheee, Obviously) pushing variable fonts with non-traditional axes — SERIF, WONK, CASUAL, even a 'MOOD' slider.
design_notes: Coverage frames OH no as leading both 'hyper-personal variable display' (sliders dialing formality/irregularity live) and 'anti-AI handwriting' — organic over geometric, lively over perfect.
take_what: Variable-axis thinking beyond weight/width: a token exposing a literal 'personality slider' (formal to casual), mirroring tone-axis tokens.

name: Top 10 Vibe-Coded Websites 2026 (Triple Minds)
one_line: Case-study roundup of 10 fully AI ("vibe-coded") commercial sites, each still supervised by one senior developer.
design_notes: Sites span marketplaces, agency directories, and AI-companion apps with standard SaaS conventions (listing cards, filters, dashboards, subscription flows) — competent but visually generic; the piece's own thesis is that unsupervised AI generation converges toward sameness.
take_what: AI-generated sites are functionally solid but visually generic — proof a real design system (tokens, considered type/motion) stays the differentiator.

name: Awwwards — Best Three.js Websites
one_line: Awwwards' live Three.js category: current SOTD winners (Podium, Ten Years Away, digitalists.at) plus product sites (Obys, Ciao Energy, aorum.io).
design_notes: Recent SOTD/nominee mix skews toward interactive 3D storytelling and spatial navigation as the differentiator; digitalists.at (Jun 21 2026 SOTD) also Three.js-driven, emphasizing motion-forward responsive design.
take_what: An always-current trend radar for which specific Three.js execution patterns are winning now, vs. relying on one dated best-of list.

name: Awwwards — Best GSAP Websites
one_line: Awwwards' GSAP category: Wembi, Podium, Ten Years Away, Clico, CyberCrest Compliance, SSTR — spanning AI, B2B compliance, technical products.
design_notes: Notably includes B2B/compliance-software sites (CyberCrest Compliance, SSTR 'Friction Reduction Systems') getting award attention for GSAP execution — motion craft now reaches dry B2B categories, not just consumer/creative brands.
take_what: Evidence that award-grade motion polish is now expected even for un-glamorous B2B products — raises the bar industry-wide.

name: ampcode.com (Sourcegraph's Amp)
one_line: Sourcegraph's agentic CLI "Amp" pairs a dark, no-gradient hero with a monospace install snippet and a rolling news feed, not a case-study carousel.
design_notes: Dark background for contrast, large sans display headline ("Everything Is Changing") over monospace `curl` install command, testimonial quotes, footer news feed implies ongoing motion/freshness without animation gimmicks.
take_what: A small persistent "latest updates" feed block near the footer keeps a static marketing page feeling current without motion graphics.

name: Linear design: the SaaS trend that's boring and bettering UI (LogRocket)
one_line: UX-press piece arguing sequential linear layout cuts cognitive load and lifts conversion, while warning the look (Stripe, Raycast, GitHub, Wise) risks sameness.
design_notes: N/A, editorial piece. Defines 'linear design' as straightforward, sequential, one-dimensional scrolling with minimal branching; flags ubiquity making sites indistinguishable.
take_what: The UX case for restraint (lower cognitive load, higher conversion) plus a warning to add one distinctive signature so restraint doesn't collapse into sameness.

name: Wolverine Worldwide
one_line: Locomotive-built corporate brand site, Awwwards SOTD June 24 2026, monochrome and confident.
design_notes: Strict 2-color palette (#010101 black, #FFFFFF white). Big background imagery, Locomotive Scroll smooth-scroll library, GSAP, Craft CMS. Clean corporate register — proves brutal-simple monochrome still wins top design awards.
take_what: A pure black/white palette plus one smooth-scroll library reads as premium without any 3D budget.

name: Manus (Butterfly Effect)
one_line: Singapore-headquartered AI agent ("hands-on AI") now folded into Meta; site markets slide/website/app-building agent capability directly.
design_notes: Bold minimalist headline "Less structure, more intelligence"; hero built around task-shortcut buttons (Create slides / Build website / Develop desktop apps) instead of an abstract pitch; prominent banner announces the Meta acquisition.
take_what: Replacing a generic hero CTA with task-specific shortcut buttons that map directly to what the product does.

name: OpenAI rebrand critique — House of Gai
one_line: Design press splits on OpenAI's rebrand: futuristic and human-warm, but some argue it leans on motion to carry work static design usually does.
design_notes: Frames the identity as 'Black Mirror meets Apple' futurism. Praise for restraint and warmth, but a 'motion design flex' critique: the pulsing Emotive Point does a lot of the identity's work, leaving static/no-motion states thinner.
take_what: Don't let one animated hero flourish carry the whole identity — back it with a strong static state for reduced-motion and no-JS contexts.

name: AREA 17 × OpenAI case study
one_line: Agency case study on building openai.com: zoned site architecture, black-for-sophistication, candid team photography, Twill CMS for velocity.
design_notes: Site split into research / deployment / applications zones for technical vs general audiences. Black signals technical sophistication; vibrant accents signal accessibility. Candid team photography humanizes. Twill CMS enables fast cross-team publishing.
take_what: Zone a marketing/docs site by audience intent (engineers vs designers) rather than one linear scroll.

design_notes: Custom cursor lets visitors 'draw with fluorescent lights' across the page — Awwwards notes it requires 'significantly more coding' than standard cursor swaps. Signature flourish for a creative-agency homepage, not a utility pattern.
name: Komnata — creative agency site
one_line: Awwwards-honored agency site where the cursor becomes a paintbrush of fluorescent light — the high-effort end of the spectrum.
take_what: Marks the upper bound of cursor-as-canvas effort — a reference for 'how far it can go,' not a pattern to copy for a B2B product site.

name: Fellou
one_line: Self-styled 'first agentic browser' with a minimalist white-space hero and a live 'shadow workspace' visualization of its own AI actions.
design_notes: Restrained white-space layout, no bold house color (accents borrowed from integrated logos: Google blue, Reddit orange, X black); Fellou Home is a spatial/Z-axis 3D workspace; live status chips ('Thinking…', 'Connecting…') visualize the agent under a 'never a black box' promise.
take_what: Real-time agent-status-chip micro-pattern ('Thinking…', 'Connecting…') as a trust-building live-state indicator for any async AI action.

name: Stark Defence
one_line: Defense-drone maker (€500M round, ~€3.5B valuation) presents itself via stark black-and-white photography, not illustration.
design_notes: Dark, high-contrast, near-monochrome palette (black/white/gray); photography-led hero (operational drone imagery) instead of animation; blunt all-caps tagline ('RAPIDLY DEVELOPED. PRECISELY DEPLOYED.'); card-grid product showcase (VIRTUS, VANTA, MINERVA, GAMBIT, CASCADE).
take_what: Photography-over-illustration restraint proves a design system can skip motion/3D entirely and still read as premium.

name: Goldfish (goldfish.sh)
one_line: Swedish-founder Mac AI-memory app, won Product of the Day and ranked #2 monthly PH leaderboard for June 2026.
design_notes: Stark white background, high-contrast black text, italicized emphasis mid-headline ('One click to answer every message.'), live playful counter widget ('0 Option clicks made so far'), YC/Harvard/Stanford + ElevenLabs/Mistral/PostHog logo wall, minimal motion.
take_what: A single playful live-counter widget as the one 'delight' flourish on an otherwise stripped-down page.

name: 8 Landing Page Design Trends for B2B SaaS in 2026 (SaaSHero)
one_line: Data-backed trend roundup: bento grids (67% of top 100 PH SaaS sites), single-CTA minimalism, interactive demos, video-first proof.
design_notes: Cites stats: single-CTA pages convert 13.5% vs 10.5% for 5+ CTAs; bento grids correlate with 47% higher dwell time/38% higher CTR; personalized CTAs beat generic by 202%; interactive demos drive 63% higher lead conversion.
take_what: Bento-grid modular card layout for feature showcases, and a single dominant CTA per section, both directly applicable to a design-system marketing site.

name: Airtable AI-native relaunch (Howie Liu)
one_line: Howie Liu's founder-to-camera X thread repositioning Airtable as an 'AI-native app platform' pulled 8.1M views.
design_notes: Delivered as a native video thread on X, not a press release; paired same-day with airtable.com's clean white full-bleed homepage, bold sans headline, dual CTA, product-screenshot carousel and AI-feature GIFs.
take_what: Ship a founder-narrated video thread on X same-day as a marketing-site relaunch; the video is what actually spreads.

name: Tesoro
one_line: Awwwards SOTD site cited by Webflow for deploying its entire color system, not just an accent, across the whole homepage.
design_notes: Webflow: 'shifting background colors and icon treatments' plus animated preloader all pull from one deployed color system. Awwwards/ecomm.design lists it Webflow-built, light-cream/charcoal (#FDF8F3 / #222222) base.
take_what: Color as a full deployed system (loader, icon fills, section bg all shifting in register) is an alternative to one-accent-on-neutral.

name: Manish Kumar (@Manixh02) on X — why every AI-built website looks the same
one_line: Viral X post naming the exact AI-website tell — purple gradients, Inter, three boxes, rounded corners — 'statistical average design, not bad design.'
design_notes: Calls out the precise cliché stack — purple/indigo gradient hero, Inter, three-card feature row, rounded corners — as the default LLM output signature; frames it as pattern-matching, not taste.
take_what: Confirms which tropes (purple-gradient hero + Inter + 3-card row) currently read 'generic AI site' — Astryx's site should visibly break one.

name: Brutalist Report
one_line: "The day's headlines delivered to you without bullshit" — a tech-news aggregator styled as a bare text feed, zero ads or cards.
design_notes: Plain sans headlines, horizontal topic nav (Tech/News/Business/Science), columnar feed of source+headline+timestamp, minimal borders/spacing, light/dark toggle, filter controls as the only interactive chrome.
take_what: A zero-card changelog/blog-index pattern — headline, source, date, nothing else — as an alternative to image-heavy blog card grids.

name: Rijksmuseum
one_line: Gold-standard museum site: art-forward, frictionless architecture, near-zero visual noise around 800k+ artworks.
design_notes: Simple, striking layout puts the artwork itself front and center rather than institutional branding; engaging video stories woven into collection browsing; frictionless ticket-purchase flow cited as UX benchmark.
take_what: Content (the component/example) as the hero visual, chrome minimized around it — analogous to letting component previews star over marketing illustration.

name: Sarvam AI
one_line: Bengaluru sovereign-AI unicorn ($1.5B valuation, $234M Series B close Jun 2026, backed by HCLTech/Bessemer/Khosla) building Indian-language LLMs.
design_notes: Monochrome black-on-white base with decorative hero-gradient SVG motifs, enterprise-logo carousel, card-grid feature/product sections, testimonial carousel, Hindi-script TTS sample embedded in-page, SOC2/ISO trust badges in footer.
take_what: Embedding a live, native-script product sample (Hindi TTS) directly in the marketing page as concrete proof-of-capability instead of a screenshot.

design_notes: DOM+GSAP only, no WebGL/canvas: preloaded hidden images spawn along the cursor path, elastic.out/back.in easing drives bounce+rotation+drift physics — a lightweight, non-shader implementation path for the trend.
name: Codrops — Gravity-Based Mouse Trail (May 2026)
one_line: Codrops tutorial: a GSAP-only gravity mouse trail where images spawn at the cursor and bounce off the viewport floor.
take_what: A lightweight DOM+GSAP recipe proving cursor-trail effects don't require a WebGL/shader stack — usable as an Astryx motion cookbook example.

name: Robinhood queue-jump waitlist (via KickoffLabs teardown)
one_line: The 2013 case study still cited in 2026 guides: a post-signup status page shows exact rank plus a same-page share widget instead of a dead thank-you page.
design_notes: Email-only signup, benefit-only headline; confirmation screen shows numeric rank ('#198,432') with inline share buttons on the same screen. KickoffLabs' widget auto-renders rank + reward-tier notices + extra actions (Instagram follow, Shopify buy).
take_what: Fold position display + share CTA into one screen instead of a dead-end confirmation.

name: Board (board.fun)
one_line: Face-to-face gaming console from Mirror founder Brynn Putnam; $20M Series A led by USV, announced June 2 2026 (TechCrunch).
design_notes: White bg, bold black type, hot-pink game-piece accents; multi-frame animated flipbook hero sequence demoing the product in motion; alternating full-width sections, game-card grids, and a press-logo testimonial carousel; isolated product photography on white.
take_what: Frame-by-frame flipbook hero animation as a lightweight alternative to autoplay video — shows motion without WebGL/video weight.

name: Cosmos
one_line: Moodboard/visual-research tool for creatives — search images 'by color' or similarity; beloved reference tool in the design community.
design_notes: Neutral white/gray/black base with one saturated accent (#bc361b) used functionally in a 'search by color' demo, not decoratively. Oversized headline sits above three vertical image tiles; full-width image grids alternate with text down a single scroll column.
take_what: Neutral base palette + one saturated accent reserved for a specific functional demo, not spread across the UI

name: Cloaked
one_line: Privacy/identity-protection platform raised $375M Series B + growth financing (Mar 2026) led by General Catalyst, expanding into enterprise.
design_notes: Minimalist neutral base (white/gray) with a purposeful accent on primary actions; threat-framed hero copy; large stat callouts ('60M+ calls screened', '1.7B+ records removed'); Trustpilot/Product Hunt/PCMag badges; star-rated testimonials.
take_what: Blunt stat callouts as trust-building hero-adjacent content; badge clustering to borrow credibility fast for enterprise buyers.

name: TechCrunch: 16 of the most interesting startups from YC W26 Demo Day
one_line: TechCrunch's roundup of 16 W26 Demo Day startups worth watching, spanning AGI benchmarking, robotics data, security-camera AI, and drone radar.
design_notes: Standard TechCrunch editorial article, not itself a design artifact — used as sourcing evidence for which W26 companies are drawing press attention and are worth site-checking.
take_what: Use as a sourcing map for which W26 companies to revisit as their site polish and attention grow post-Demo Day.

name: TownSquare
one_line: A lightweight embeddable widget giving any website real-time visitor presence and brief interaction, no accounts, no algorithm.
design_notes: Light neutral palette (white/off-white, dark text), heart-symbol accents, casual emoji copy ('Let's go! 🎉'); a live interactive demo square lets visitors 'activate' presence in place; deliberately 'cozy corner of the internet' rather than growth-hacky.
take_what: The 'cozy, human, anti-algorithm' voice, and a live-demo-embedded-in-page pattern — show the actual widget live, in situ, not a screenshot or video.

name: Daylight Computer
one_line: The e-ink 'Daylight' tablet's one-page site, built by basement.studio, sold out its launch and swept design-award galleries.
design_notes: Calm off-white/paper tones echoing the e-ink screen; large humanist type; long-scroll storytelling with sparse full-bleed product shots; minimal chrome; deliberately no dark-mode/neon-gradient cliche.
take_what: A quiet, paper-toned, slow-scroll voice can out-award the loud dark-neon AI aesthetic; a calm alternative for a trustworthy site.

name: Anti-AI Crafting: The $50M Handmade Rebellion
one_line: Brands command 10-50x pricing premiums in 2026 by proving visible human process against AI-generated sameness.
design_notes: Wabi-sabi framing: beauty in imperfection. Examples: Burberry's stitched-fabric campaign, Apple TV intro shot with hand-blown glass/zero CGI (imperfections left visible), Madalena Studio growing bacteria on a cork logo. Cites 67% higher engagement for handmade vs AI-only work.
take_what: Visible-process detail (texture, a hand-drawn mark, one imperfect flourish) as a craft signal — worth one deliberate touch inside a systematic site.

name: saaslandingpage.com
one_line: A 940-strong SaaS-only landing page swipe file whose own trend note quantifies bento-grid dominance among top Product Hunt SaaS sites.
design_notes: Cites 67% of the top 100 Product Hunt SaaS sites now using bento-grid layouts, correlated with 47% higher dwell time / 38% higher click-through; also flags looping hero video, liquid-glass surfaces and disciplined italic editorial type.
take_what: Bento-grid feature layout as the default way to present a multi-capability product scannable in one fold, backed by a measured engagement-lift claim.

name: Marketer Milk — 32 Best SaaS Websites 2026
one_line: 32-site breakdown of current SaaS sites (Framer, Ramp, Spline, Gumroad, Cofounder, Wispr Flow) with hero/nav/pricing detail.
design_notes: Recurring patterns: PAYG pricing sliders (Cofounder, Ghost, Jasper); hidden dropdown pricing forcing a demo click (Wispr Flow, tranch, Pipe); left-sidebar nav breaking top-nav norms (Cofounder); dark-mode dev aesthetic (Spline, Decodable).
take_what: Usage-based pricing sliders and 'hide pricing behind a dropdown' are both viable moves for a dev-tool pricing page.

name: Cofounder.co
one_line: "Run an entire company with AI" agent platform; pairs pay-as-you-go pricing with a chaptered, stage-based nav.
design_notes: Modular card-grid layout with decorative SVG cloud motifs and dashboard mockups showing growth-arrow metrics; top nav organized as sequential company-building chapters (Start/Build/Sell/Scale) rather than a feature taxonomy; $20/$50 base-plus-usage pricing via calculator.
take_what: Structuring primary nav around customer journey stages, not the product's feature taxonomy, is a distinctive IA move.

name: Thinking Machines Lab — thinkingmachines.ai
one_line: Mira Murati's $12B AI lab runs a text-forward, ornament-free site — no hero imagery, pure typographic hierarchy carrying the entire homepage.
design_notes: No hero visual, gradient, or 3D — typography alone carries the page. Short mission-statement sections ('Science is better when shared') ARE the homepage. Minimal nav (Tinker, Connectionism, News). Credential-drop footer (ChatGPT, PyTorch lineage) replaces a logo bar.
take_what: Proves a frontier AI org can win attention via pure typographic confidence, zero ornamentation — a 'quiet mode' opposite bento/gradient maximalism.

name: Typescale.com
one_line: Google-Fonts-integrated type scale generator with a split-pane editor and live rendered preview at multiple breakpoints.
design_notes: Split layout: left control panel (font pickers, weight, line-height, letter-spacing, ratio presets like "1.618 Golden Ratio"), right live preview toggling mobile/desktop; neutral white bg, icon-driven toolbar (save, CSS export, login); minimal chrome, type is the content.
