take_what: Named-ratio presets (Golden Ratio, Minor Second) as human-readable labels instead of raw numbers make a token scale legible to non-engineers.

name: Waitlister — no-code waitlist + referral builder
one_line: A waitlist-building SaaS whose own site demos the pattern live: tabbed mockups of landing page, thank-you/referral screen, and subscriber dashboard.
design_notes: White/light bg, dark high-contrast text, bold headline ('The waitlist software to launch your product'), dual CTAs, social proof ('10,000+ founders', 4.6/5). Three tabbed demo panels swap via interactive tab state: landing, referral thank-you, submissions.
take_what: Tabbed self-demo: show the exact screen types (signup, status, referral) inline on the marketing page.

name: Muzli — Pricing & Plans Page Inspiration
one_line: Muzli's 60+ pricing & plans page roundup framed explicitly around "2026 trends."
design_notes: Curated screenshot list from the long-running Muzli design-inspiration aggregator; groups by pricing model (subscription, usage-based, one-off) rather than just company logo.
take_what: Cross-check Astryx's own pricing-related doc pages against a trend-labeled set to keep card/toggle/badge conventions current.

name: YC Tier List (W26)
one_line: Independent, non-YC-affiliated site that grades every YC batch company S-through-D on a classic gamer tier-list board, with a detail page per W26 startup.
design_notes: Literary italic serif wordmark 'YC Tier List' over a plain light background, colored horizontal tier bars (red S, orange A, gold B) each packed with small square company-logo tiles, batch-switcher dropdown, search bar.
take_what: Borrowing a meme UI convention (tier list) wholesale as an information-dense grid/legend pattern could inspire a component-comparison gallery page.

name: Design Signal — Glassmorphism vs Liquid Glass
one_line: Argues Apple's Liquid Glass language is superseding static glassmorphism with panels that adapt opacity/contrast to their background.
design_notes: Contrasts fixed frosted-glass cards (Spotify playlist cards, Stripe dashboard overlays) against adaptive surfaces (Figma's context-aware panel opacity, Material Design 3 dynamic color tokens); claims better performance and accessibility for the adaptive approach.
take_what: Adaptive-opacity panel background (color-mix()/light-dark()-driven) over a static frosted-glass blur, for translucent overlay/popover surfaces.

name: Artboard Studio
one_line: Graphic/motion design automation tool; Yasir Ekinci's Framer site was a June 2026 SOTM runner-up and an Awwwards honorable mention.
design_notes: 'Stunning bright palette and energetic illustrations' with carefully crafted scroll effects and micro-interactions — a SaaS tool site leaning maximalist/colorful rather than the dark-minimal SaaS default.
take_what: Counter-example to dark-mode-SaaS default: bright, illustrated, playful can still read premium for a dev tool.

name: ABC Dinamo — ABC Schengen release
one_line: Berlin foundry Dinamo's Feb 2026 ABC Schengen: a 108-font, six-years-in-development auto/industrial family, plus a per-purchase 'Font Customizer.'
design_notes: Visual language drawn from European trade, transport, and manufacturing signage. Large stylistic-alternate sets let buyers dial in tone before checkout — a productized approach to type customization.
take_what: The 'customizer before checkout' pattern: a typeface or design-system theme as configurable product with live alternate/token preview.

name: Fonts In Use — Tech Startups tag
one_line: Curated archive of real startup type pairings (Nothing Phone, Rabbit R1, Matter Intelligence, Wellhub) documenting exactly which faces each shipped with.
design_notes: Concrete pairings: Nothing Phone→NType 82 + Mono + NDot; Rabbit R1→Power Grotesk; Matter Intelligence→ABC Monument Grotesk + ABC Diatype Mono — a primary grotesk plus companion mono recurs.
take_what: Reusable two-typeface system: one humanist face for voice, one mono for data/specs/code, rather than a single do-everything face.

name: The rise of Linear style design (Medium)
one_line: Traces how Linear's dark, restrained look became a named genre ('Linear style'), citing Raycast, Reflect, and Twingate as followers.
design_notes: N/A, editorial piece. Describes genre traits: dark backgrounds, one accent gradient/sphere, subtle blur, micro-motion, Inter typography.
take_what: Named-genre evidence for 'Linear style' — useful shorthand when briefing a direction as Linear-descendant, not generic dark mode.

name: 20 Most Beautiful Website Designs of 2026 (SitesPlaced)
one_line: Curated 2026 roundup that surfaces cream-and-gold, cream-canvas, and 'quiet editorial' templates as standout categories alongside dark/cinematic sites.
design_notes: Named entries include a 'cream-and-gold' gallery-grade luxury storefront, a 'cream-canvas' tilted-reel agency layout, a 'quiet editorial' studio landing with refined type and generous whitespace, and a monochrome scroll-driven word-reveal style.
take_what: Editorial-cream and monochrome-restraint are named premium categories in 2026 roundups, not niche outliers — vocabulary ('quiet editorial') for briefs.

name: Why Do Most AI-Generated Websites Look the Same (Shuffle)
one_line: January 2026 piece diagnosing why AI website builders converge on dark, purple-gradient sameness — exactly what light/editorial sites react against.
design_notes: Names AI design-slop patterns: dark mode with low-contrast body text, lavender-purple accents, Inter font, gradient glows, centered hero with badge, identical icon feature-cards. Frames the $6.3B AI website-builder market as the volume driver of sameness.
take_what: Confirms the pattern-set (dark mode, purple glow, centered badge hero, icon feature grid) to deliberately avoid so a light/serif site reads intentional.

name: Max Mara — Jacket Circle
one_line: Adoratorio Studio's illustrated PixiJS microsite for Max Mara, Awwwards SOTD April 16 2026, pastel 3D illustration world.
design_notes: 2-color pastel palette (#E59291 dusty rose, #E7D497 gold). Hand-illustrated 3D scenes rendered in PixiJS + GSAP, microinteractions, big illustrated backgrounds instead of photography — reads as a picture-book, not a lookbook.
take_what: Illustration-as-hero instead of stock photography lowers production cost while reading as distinctive; PixiJS for light 2D-in-3D scenes vs heavy WebGL.

name: Bolt brand refresh
one_line: Estonian mobility giant's in-house rebrand: unified green, switch to Inter, dimensional 3D illustration, and a bespoke sonic identity.
design_notes: Single unified darker-green (a11y-adjusted) across 600+ cities; typeface Euclid→Inter (990 languages); 400+ illustrations moved flat Corporate-Memphis to dimensional subtly-animated 3D; sonic identity 'Qui' built from disassembled scooter parts.
take_what: Sonic identity and motion-illustration treated as first-class rebrand deliverables, not afterthoughts — built entirely in-house.

name: Studio Dumbar/DEPT — Instagram motion identity
one_line: Dutch motion studio (part of DEPT); its imperfection-driven Instagram motion system exemplifies the 2026 kinetic, human-imperfect identity trend.
design_notes: Motion system deliberately echoes imperfections of natural human movement and UGC rather than slick geometric loops; studio speaking on 'Everything in Motion' at Forward Festival Frankfurt 2026.
take_what: Motion identity as a designed rule-system for how brand elements move, and deliberate imperfection reading as more human than polished loops.

name: Genspark
one_line: LG- and Korea Mirae Asset-backed "AI workspace" startup, $2.6B valuation (Series B extension to $485M, mid-2026), expanding into Japan and Korea.
design_notes: Reviewers note the homepage "drops you straight into the workspace with no product introduction" — skips the traditional feature-showcase marketing funnel entirely in favor of immediate tool access, echoing Google Workspace's familiar editor chrome.
take_what: Counter-trend worth weighing: for a docs site, skip the pitch and default straight to a live tool/sandbox for a technically fluent audience.

name: Microsoft 365 Copilot — 2026 redesign
one_line: Copilot's redesign skips an expressive AI look entirely: progressive disclosure, a task-aware workspace, and shared Fluent 2 styling with Office.
design_notes: Static prompt box becomes a 'task-aware workspace' revealing tools beneath it only as needed (progressive disclosure). Collapsible left nav; side pane as 'editing partner.' Adopts Fluent 2 tokens shared with rest of M365 — no bespoke AI palette, unlike OpenAI/Gemini.
take_what: Progressive disclosure as a layout principle — start minimal, surface controls only when the task needs them — for component docs/playgrounds.

name: ChatGPT Atlas (AI browser)
one_line: OpenAI's Chromium-based AI browser: minimal, ad-free chrome-alike shell with a chat-first sidebar as the primary surface.
design_notes: Clean, ad-free layout; ChatGPT history rail on left, 'Ask ChatGPT' sidebar on right; resizable vertical tabs; accent-color slider; cursor hover-state morphs into the ChatGPT logo. Reviewers: 'looks like Chrome' but feels app-not-browser.
take_what: Sidebar-as-first-class-surface: a contextual assistant panel that reflows content, relevant for an AI-assisted docs/playground panel.

name: ViralWait — 'Get 1000s of Signups Before You Launch'
one_line: A 2026 waitlist tool positioned squarely on virality math ('people bring 4-6 friends automatically'), with fraud protection called out as a headline feature.
design_notes: Bold large headline hero, light bg, green-check/red-X pain-point comparison table, three-step process visual, feature grid pairing 'Viral Mechanics' with 'Fraud Protection', pricing table, dual CTA.
take_what: Pair the growth feature with its safeguard in one tile (virality + fraud protection) — reads more credible.

name: 30 Best Tech Website Designs & Examples [2026]
one_line: 30-site roundup of top tech/dev-tool site design (Linear, Vercel, Stripe, Cursor, PlanetScale, Supabase, PostHog).
design_notes: Linear: precision type + motion showing speed. Vercel: animated build-log as hero demo. Stripe: gradient + docs-as-marketing. Cursor/PlanetScale: monospace on dark ('specificity over polish'). Supabase: green breaking category's blue sameness. PostHog: mascot + public roadmap.
take_what: Category pattern of showing real product UI as hero art, not illustration, and treating docs as a styled marketing surface — maps onto a component-library site.

name: TechCrunch — Beyond Instagram: next-gen social apps
one_line: TechCrunch roundup of next-gen social apps (Retro, Cosmos, Corner, Divine, Locket, Shelf) replacing algorithmic feeds with curation and private sharing.
design_notes: Plain press-style article, but its subject matter documents a cross-cutting trend: nearly every app profiled replaces algorithmic infinite feeds with curated formats — lists, widgets, weekly digests, taste 'shelves' — a shift from feed-scroll to curated-collection UI.
take_what: Structured curated-collection format (lists/shelves/weekly digest) as an alternative information architecture to an endless feed

name: TwelveLabs
one_line: Enterprise video-AI platform, Index Ventures' newest bet (July 1 2026), pairs emotive copy with modular SaaS cards.
design_notes: Bold declarative headlines ('See the unseen. Know the unknowable.'); high-contrast minimal palette with accent CTA color; vertically stacked modular sections (hero, feature cards, product showcase, testimonials); stat callouts (+13.1%, 10x faster) for social proof.
take_what: Emotive one-line headline paired with hard stat callouts makes an abstract AI capability feel concrete for enterprise buyers.

name: Touchmark
one_line: YC S26 'AI pricing' startup's pre-launch page is just a wordmark floating over an animated black wireframe gravity-well grid.
design_notes: Full-bleed animated WebGL grid warping like a spacetime gravity well, pure black bg, minimal centered wordmark with one italic-serif letter inside an otherwise plain sans logotype, 'SCROLL' + animated arrow, tiny YC badge — content-free teaser.
take_what: A single animated WebGL grid can be the whole pre-launch page; one serif-italic letter inside a sans wordmark is a cheap distinctive-logotype trick.

name: ZeroFS
one_line: Solo-built S3-filesystem tool ZeroFS (#2 on Show HN, July 2026, 116 pts/51 comments) skips AI-slop flourish for numbered, dense minimalism.
design_notes: Monochrome/near-neutral palette, no gradients or glassmorphism; large bold numbered section headers (01-06); terminal recordings and workflow diagrams instead of illustration; hero is one purpose statement plus an install command, no marketing flourish.
take_what: Proof a technical audience rewards information density and zero-ornament restraint over a polished 'AI-generated' hero.

name: Fourmula AI (design by Fourmeta Agency)
one_line: Generative platform for AI visual-asset presets; Awwwards Site of the Day May 2 2026, scored 7.41/10.
design_notes: Deep black (#020108) base, one vibrant orange accent (#FF6B02), Webflow + GSAP; 'dynamic hero' with seamless scroll-triggered transitions, animated loader, interactive footer — praised for animation choreography over static layout.
take_what: Near-monochrome plus one accent with GSAP scroll choreography is a lower-cost motion strategy than full 3D/WebGL, closer to typical eng budget.

name: Passionfroot
one_line: Creator-sponsorship AI SaaS rebranded as "The Agentic Marketing OS for the AI era," featured on Lapa Ninja.
design_notes: Charcoal/graphite bands alternating with white content cards, bold sans headline, dual CTA ("Start for free"/"Watch the trailer"), circular creator-avatar rows, dashboard-mockup screenshots, generous whitespace rhythm.
take_what: Alternate dark/light section bands down a long scroll instead of one flat page — keeps rhythm readable while still feeling premium.

name: GSAP Showcase
one_line: GSAP's own showcase of production sites built with the library — a direct index of current motion techniques.
design_notes: Features agency/production work like Noomo, Trionn, and Studio375's 'Ten Years Away' (SOTD June 26 2026) — heavy on scroll-triggered digital storytelling and full-bleed motion; mostly agency/portfolio sites, but techniques transfer directly to product marketing.
take_what: A living index of GSAP scroll-storytelling patterns (ScrollTrigger timelines) to turn into reusable Astryx motion recipes/tokens.

name: Minimalist Design Isn't Dead — It's Winning in 2026 (Medium)
one_line: Argues minimalism wins in 2026 on performance grounds (mobile speed, 1.5-second attention window, WCAG contrast), not just taste — cites Apple, Airbnb, Spotify.
design_notes: N/A, editorial piece. Prescribes 'one clean sans-serif + maybe a serif for contrast,' max three colors (neutrals + one accent); cites Inter/Helvetica/Work Sans as the default toolkit.
take_what: The practical/performance argument for restraint (load speed, accessibility, attention economics) to justify a text-first hero beyond taste alone.

name: Cradle
one_line: Dutch-Swiss protein-engineering AI (serving 6 of top-25 pharma) presents deep science through a scannable, modular SaaS-style site.
design_notes: Uppercase confident section headers ('PROTEIN ENGINEERING 2.0', 'WORK ON ANY PROTEIN'); modular protein-type cards (Antibodies, Enzymes, Vaccines, Peptides); embedded data-viz previews ('Round Progress' charts); customer case-study tiles.
take_what: Translating deep-tech complexity into consumer-SaaS-legible card modules rather than dense academic prose makes a hard domain approachable.

name: Koto
one_line: London/Berlin branding studio behind 2025–26's highest-profile rebrands (Amazon, GoFundMe, Stack Overflow) sets the template others imitate.
design_notes: Case studies emphasize flexible brand systems scaling across product, web, and marketing simultaneously rather than a static logo-first deliverable; 'living' brand-idea framing (e.g. Stack Overflow reframed as a 'truth engine').
take_what: Pitching identity as a flexible cross-surface system with one throughline idea, not a logo-and-colors package.

name: Kling AI
one_line: Kuaishou's AI video generator, #1 ELO video-model benchmark (Feb 2026), 100M+ global users across 224 countries — product UI reviewed as deliberately unfussy.
design_notes: Reviewers describe a minimal dashboard with no menu clutter, a single centered prompt box, and intuitive generation controls — the marketing/product surface collapses into the tool itself rather than a separate pitch page.
take_what: The "drop straight into the tool" pattern — minimal chrome, one centered input — for a product whose output (generated media) is the best marketing.

name: What we can learn from this new Stripe landing page (Charli Marie)
one_line: Design-critique breakdown of a Stripe Sessions landing page: code-driven organic wave hero, Apple-style container blocks, negative-space CTA.
design_notes: Hero = code-generated organic gradient wave interacting with the typography. Dense info via expanding/collapsing carousel "container blocks" (Apple-popularized) so photo cards anchor while text scrolls beside them. CTA relies on negative space, not size/color.
take_what: Container-block carousels show dense content (case studies, integrations) without a wall of cards; a CTA read via whitespace, not brightness, keeps hero calm.

name: Rork
one_line: 'Vibecode a mobile app, ship to App Store' launch video pulled 8.1M X views — more than OpenAI's or Manus AI's clips in the same ranking.
design_notes: Mobile-first single-column layout, hero 'Be the next app founder,' central chat-style input for app descriptions with drag-drop upload. Quick-action suggestion chips ('Create a Multiplayer Game'). Light mode, emoji accents, embedded game-demo videos.
take_what: Quick-action suggestion chips beneath a prompt-box hero lower the blank-page problem for a generative tool.

name: Jeton (rebrand by Büro)
one_line: Payments app's 2026 rebrand by studio Büro built on a burnt-orange 3D coin-motif brand universe, cited as a standout fintech design case study.
design_notes: Deep burnt-orange dominates typography/backgrounds, offset by subdued pastel 3D renders; soft-geometric wordmark; coin-motion brand symbol; two parallel 3D asset tracks (abstract headers + real-use-case store scenes) unify web and app.
take_what: A saturated brand-color-as-material plus a recurring 3D object-metaphor gives a financial product warmth vs. generic blue/navy fintech palettes.

name: AIOS Medical
one_line: HF0-incubated 'full-stack AI Doctor' pitched a $350M ARR target at HF0's June 2026 demo day; went viral via Robert Scoble's coverage.
design_notes: Page reads sparse/centered, company name repeated for emphasis, one bold claim ('world's first full-stack AI doctor'). Could not confirm deeper color/type/motion via fetch — looks like a pre-launch minimal landing page, not a built-out site yet.
take_what: The 'confidence over content' pattern: one audacious claim, almost no supporting page, generating buzz before the product visibly ships.

name: Silurian AI
one_line: AI Grant-backed startup building foundation models to simulate Earth's weather at planetary scale; roughly $11M raised.
design_notes: Near-black dark mode (#0B0B0B-#1C1C1C) with earth-toned accents, not tech-blue: deep teal #325251, terracotta #D3884F, alert red #BF0F1A. H1 'Tailored Earth Intelligence' uses two-tone heading class (primary + muted secondary word), uppercase subhead below.
take_what: Dark mode with earth/terracotta accent instead of default tech-blue; two-tone (primary/muted-word) treatment within one headline.

name: Humalike (humalike.ai)
one_line: YC-style 'behavioral infrastructure for humanlike AI agents' API startup; PH launch pitching social intelligence for agents.
design_notes: Alternates full dark sections (white logo/text) with full light sections (black logo/text) for scroll rhythm; bold uppercase headline; rounded-corner API/use-case cards; star-rating trust badges; deliberately static, no motion.
take_what: Section-by-section dark/light inversion as a pacing device for the whole page, giving scroll rhythm without a motion budget.

name: minimal.gallery
one_line: Hand-picked minimal-site gallery run by Piet Terheyden since 2013; Startup/SAAS/AI tags, weekly digest, June 2026 adds include Ponder AI, Beacon, Monolog.
design_notes: Aggregator, not a single design — but its own UI models the trend it curates: dense thumbnail grid, tag-filterable, minimal chrome, mono/mono-grotesk labels typical of dev-tool directories.
take_what: Standing scouting source — check weekly for freshly-tagged Startup/SAAS/AI entries before each design refresh instead of relying on memory.

name: Brutalist AI SaaS Landing Page (v0 template)
axis: Brutalist dark UI template for AI SaaS
one_line: Vercel v0 marketplace template productizing the 2026 'brutalist AI SaaS' look as an engineering-grade dark UI kit — the trend turned reusable starting point.
design_notes: Dark, high-contrast 'engineering-grade' UI kit per its own framing: hard borders, monospace/system type, exposed-structure component styling, zero glassy polish.
take_what: Signals brutalist/dark-engineering is now templatized for AI dev-tool positioning — a 'technical credibility' theme variant Astryx docs could offer.

name: Wikipedia — 'Your AI Slop Bores Me'
one_line: Documents the viral 'Insane AI Slop' callout movement spreading across X, Bluesky and Tumblr mocking generic AI-generated content and aesthetics.
design_notes: Not a single visual style — a naming/callout movement. Establishes that visibly generic/AI-generated aesthetics are now actively mocked and screenshotted publicly, not just critiqued in design blogs.
take_what: Signals real reputational risk in shipping a visibly 'AI slop' marketing site — an active public callout culture exists right now.

name: Neubrutalism.com — definitive neubrutalist web design reference
one_line: Reference site cataloguing neubrutalism — thick black borders, flat primary colors, offset shadows — as the reaction to templated SaaS sameness.
design_notes: Cites Gumroad's 2021 rebrand as the definitive case, Panda CSS and Dodonut as current adopters, neobrutalism.dev (shadcn/ui-based kit, 5000+ stars) as reference implementation — but notes Figma itself dropped the look in its 2024 rebrand.
take_what: A bounded neubrutalist theme (hard borders, offset shadows, flat color) reads as intentional rejection of the AI-gradient look critics call out.

name: Periodic Labs — periodic.com
one_line: Ex-OpenAI/DeepMind AI-for-materials-science startup ($300M raise) pitches with the tagline 'From bits to atoms' on a stripped editorial layout.
design_notes: Short micro-headers drive a scannable, left-aligned editorial layout; dual 'Bits'/'Atoms' career tracks pun on the tagline; advisory-board roster with institutional credentials replaces a logo wall as trust signal; grant program as secondary mid-page CTA.
take_what: One punchy positioning line doing the work of a hero, paired with credential-based trust signals — copy-led differentiation over visual spectacle.

name: Commercial Type (Druk / Graphik)
one_line: Barnes & Schwartz foundry behind Druk (brutalist condensed display, ex-Bloomberg Businessweek) and Graphik — cited as 2026 industrial-display staples.
design_notes: Druk deliberately skips normal widths/light weights, starting at Medium going to Super — built for 'heavy, unapologetic' brutalist headlines, a named 2026 trend alongside National Park, PP Neue Machina.
take_what: An intentionally extreme, weight-limited display cut reserved strictly for hero headlines/big numbers, never body text.

name: Framer startup gallery
one_line: Framer's own curated gallery of startup sites built on the platform, its proof design-led teams ship fast without a front-end crew.
design_notes: Category-filtered showcase; Framer positions itself in 2026 as design-first (closer to Figma than a classic site builder), now bundling CMS/hosting/SEO/localization/AI setup.
take_what: Living reference set of current Framer-built startup sites — pull layout/motion patterns when benchmarking against no-code competitors.

name: Bakken & Bæck
one_line: Pan-EU product-design studio (Oslo, Bonn, Amsterdam, London, Barcelona) shaping startup visual language from Sierra to climate-tech Carbo Culture.
design_notes: Studio's own site cited as a hand-picked gallery exemplar of clean, minimal creative-agency design; pairs climate/nature-driven concepts (e.g. Carbo Culture identity) with rigorous product-design craft over pure decoration.
take_what: One European studio whose client roster is a live index of what's about to trend next in startup identity, worth monitoring beyond its homepage.

design_notes: By Ashraf Omran; auto-fills a container with tiled shapes that each respond to the pointer (rotate, scale, fade, shift), smooth reset on cursor-leave. Marketed for 'modern hero sections, product backdrops, playful UI surfaces.'
name: Framer Marketplace — 'Magnetic Pattern' component
one_line: Premium Framer component: a pointer-reactive tiled-shape field that rotates/scales/fades toward the cursor, resets on leave.
take_what: Packaged pattern for a cursor-reactive hero backdrop (tiled shapes, subtle rotate/scale/fade) short of a full custom cursor.

name: Fika Jobs
one_line: Stockholm video-first hiring platform, $4M pre-seed (June 2026 TechCrunch), pitched as 'LinkedIn crossed with TikTok'.
design_notes: Bold headline broken across lines ('Standout. / From the crowd.'), repeated CTA at multiple scroll depths, simulated chat/interview dialogue snippets previewing the AI agent, scannable profile cards mimicking a feed, simplified top nav.
take_what: Simulated chat-bubble UI snippets let a site borrow the 'feed' feel without real video — signals video-native product cheaply.

name: OpenAI's bold rebrand critique
one_line: Creative Bloq design critique: OpenAI 'finally fixes its logo,' calling the rebrand surprisingly warm/human for an AI lab.
design_notes: Frames the shift from sterile/generic tech-startup branding to a warmer, imperfect-geometry system as the notable move — circles with deliberately uneven interiors, softened grid, human photography mixed with AI-generated texture.
take_what: 'Intentional imperfection' as a 2026 counter to sterile geometric minimalism — a differentiator for an otherwise clinical component-library site.

name: "Make It Like Stripe," or Why Imitation Is a Tricky Design Strategy (Eleken)
one_line: Argues that cloning Stripe's gradients/visuals without the underlying user research and craft obsession is why "Stripe clones" usually fall flat.
design_notes: Contends Stripe's site "looks amazing because it is amazing" — the differentiator is deep user knowledge and sweating every detail, not the gradient CSS itself; warns against surface-level imitation as a design strategy.
take_what: Caution against copying Stripe-style gradients/bento grids as pure decoration — any borrowed pattern needs a real IA reason, not just visual mimicry.

name: Trase
one_line: Agentic-AI OS for regulated back offices raised $107M seed (Jun 2026) led by ARCH Venture Partners.
design_notes: White base with navy/blue accents, dark-inverted footer; bold hero 'Elite AI Performance. Powered By Trase'; alternating text/image blocks; blunt stat callout ('99.8% Admin work reduction'); marketplace-grid of AI-agent cards; 4-step deployment timeline; logo carousel.
take_what: Marketplace-grid pattern for many discrete AI-agent/feature 'products' as browsable cards, plus one hard metric as the whole value prop.

name: Runtime (YC P26)
one_line: YC-backed sandboxed runtime for deploying coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) across a whole team, with governance and audit logs.
design_notes: Dark background, vibrant teal/cyan accent on CTAs and logo; large bold centered hero headline over lighter body copy; modular vertically-stacked sections with generous whitespace; product screenshots and horizontal rows of integration logos (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex).
take_what: Dark-mode-with-single-accent restraint (teal-on-black) instead of multi-gradient noise, plus the logo-row 'works with X' trust pattern for integrations.

name: Expanse (YC P26)
one_line: YC-backed intelligence layer that predicts GPU/HPC cluster resource fit and failure risk at submission time to unlock idle capacity.
design_notes: Stark white/gray palette, sans-serif hierarchy, near-zero color accents — relies on typography weight and whitespace over decoration; hero pairs the pitch with a literal cluster-utilization visualization (12/32 GPUs at 37%); five-step onboarding flow, deliberately un-flashy.
take_what: A counter to gradient/motion-heavy AI marketing — restraint (data visualization over decoration) reads more credible for a technical-buyer audience.

name: The Launch Video Company
one_line: An agency producing founder-facing launch videos (Airtable 8.1M views, Brad Menezes 4.5M) distributed natively on X; now the default launch playbook.
design_notes: Not a visual artifact; documents the current template of founder-to-camera video plus coordinated launch-day post replacing the old blog-post/press-release relaunch.
take_what: Pair any major site/product relaunch with a short founder-narrated native video post; it drives outsized reach versus the page alone.

name: Clico
one_line: AI-everywhere-you-type Chrome extension; nominee for flat-illustration, storytelling UI with GSAP microinteractions.
design_notes: Flat design + illustration, Tailwind CSS, GSAP microinteractions across homepage/about/footer, form and header transitions. Community scores 6.4-8.0.
take_what: Flat illustration + Tailwind-speed microinteractions is a lighter alternative to WebGL for a component-library site.

name: "The Y3K Aesthetic" (Envato Elements)
one_line: Defines Y3K hyperfuturism — glossy black/silver/neon palettes, holographic 3D blobs, alien-sleek type — Y2K nostalgia escalated into 2026 AI-brand visuals.
design_notes: Characterizes the look as 'hovering UI panels, holographic product renders, environments that look half-digital half-organic' — chrome textures and impossible holographic effects increasingly generated via AI tooling itself.
take_what: A more maximalist neon-on-black alternative to flat dark minimalism — useful if Astryx wants a bolder gradient/chrome accent system.

name: Superhuman
one_line: 2026 roundups (framerbite, Framer-gallery coverage) call Superhuman 'the benchmark for SaaS startups,' citing dark-mode minimalism.
design_notes: CONFLICT FLAGGED: secondary sources describe dark-mode, minimalist type, scroll micro-interactions. A direct fetch of the live site (July 2026) showed light, white-background, product-block layout with 'Trusted by' logos — treat 'dark-mode' as reputation/lag, unconfirmed.
take_what: The 'SaaS benchmark' citation is itself a buzz signal, but re-verify visual specifics before copying — don't trust secondary claims blind.

name: Creative Boom — "15 Typefaces Designers Love to Use in 2026"
one_line: Curated 2026 roundup: workhorses (Inter, Roboto, Helvetica) to foundry darlings (Druk, Degular, Bricolage Grotesque, Aeonik), with named brand users.
design_notes: Names real adopters per face: Druk→Bloomberg Businessweek, Aeonik→Revolut/Eurosport/Virgin Hyperloop, Inter→Google Maps/YouTube, Avenir→Disney+/Bloomberg/Snapchat — grounding trend claims in shipped brands.
take_what: Cross-reference which typeface a brand is 'known for' before adopting it, to avoid an inadvertently generic pick.

name: Podium
one_line: Sports creative-production studio site (not a funded tech startup) — Awwwards Three.js Site of the Day June 27 2026.
design_notes: Minimalist black/white canvas; a '0% Available worldwide' progressive counter gates scroll-reveal content; alternating full-width media/centered blocks put all visual weight on embedded 3D/video against a bare shell.
take_what: Progressive-reveal percentage counter as a scroll-gated loading device; bare monochrome shell puts 100% of visual budget into motion.

name: Nordiska Museet
one_line: Sweden's largest cultural-history museum site — 2025 Webby + Lovie + two Swedish Design Awards + Muse Award winner.
design_notes: Uses the museum's own seal/emblem as a recurring 'dynamic framing device' across pages; scroll-responsive text animations; color palette reassigned per exhibition rather than one fixed brand color.
take_what: A single graphic mark reused as a structural framing/masking device across the site gives continuity without a huge asset library.

name: Awwwards Mobile Excellence collection
one_line: Curated Awwwards+Google badge collection of sites scoring 75+/100 on dedicated mobile-UX guidelines, independent of the desktop-centric Site of the Day award.
design_notes: Not a single design but a judged index — mobile-first quality is now scored on its own axis apart from desktop 'wow' sites; winners like Jeton are praised for touch-friendly scroll flows over decorative desktop-only motion.
take_what: Use as a sourcing list: every entry is a pre-vetted mobile-first exemplar worth a follow-up deep-crawl pass.

name: Ark UI
one_line: Headless, framework-agnostic primitives sold almost entirely via cross-framework code parity, not decoration.
design_notes: Deliberately minimal, no decorative styling or heavy animation. Hero: 'Unstyled UI components for your Design System.' Centerpiece: tabbed code panel, identical Slider implementation across React/Solid/Vue/Svelte tabs. Adopter-logo showcase, team-avatar community section.
take_what: Restraint-as-differentiation: one cross-implementation code comparison does the persuading instead of visual flourish.

name: Clamp Generator
one_line: All-in-one CSS clamp() generator for font-size, layout, width/height, padding/margin/gap with an icon tool picker and viewport-vs-value graphs.
design_notes: Hero with embedded product video; six SVG-icon tool cards (font size, layout, width/height, padding/margin, gap, custom) as primary nav; viewport-vs-property graphs visualize the interpolation curve; monospace clamp() output; Product Hunt badge; darker footer.
take_what: Icon-card tool picker as IA for a suite of utilities, plus a viewport-vs-value graph that makes an abstract formula visually verifiable.

name: LaunchList — Dropbox-style viral waitlist referral guide
one_line: The fullest 2026 design spec for the loop: referral link, visible position counter, public-vs-private leaderboard, milestone rewards scaled 5-10x.
design_notes: Prescribes concrete UI rules: position shown at 4 touchpoints (confirmation screen/email, update emails, 'moved up' notices); public leaderboards only for competitive audiences (devs, traders); typical K=0.2-0.6, K>1 exceptional (Dropbox/Robinhood).
take_what: Multi-touchpoint position display plus explicit tier-reward ratio as a spec for a queue/progress component.

name: Landing.Gallery — Pricing Page inspiration
one_line: 133+ pricing-page screenshots collected as a browsable inspiration board inside a broader landing-page archive.
design_notes: Screenshot-grid gallery, no annotation beyond company name; sits inside a larger landing-page inspiration site so pricing sections get cross-referenced against hero/nav patterns from the same sites.
take_what: Cheap way to sample current pricing-card visual conventions (spacing, badge placement) across dozens of sites at once.

name: Monaco
one_line: AI-native sales/CRM ($50M Series B led by Benchmark) runs a stark black-on-white site anchored by name-brand testimonials.
design_notes: Monochrome black-on-white palette, clean sans-serif, no ornamental type; hero background video behind headline 'The first revenue engine for startups'; three-column feature cards; testimonials from Garry Tan and Peter Thiel as primary social proof, not logos.
take_what: Named-individual quotes, not just company logos, as the dominant trust signal: sharper than a generic client-logo wall.

name: Twinr (twinr.dev)
one_line: No-code website-to-mobile-app builder; won #1 Product of the Day twice back-to-back on PH, 1,000+ signups on launch day.
design_notes: Off-white bg, charcoal text, teal/blue CTAs, asymmetrical hero with phone mockup right, organic SVG curved dividers between sections, alternating content/image blocks, numbered Day1-7 launch timeline, checkmark benefit lists, client-logo carousel.
take_what: Numbered horizontal timeline component (Day 1 to 7) to visualize a multi-step process, an alternative to a generic feature grid.

name: Krea AI
one_line: Krea's March 2026 interface overhaul turned the live generation canvas into the homepage itself, making real-time AI feel tactile.
design_notes: Unified navigation, transparent model picker, drag-and-drop workflows, customizable workspace, rebuilt mobile; the interactive canvas IS the hero, not a screenshot or video of it.
take_what: Let the live, touchable product surface double as the marketing hero instead of a rendered screenshot or video.

name: CyberCrest Compliance
one_line: Cybersecurity/compliance rebrand by studio Foursets; nominee for 3D+Lottie-driven services storytelling.
design_notes: Custom 3D built in Blender, GSAP interactions, Lottie animations, black footer, services-section storytelling. Webflow build. Community scores 6.0-9.9.
take_what: Lottie for lightweight motion (vs full WebGL) on a services page — a cheaper motion tier Astryx could document.

name: Metabrand — "30 Best Startup Websites in 2026"
one_line: 30-site curated gallery covering current default-good startup homepage patterns (Linear, Anthropic, Supabase, Vercel, etc).
design_notes: Callouts: Linear (speed/precision type), Anthropic (serif wordmark, restraint), Supabase (bold green vs. category blue/gray), Vercel (animated build-log hero). Skews to familiar leaders, not fresh finds — a baseline resource, not a novelty signal.
take_what: Fast baseline comparison — if Astryx doesn't clear what these 30 do by default (product-in-hero, transparent pricing), it's behind category norms.

name: Top Trend in AI Landing Page Design (Lapa Ninja)
one_line: Lapa Ninja roundup of current AI-product landing pages (Spellbook, expand.ai, Poolside, Anterior, Amplemarket) and their shared patterns.
design_notes: Minimalist layouts with heavy whitespace, bold large type paired with vivid product imagery, dominant black/violet dark palettes (Spellbook), collapsible sections for dense feature info, playful motion on some entries.
take_what: Black+violet dark palette recurs across funded AI tools — a low-risk, currently-fashionable dark-mode accent pair worth testing in a theme preset.

name: Photoroom
one_line: A rare profitable consumer GenAI startup (Paris), $500M valuation, with a clean product-forward site that lets generated imagery carry the design.
design_notes: Neutral white/dark-text foundation, minimal accent color so product imagery dominates; headline 'Sell at first sight'; modular 2–3 column feature cards with real lifestyle/product screenshots; customer logo carousel under hero.
take_what: Letting actual generated product output, not illustration, be the hero visual — the AI output itself is the marketing asset.

name: Sakana AI
one_line: Tokyo frontier-AI lab (multi-round VC backed, 'school of fish' swarm-intelligence brand) with a clean, professional, product-suite marketing site.
design_notes: Minimal white-ground layout, hierarchical dropdown nav (Research/Solution/Product/Careers), red fish-swarm logo mark as sole color accent, SVG-driven product icons for Chat/Marlin/Fugu — restraint over spectacle.
take_what: Single strong brand-color accent (red) against near-monochrome UI to keep a component-heavy nav legible without competing with content.

name: Sakazuki
one_line: Suntory-backed private membership platform for Japanese craft/culture experiences; won Awwwards Typography Honors (May 2026) and Site of the Day (Jun 14 2026).
design_notes: Two-color palette, condensed/tight-tracked oversized headline ("UnlockingJapan'sHiddenGems"), abundant whitespace, sparse imagery, extensive scrollable member roster for social proof, OpenSea link signaling web3/collectible tie-in.
take_what: Condensed run-together headline type as a single graphic mark, plus a scrollable name/logo roster as a lightweight trust signal.

name: Krutrim Cloud (Ola)
one_line: Ola's Krutrim pivoted from LLMs/chips to an "AI-first, data-stays-in-India" cloud platform in 2026; India's first AI unicorn, now profitable.
design_notes: Dark-background, high-contrast monochrome with a repeated Indian-flag-emoji motif reinforcing 'data stays in India,' bold hero headline plus a live dashboard-preview screenshot, client-logo carousel, ISO/SOC badges, testimonials with headshots.
take_what: A single repeated motif as a lightweight trust signal, and leading the hero with a real product-dashboard screenshot rather than abstract art.

design_notes: Copy-paste GSAP-only component: per-element magnetic radius via data attributes, separate inner-content parallax for depth, auto-disables on touch. £5 single-project / £49 unlimited — cursor magnetism now a packaged commercial primitive.
name: GSAP Vault — Magnetic Cursor Effect
one_line: Commercial GSAP snippet: elements attract/repel from the cursor with elastic physics — marketed as a premium web-design hallmark.
take_what: Validates packaging magnetic-hover as a reusable Button/Link modifier (elastic attract, auto-disable on touch) vs. one-off builds.

name: Easings.co
one_line: Cubic-bezier easing generator/showcase pairing a live curve editor with real UI demo galleries, built by SuperHi/Works studio.
design_notes: Interactive Bezier curve selector (easeInOut/easeIn/easeOut) with duration/offset/play scrubbing and copy-to-clipboard snippets; same easing curve reused across concrete UI contexts (carousel, transit directions) instead of an isolated graph, with named studio/renderer credit.
take_what: Reusing one motion primitive across several concrete UI contexts, not just an abstract graph, sells the felt quality of the curve, not just its math.

name: AI browser comparison 2026: Atlas, Comet, Dia and 5 more
one_line: Syndicated ranking of 8 AI browsers: Arc still 'wins on UI design' while Comet wins on agentic automation — polish and agentic power haven't converged.
design_notes: Ranking explicitly separates visual-design quality (Arc), agentic capability (Comet), and privacy (Brave) as three still-distinct axes reviewers judge these browsers on, rather than one browser sweeping all three.
take_what: Caution: bolting on AI affordances shouldn't erode visual polish — the two are still judged, and won, separately by this category's leaders.

name: Mach Industries
one_line: Defense hardware startup; $300M Series C at $1.8B valuation, announced June 1 2026 (TechCrunch).
design_notes: Dark bg, high-contrast technical type; numbered sections (01-06) for each product line (Viper, Glide, Stratos, Pike, Dart, Energetics); modular product cards with real test-footage video thumbnails; subtle SVG grid-pattern accents and directional arrows between sections.
take_what: Numbered-section product taxonomy (01-06) as wayfinding across a long multi-product page — pattern for a component index.

name: Mati Carbon
one_line: Enhanced-rock-weathering startup won the $50M XPRIZE Carbon Removal grand prize (2026), largest prize in XPRIZE history.
design_notes: Mission-first structure built on farmer testimonials from India, Tanzania, Zambia rather than product screenshots; four-part process explainer; impact-metrics section; dense partner-logo wall (Shopify, Stripe, H&M as credit buyers); vertical narrative flow.
take_what: Testimonial-led, human-first storytelling as an alternative hero pattern when the story is outcomes/impact, not a UI to preview.

name: Gumloop
one_line: No-code AI-agent platform (Benchmark-led Series B) uses dark charcoal sections with animated gradient dividers.
design_notes: Dark charcoal/navy backgrounds with purple-blue-teal gradient overlays used as animated section dividers; large sans-serif headline ('AI agents built for by your team'); live Slack-chat mockup embedded in page; customer avatar clusters plus real-time usage charts.
take_what: Gradient-as-divider: an animated color gradient strip instead of a hard line to transition between dark sections, keeps energy without extra chrome.

name: XDOF
one_line: Robotics-data infra startup, $70M stealth launch led by Thrive, runs a stark white/navy site led by real robot-task video.
design_notes: White background, dark navy/charcoal text, minimal color accents; bold uppercase headline ('Educating the world's general purpose robots'); code-styled tagline 'xdof.build()'; carousel of 25+ real robot-task demo clips, each version-labeled (v2.1.0); investor-logo footer.
take_what: Version-labeled real capability footage (v2.1.0-style demo carousel) as literal proof-of-progress, better than a generic feature grid.

name: Silmaril
one_line: YC W26 AI-agent security startup ('runtime security for AI that self-improves') named a Demo Day VC standout, guarding agents against prompt injection.
design_notes: Dark navy/black background, white/gray sans type, numbered (01/02/03) feature breakdown, interactive threat-detection demo with filterable execution traces, bar-chart performance comparisons, compliance-badge footer.
take_what: Numbered section scaffolding (01/02/03) walks a technical buyer through a multi-step product story without feeling like a plain feature list.

name: GUILD
one_line: YC S26 'AI-Native Defense Prime' startup pairs a black bg with a violet-orange particle-explosion graphic and slab-serif display type.
design_notes: Pure black bg, bold slab-serif/grotesk hybrid H1 ('Building the AI-Native Defense Prime.'), abstract violet-to-magenta smoke/particle graphic bleeding into the hero, orange accent (target-ring logomark, glowing CTA, tracked-out eyebrow label), YC badge.
take_what: Confirms a small S26 cluster: defense-tech sites on black bg + one hot accent + particle hero art + slab-serif type — worth naming as a sub-genre.

name: Clico (tryclico.com)
one_line: Clico (AI-everywhere-you-type Chrome extension) pairs serif display headings with sans body copy on a light, whitespace-heavy layout.
design_notes: Serif headline type over sans-serif body — a font-pairing break from the all-grotesk SaaS default; logo carousel of compatible platforms, testimonial cards, accordion FAQ; keyboard-shortcut (⌘+O) glyph used as a UI-literacy trust signal.
take_what: Serif-headline/sans-body pairing reads less generic-SaaS; the inline keyboard-shortcut glyph is a credibility device docs pages could reuse.

name: Formless.xyz
one_line: Formless.xyz uses generative, cursor-responsive background color and 3D scroll/hover depth, at the cost of a reported 35% performance score.
design_notes: Explosive/generative background color reacting to cursor movement; 3D scroll and hover effects create spatial depth; numbered section markers (01, 02...); minimal text, desktop-first; flagged in source as a performance cautionary tale (heavy interaction load).
take_what: Cautionary, not to copy: cursor-reactive backgrounds read trendy but tank perf — argues for CSS-native motion (StyleX transitions) over WebGL/canvas.

name: Pencil.dev
axis: vintage art motif meets dev-tool UI
one_line: Agent-driven design-canvas tool; Webflow's trend report singles it out for ASCII art of classical figures on the homepage.
design_notes: Per Webflow's characterization: homepage pairs retro ASCII-art of classical figures with a technical dev-tool story ('Design on canvas. Land in code.'). Could not independently confirm visually via text-only fetch — sourced from Webflow's writeup, not directly observed.
take_what: Contrasting a nostalgic/analog motif (ASCII, hand-drawn) against a technical dev-tool product adds warmth without illustration overhead.

name: Web Design Trends 2026: What B2B Sites Must Get Right
one_line: Agency brief on 2026 B2B must-haves: bento layouts, GSAP scroll motion, AI-personalized blocks, WCAG 2.2 AA/AAA, dark-mode toggle as standard.
design_notes: Bento boxes explicitly framed via the Japanese-bento metaphor for compartmentalized B2B content. GSAP scroll narratives called the standard motion tool. Dark-mode toggle now baseline, not novelty.
take_what: Treat dark-mode toggle and WCAG 2.2 AA/AAA as non-negotiable baseline, not stretch goals, for any B2B-facing docs/marketing surface.

name: Are.na
one_line: Cult-favorite visual-research/curation platform whose pages stay deliberately dense and unpolished rather than whitespace-padded.
design_notes: Information-dense grid layout, numbered lists, extensive but plainly categorized nav (Editorial/Extended/Info), minimal ornamentation, trusts users to scan rather than hand-holding with big hero art.
take_what: A docs/resources index that favors dense, well-labeled lists over card grids with generous padding — higher information scent per screen.

name: Nottingham Contemporary
one_line: Deliberately retro brutalist museum site with an analogue clock and a rotating support-button microinteraction.
design_notes: Consciously subverts polish: raw brutalist layout, an analogue clock widget rendered in-browser, a donate button that physically rotates on interaction — plain aesthetic as identity choice, not budget constraint.
take_what: Proof 'undesigned'/brutalist can be a confident identity choice — a counter-note against defaulting to polished gradients/glassmorphism.

name: LayerX
one_line: Tokyo fintech/AI-SaaS unicorn-track startup ($192M raised, 15k+ customers) with a poetic bilingual corporate site.
design_notes: Generous letter-spaced large Japanese copy ("未来の希望を") paired with English translation, strict black/white/grayscale palette, scroll-triggered section reveals, masonry employee-photo grid for culture, card-grid business-unit layout.
take_what: Bilingual headline pairing (large native-language line + smaller translation) as a hero pattern; masonry photo grids instead of stock "who we are" imagery.

name: Cal AI
one_line: Teen-founded calorie-tracking app that went viral on TikTok/Reels via a 150-influencer engine, acquired by MyFitnessPal in 2026.
design_notes: Dark-gradient bg with vibrant accents, two-column hero (headline + copy left, phone mockup with live scanner UI right), download CTAs repeated in header/hero/footer, testimonial carousel with influencer photos and stat badges ('5M users', 'lost 17 lbs').
take_what: A phone mockup showing the live camera/scan UI (not a static icon) doubles as the product-demo video substitute in a plain two-column hero.

name: IBM Carbon Design System — Homepage
one_line: Carbon runs its type hierarchy on IBM's own Plex typeface, split into "productive" (condensed) vs "expressive" type sets, and is mid-redesign as of 2026.
design_notes: IBM Plex Light/Regular/SemiBold across two calibrated type sets: productive for dense docs tables, expressive for marketing prose; grid-based enterprise docs IA; team shipping a homepage redesign (preview build live on Vercel, 2026) alongside stable prod docs.
take_what: Productive-vs-expressive type-set split: condensed scale for dense docs tables, looser scale for marketing prose.

name: Cursor for Designers (cursor.com/for/designers)
one_line: Cursor's own designer-facing landing page pitching its browser "Design Mode" — point/draw/talk-to-agent visual editing with a live style sidebar.
design_notes: Sidebar exposes sliders, color palettes, and design-token controls for live-editing a rendered site; positions itself as unifying design and code rather than a separate Figma-to-code handoff step.
take_what: A token-driven live-editing sidebar (sliders/palettes tied to real tokens) is a strong pattern for an Astryx theming demo — tweak-and-see-it-update.

name: Dia Browser — Landing Page Design (Lapa Ninja showcase)
one_line: Curated landing-page gallery entry for diabrowser.com — an AI browser's marketing site circulating as a design reference in its own right.
design_notes: Entry in Lapa Ninja's landing-page showcase, confirming Dia's marketing site (not just its app UI) is cited by design-gallery curators — evidence this wave now produces marketing-site exemplars, not just product-UI ones.
take_what: Signal to deep-crawl diabrowser.com directly for hero/typography specifics — its site is treated as a design reference apart from the product.

name: Prefinery — 'Build a Viral Waitlist That Grows Itself'
one_line: Enterprise waitlist/referral platform whose hero pitches built-in virality, backed by a white-label customer screenshot showing live referral-rank UI.
design_notes: Minimal navy/charcoal wordmark, high-contrast sans-serif, fixed nav, full-width hero, alternating text/image blocks, testimonial carousel. Screenshots show a client's (Woodpecker) referral-rewards panel visualizing queue advancement per referral.
take_what: White-label proof: show a real customer's branded instance of the referral-progress UI as social proof.

name: Seltz
one_line: AI search engine built for agents/chatbots (not humans) — $12.5M seed led by Speedinvest + B Capital, announced June 24 2026.
design_notes: Enterprise SaaS structure: hero, feature blocks, testimonials, FAQ; dual CTAs 'Try The API' / 'Talk To Us'; copy emphasizes speed/scale/security — clean, technical positioning, not experimental visuals (per live fetch).
take_what: Dual-CTA hero (self-serve API trial + sales-assist) mirrors what a dev-facing design-system site could offer: docs path vs. contact-sales path.

name: Queue
one_line: Fully autonomous robotic pharmacy kiosk; $12.6M seed led by AlleyCorp, emerged from stealth June 30 2026 (total $18.6M raised).
design_notes: Black-and-white minimal palette (separate logo lockups for light/dark); bold hero type 'A new way to pharmacy' over studio product photography; live metric strip (pills/min, meds supported, cost cut %) plus a press-logo trust grid.
take_what: Metric strip directly under the hero (three bold numerals) is a fast trust-building pattern for adoption stats like components shipped or bundle size.

name: Enter (getenter.ai)
one_line: Brazilian legal-AI startup, tripled to $1.2B valuation on Founders Fund round, uses a data-driven white/navy/teal site.
design_notes: White/off-white background, dark navy text, teal accent CTAs; grayscale testimonial photography; alternating two-column text/image blocks; case-study callouts with hard metrics (+6 p.p. win rate); minimalist numbered-icon process diagram.
take_what: Metric-forward case-study callouts (hard percentage-point numbers inline in the page flow) as proof for an enterprise buyer.

name: Paul Graham argues investors focusing on HF0 demo days
one_line: 2026 commentary on investor attention shifting to small curated residencies like HF0 vs. mega-batch accelerators — a live positioning debate.
design_notes: N/A — aggregator news/opinion post.
take_what: The 'small and curated beats big and broad' narrative — relevant framing for a boutique design system versus sprawling competitors.

name: RetroUI — 12 Neobrutalist Websites You Should Know in 2026
one_line: A curated 2026 round-up of neobrutalist product sites, evidence that Gumroad's redesign is part of a wider movement, not a one-off stunt.
design_notes: Round-up pairs named sites with screenshots showing the recurring neobrutalist toolkit: thick borders, flat saturated fills, hard drop-shadows, oversized blocky type.
take_what: Confirms neobrutalism as a legible counter-current worth tracking — an explicit 'don't drift here' marker for a refined-minimal design system.

name: Lapa Ninja — SaaS category
one_line: 691 B2B SaaS landing pages (7,300+ sitewide) filterable by brand color and layout style.
design_notes: Filter-driven browsing by color/style/business-type gives a fast read on the dominant palette and layout cluster for SaaS sites this quarter.
take_what: Filtering by color/style fast-tracks spotting the currently dominant palette cluster before designing a hero.

name: MaxiBestOf — Best Editorial Websites
one_line: A standing curated gallery category dedicated to 'editorial' website design on the inspiration site MaxiBestOf.
design_notes: Design-inspiration gallery with 'Editorial' as a first-class style filter/category alongside typography and industry filters — signals print/editorial style is an established taxonomy bucket, not a one-off niche.
take_what: A rolling reference feed — filtering by 'editorial' surfaces fresh light/serif/print sites continuously, cheaper than a one-time trend report.

name: Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art
one_line: UK contemporary-art museum site with a typographically-driven loading animation and bold brutalist exhibition pages.
design_notes: Typography-first loading sequence, bold uncompromising type scale, scroll-based exhibition-page animations, open/closed status indicator pinned top-left as a small confident UI flourish.
take_what: A typographic loading animation (not spinner/logo) as first-impression branding; a persistent small status chip is a transferable pattern.

design_notes: Circle-shaped custom cursor triggers a color-invert effect on underlying content as it moves, paired with a color-changing background — likely a mix-blend-mode technique. Cursor-as-narrative-device rather than pure decoration.
name: Waaarhol — Andy Warhol editorial site
one_line: Warhol-themed editorial: a circle cursor inverts the color of whatever it points at, for a playful scroll experience.
take_what: A cheap mix-blend-mode cursor trick (color-invert on hover) — reservable for a single playful docs/404 Easter egg, not global.

name: Sora app: viral launch to shutdown
one_line: TechCrunch post-mortem: Sora 2's social app hit #1 on the App Store in 24 hours, then shut down April 26, 2026 as downloads fell 3.3M to 1.1M.
design_notes: Overtly TikTok-derivative design: vertical full-bleed video feed, remix/duet-style social loop, one-time video/audio capture to insert a user's likeness into generations; the aesthetic won attention fast but the product didn't survive.
take_what: Caution against chasing a hot social-feed aesthetic wholesale — buzz and retention are different curves; novelty UI without utility burns out.

name: Netris
one_line: Network automation for AI neoclouds; $15M Series A from a16z, announced June 25 2026 (TechCrunch).
design_notes: Light white-background palette, dark text, blue SVG line-icons — a light-mode counter-signal in a dark-mode-saturated category; blunt ROI headline 'Turn GPUs into Revenue'; three-up feature cards; testimonial carousel; explicit 'vs. alternatives' comparison section.
take_what: Icon-led feature-card grid tied to plain-language outcome statements — clean template for a product-pillars section.

name: Evervault
one_line: Payments security infra ($25M Series B) runs a dark, premium fintech look anchored by a payment-card carousel hero.
design_notes: Dark theme, white text, modern sans-serif; hero shows a rotating carousel/grid of tokenized test payment cards; code snippets and a 'Why Trust Us?' security-credential section; sticky-nav SaaS layout with client logo wall (Rippling, Uniswap).
take_what: Literal product artifacts (cards) as hero imagery instead of abstract illustration, plus inline code-snippet proof for developers.

name: Button Computer
one_line: YC W26 wearable voice-AI device covered by TechCrunch and Wired, whose site leans entirely on real-context product photography instead of illustration.
design_notes: Light/dark mode toggle, full-width alternating photo/text sections, large lifestyle photography (device in car, outdoors, at home), fixed header, minimal wordmark, press-logo credibility row (TechCrunch, Wired).
take_what: A photography-led rhythm (full-bleed image, then text, repeat) is a viable alternative to illustration-heavy SaaS hero patterns.

name: Product Hunt Launches News, June 2026 (Startup Edition)
one_line: Roundup blog analyzing what made June 2026's PH winners (Twinr, Air, Lovable, Screen Studio) succeed, plus design commentary.
design_notes: Argues winning PH launches in mid-2026 converge on 'simple demos, fast before-and-after stories, clean UI, immediate output' - conversion clarity over visual maximalism, countering award-gallery cinematic trends.
take_what: Counter-signal: PH-winning startup sites favor plain clarity and instant demo-ability over ornate visuals.

name: Superset (Launch HN)
one_line: Desktop app that runs multiple CLI coding agents in parallel across isolated git worktrees — 'code 10x faster with no switching cost.'
design_notes: Clean modern branding with dark/light mode support, sidebar-plus-terminal-pane desktop-app layout, built-in diff viewer; React/Tailwind-built UI emphasizing a streamlined, IDE-like interface over marketing flourish.
take_what: The 'product screenshot as the whole pitch' approach — showing the real working UI (sidebar, terminal, diff viewer) instead of abstract illustration.

name: putt.day
one_line: A new mini-golf course to putt every day, browser-based with a 'party mode' for social competition.
design_notes: Whimsical 3D-rendered hero — a floating mini-golf course over water — with simple legible type, minimal horizontal top nav, and sections split by plain dividers; casual, playful copy ('grab the ball, drag back') and a golf emoji instead of corporate iconography.
take_what: A lightweight, low-chrome way to foreground a single 3D hero scene as THE interface, not illustration-plus-copy — useful for a playful docs/demo page.

name: Temper (Studio)
one_line: 'A towel made for sweat, tears and everything in between' — Matthias Mentasti's site won Best Visual Design in the 2025 Framer Awards.
design_notes: Judges called it 'light, calm, and visually effortless' minimal e-commerce; poetic single-line hero copy, numbered limited product 'drops,' modular product grid, thematic 'Temperaments' categorization instead of standard nav.
take_what: Emotionally-toned one-line hero copy over a feature headline, plus 'calm minimal' as a named aesthetic target.

name: Adaline
one_line: AI-agent observability/evals platform ("ship agents that self-improve"); enterprise hero with an infinite logo carousel.
design_notes: Minimal neutral gray/white palette, no bright accent color; benefit-driven capitalized headlines ('Truly understand your agents'); continuous-loop scrolling logo carousel for social proof; one decorative footer illustration breaks up an otherwise plain page.
take_what: A restrained neutral palette plus one deliberate illustration moment reads more enterprise-credible than maximalism.

name: The Ultimate Guide: YC Startup Landing Pages
one_line: Structural breakdown of a 2026 YC-caliber homepage, drawn from real sites: Chatbase, Pulley, Artisan, Resend, Deel, FlutterFlow, Firecrawl.
design_notes: Defines an 11-section anatomy: interactive-demo hero, product page, before/after value math, customer-logo proof, testimonials, low-friction demo booking, transparent pricing with free tier, AI-chatbot FAQ, investor-credibility block, community section, docs-heavy footer.
take_what: Investor-credibility and AI-chatbot-FAQ blocks are new-in-2026 additions to standard SaaS anatomy worth checking Astryx's template library covers.

name: I Love Typography — "10 Must-Have Typefaces for 2026"
one_line: Counter-trend list of 'human touch, not machine-made' typefaces — calligraphic serifs (Pliego, Maiola) over geometric/AI-adjacent faces.
design_notes: Every entry emphasizes calligraphic pedigree, hand-drawn irregularity, or a named designer's craft story — a deliberate rebuke of templated, AI-generated-feeling branding.
take_what: Foreground the human design story behind type/component choices as a trust signal on the marketing site, not just specs.

name: Behind the Gradient: Design at Stripe (Medium)
one_line: April 2026 essay unpacking Stripe's gradient-and-craft design philosophy as a case study in making "not-so-pretty" infrastructure feel frictionless.
design_notes: Frames Stripe's purple gradient system + weight-300 type as the visible tip of a deeper obsession with anticipatory documentation UX — showing developers exactly how something works, not just explaining it.
take_what: Lesson isn't "add a gradient" — use polish to make technical products feel legible; pair any flourish with a real UX payoff (docs that show, not tell).

name: Bond
one_line: Post-feed social app turning friend memories into AI recommendations, deliberately dropping infinite scroll; widely covered for anti-doomscrolling stance.
design_notes: Light, airy, mostly-white palette; modular vertical sections (Capture, Share, Discover, Connect, Explore) pair a headline with a full-width image; each feature sits inside an iPhone device-frame mockup showing real in-app screenshots, not illustrations.
take_what: Device-frame mockups of real screenshots per feature section instead of abstract icons/illustrations

name: Mireye
one_line: YC S26 physical-world-agent infra startup uses a soft cream-to-sage gradient hero with a live annotated globe visualization.
design_notes: Soft pastel gradient bg (peach top-right to sage-green bottom-left), bold black grotesk H1 with a green accent phrase and a blinking text-cursor bar mid-sentence, interactive globe with floating geo-data pills, pill buttons, YC badge.
take_what: Soft gradient + bold sans + one accent color reads warmer than the all-black dev-tool look; a mid-headline blinking cursor signals 'still live'.

name: AIOS Medical Unveils AI Doctor at HF0 Demo Day with $350M ARR Target
one_line: Write-up of AIOS Medical's HF0 demo-day pitch and the mixed reaction to its $350M ARR claim against a still-sparse website.
design_notes: N/A — aggregator news post.
take_what: Shows how one bold ARR number becomes the entire headline/marketing hook post-demo-day — a single-huge-stat-as-hero-claim copy pattern.

name: Old Tom Capital (oldtomcapital.com)
one_line: Investment/capital firm site by studio Highly Necessary; added to Siteinspire April 28 2026.
design_notes: Clean corporate typographic minimalism, sophisticated restrained palette, subtle motion from the studio's branding+identity+animation package, dedicated mobile hero treatment.
take_what: Shows minimal/big-type language translating to a trust-first finance vertical — a reference for Astryx's 'serious tool' positioning.

name: Mammoth Brands (mammothbrands.com)
one_line: Business/finance-agency site tagged Big Type + Typographic on Siteinspire, added May 15 2026.
design_notes: Text-heavy statement-driven hero hierarchy, bold large-scale typography as the primary visual device over imagery, clean modern responsive layout, minimal decorative elements.
take_what: Another data point for typography-as-the-whole-hero — oversized type alone, no photography/illustration, reads premium in 2026 B2B sites.

name: startups.gallery
one_line: Curated directory of early-stage startups with jobs+funding news; useful for spotting which newly-funded companies to check for fresh site launches.
design_notes: Minimalist card-based gallery: scannable startup cards (name, description, category, funding stage, work-type, HQ), hierarchical filter nav (stage, vertical, investor, geography), infinite 'Load more' scroll — dense data kept legible via strict card grid, not heavy visuals.
take_what: Feeder list for exemplar discovery — freshly funded companies here are the ones most likely to ship a new marketing site worth scouting next cycle.

name: Carbonable
one_line: Carbon-contribution-management SaaS; Allan Floury's Framer build won June 2026 Site of the Month runner-up for its scroll interactions.
design_notes: Dark color scheme with restrained typography and 'fantastic scroll interactions' — fits the dark-minimal B2B SaaS pattern seen across several 2026 winners; motion spent on 2-3 key moments, not every section.
take_what: Discipline note: spend motion budget on a few high-craft moments in a dark B2B SaaS template, not on animating everything.

name: Wayve
one_line: British embodied-AI startup uses large real-world photography of its vehicles on London/Japan streets instead of abstract tech graphics.
design_notes: Dark/neutral background, high-contrast white type; all-caps sans nav; large photographic hero of vehicles in real urban settings as dominant visual (not renders or AI art); mega-menu with featured content cards.
take_what: Authentic real-world deployment photography instead of abstract 3D/gradient AI imagery signals operational credibility over hype.

name: Utsubo — "14 Japanese Web Studios That Actually Ship Great Work (2026)"
one_line: 2026 roundup of Japanese award-winning studios naming the defining trend: engineering-forward WebGPU/Three.js craft vs. ma (negative-space) minimalism.
design_notes: n/a — trend commentary, not a visual site; documents the density-vs-ma spectrum and cites IVRESS, Yamauchi No.10 Family Office, and NEWFOLK/MOHEIM as reference builds, plus 30-50% lower Japanese-studio rates vs. Western agencies.
take_what: Frame for choosing between dense information layouts and deliberately spacious ("ma") ones per page purpose, rather than one density for the whole site.

name: Sigma Browser — agentic browser roundup
one_line: Privacy-first AI browser's own blog positions it inside a comparison of the whole agentic-browser category.
design_notes: Content-marketing format, not a flashy hero: a category comparison round-up (Comet, Atlas, Fellou, Neon, Dia, BrowserOS) on the vendor's own domain, signaling the space is mature enough for its own 'how we stack up' genre; Sigma pitches local/offline AI as its differentiator.
take_what: 'Category comparison as content marketing' page format now standard for this wave — reference for benchmarking a design-system site against peers.

name: Longshot Space
one_line: SPC-backed startup ($5M new investment June 2026, $20M total) building a ground-based 'space gun' for hypersonic/orbital launch.
design_notes: Webflow-built. Full-bleed autoplay looping background video ('sizzle reel') behind h1 'Transforming the future of hypersonics and space access,' with scroll-triggered parallax mask shifting footage speed. Colors in external CSS, not inline-extractable.
take_what: Full-bleed looping video hero with scroll-tied parallax as a cinematic alternative to static hero imagery for hard-tech/infra products.

name: Meech213 (The Blackpepper Studio)
one_line: Fashion/beauty photographer portfolio by The Blackpepper Studio, Awwwards Site of the Day June 29 2026, 7.4/10.
design_notes: Built in Webflow with CSS/JS polish rather than custom framework; fashion-photography-led portfolio prioritizing storytelling through image sequencing over UI chrome.
take_what: A small two-person studio won a top award on Webflow — award-tier craft is editorial photo/type pacing, not stack complexity.

name: Scrolling Designs: 8 Patterns and When to Use Each (2026)
one_line: 2026 guide cataloguing scroll-snap, scrollytelling, parallax, and horizontal-scroll patterns with guidance on mobile vs desktop fit.
design_notes: Names scroll-snap (no-JS scroll-snap-type/align) as the dominant pattern for full-page mobile sections; splits 'narrative immersion' scrollytelling from 'scroll-as-navigation'; flags iOS viewport-height quirks needing a JS workaround for reliable snap on real devices.
take_what: Reference for choosing scroll-snap vs scrollytelling vs parallax per section on a mobile-first page, plus the iOS viewport gotcha to test before shipping.

name: zeroheight Showcase
one_line: zeroheight's Showcase catalogs real design-system documentation sites (Uber, NS Railways, Hitachi) by industry tag, with pull-quotes from each team.
design_notes: Light-background card grid, large featured imagery per card, company logo overlay, industry tag chips (Transportation, SaaS, Healthcare, Finance...), embedded customer pull-quotes like 'the source of truth that answers all our design questions'.
take_what: Industry/use-case tagging on a showcase grid, plus a pull-quote per entry — could tag an Astryx component gallery by use-case.

name: HaloBraid
one_line: Robotic hair-braiding assistant for salons; $7M seed from Seven Seven Six, announced June 23 2026 (TechCrunch).
design_notes: Minimalist white/neutral palette, dark bold headlines, generous whitespace; opens with a 30,000-years-of-braiding historical narrative before the product reveal; before/after salon-appointment timeline; press-logo strip (WWD, TechCrunch, Allure).
take_what: Lead-with-history-then-reveal-the-product narrative arc in the hero — builds stakes before the pitch; portable to a docs intro.

name: Series
one_line: AI-run social matchmaking network operating entirely inside iMessage; Yale founders raised $5.1M pre-seed, 750+ campuses.
design_notes: Marketing site itself returned access-blocked on fetch; press (TechCrunch, Forbes) describes the in-product UI as a swipeable carousel of 10 profile 'shares' delivered as iMessage images — a card-carousel interaction pattern rather than a traditional feed.
take_what: Swipeable card-carousel pattern for browsing a set of profiles/items, borrowed from a chat-native UI

name: Nebex
one_line: Market infrastructure/exchange for the space economy; $30M seed led by GV, announced June 29 2026.
design_notes: Neutral white/gray/black B2B SaaS layout; bold hero line 'Designed for Space. Built for Markets'; three-module feature section (sourcing, execution, payments) each with abstract SVG line illustrations; standard nav + 'Request Access' CTA.
take_what: Three-persona feature split (supplier / buyer / financial institution), each with its own icon set — reusable for multi-audience doc pages.

name: Arcturus
one_line: Carbon-nanomaterial-infused metals for grid/EV/data-center power; $8M seed led by Initialized Capital, emerged from stealth June 30 2026.
design_notes: Dark background, bold recruiting-style hero headline 'ENGINEERS WANTED' with founder-signed copy; decorative SVG cross motifs framing sections; centerpiece product photo of a nano-infused wire cross-section; investor-logo footer.
take_what: Hero-as-recruiting-pitch with a founder signature personalizes a deep-tech story — a voice technique an about/careers page could borrow.

name: Dispatch
one_line: YC W26 startup building reusable space vehicles to return manufactured goods to Earth, marketed with a single poetic line: 'bringing space down to earth.'
design_notes: Dark background, high-contrast white type, single-column vertical scroll, one poetic headline as the entire hero statement, minimal nav, one CTA ('Get In Touch'), YC badge as the sole trust signal.
take_what: Radical hero restraint — one evocative line, nothing else — counters feature-dense heroes when a story needs emotion before proof.

name: HF0's latest Demo Day outgrows its physical house venue
one_line: Coverage that HF0's 2026 demo day physically outgrew its own house venue, signaling the residency's rising scale and prestige.
design_notes: N/A — aggregator news post, not a designed site.
take_what: Evidence that small-cohort, high-density founder residencies are the current 'hot format' narrative — useful color on who's building fast now.

name: HFØ reports five of ten teams at its recent demo day broke $10M annualized
one_line: HF0's own stat-flex framing of its 2026 demo-day results, plus commentary that HF0 now works across stages, not just early-stage.
design_notes: N/A — aggregator news post.
take_what: The 'X of Y teams hit $Z' stat-flex sentence structure as a proof-of-velocity device, reusable in a results/impact section.

name: Sequence Agentic
one_line: 'Money movement API for AI agents' - PH-launched fintech infra product riding the agentic-commerce wave, July 2026 top-10.
design_notes: Clean light-theme fintech look prioritizing trust over flourish: bank/partner logo wall (Mastercard, Plaid, Thread Bank), compliance badges, promo banner ('3 months free API access'), safety/permissions FAQ, PH badge in hero.
take_what: Trust-signal-dense hero (compliance badges plus partner logos above the fold) for categories where the core anxiety is trust.

name: Ardent (YC P26)
one_line: YC-backed Postgres database branching for coding agents — spins up isolated production-like DB copies in under 6 seconds.
design_notes: Dark/black terminal-style hero with navy/blue CTA accents, standard SaaS template rhythm (hero, logo row, alternating feature/image, comparison table, integrations, testimonials); terminal/CLI screenshots dominate over illustration, targeting a developer audience directly.
take_what: Terminal-screenshot-as-hero-proof plus a direct competitor comparison table — fast technical credibility for a developer buyer, same audience Astryx targets.

name: Jeton.com
one_line: Jeton's site uses a bold pink-to-orange gradient animation with 3D-illustrated coin metaphors to visualize money movement.
design_notes: 3D illustrated coins animate through step-by-step transaction flows; interactive currency-conversion playground embedded in page; bold animated gradient as backdrop rather than flat brand color.
take_what: Metaphor-driven 3D micro-illustration makes an abstract process legible — pattern for visualizing Astryx concepts as an interactive diagram.

name: Melnūdens Coffee
one_line: Specialty-coffee brand site by designer Henriks Porciks — repeat Framer honoree (Site of the Year 2023, June 2026 SOTM runner-up).
design_notes: Praised for 'top-notch' typography and color plus 'visually stunning' scroll interactions; classy, editorial feel typical of small-studio Framer sites optimizing for craft over funnel conversion.
take_what: Proof one obsessively-crafted scroll sequence plus a tight type/color system reads premium — a polish bar for a docs/home hero.

name: Crayo AI
one_line: AI TikTok-clip generation tool; its Framer site is featured in Framer's own gallery as a creator-economy design example.
design_notes: Verified directly: blue-based color system on white, bold oversized headline hierarchy, lightning-bolt accent icon, vertical modular page (hero, 3-step workflow, icon-card feature grid, testimonials), trust badges above the fold.
take_what: Audience-matched energy (fast, saturated, gradient-heavy) is a reminder that 'the Framer look' isn't monolithic.

name: Goodspeed — Best Startup Websites Built with Framer
one_line: Curated gallery of startup Framer sites (Tomorrow, Graphy, GitBook, Flighty, Visual Electric, Wishes App) as reference examples.
design_notes: Recurring descriptors: 'dynamic typography and smooth transitions' (Tomorrow), 'bold and modern interface' with structured grid (Graphy), 'motion-driven aesthetics' (Visual Electric) — reinforces motion-forward, grid-structured as the current startup-site default.
take_what: Graphy's structured grid + strategic type, and Visual Electric's motion-driven layout, are the clearest reference patterns here.

name: Upstage AI
one_line: Seoul-based Solar-LLM maker (Solar Pro 2, 31B params, strong Korean/Japanese benchmarks); "Korea's AI national team" positioning.
design_notes: Dark-neutral palette on generous whitespace; bold two-column hero ("Build intelligence for the future of work") with a product image; modular product cards; duplicated logo marquee for continuous-scroll credibility; SOC/HIPAA/ISO badges in footer.
take_what: Two-column hero pairing a bold claim with a real product screenshot, plus a duplicated logo marquee for an always-full trust strip.

name: Torriden
one_line: Korean minimalist skincare brand gone viral on TikTok/Reddit in 2026 (DIVE-IN hyaluronic line); 2026 rebrand built around a terrain/skin-layers motif.
