design_notes: Sets body/UI in Noto Sans; 2026 logo refresh replaced a rigid technical mark with hand-pressure-varied organic strokes; graphic motifs echo terrain contour lines and skin-layer cross-sections, tying to the slogan "YOUR SKIN IS OUR PLANET."
take_what: A single recurring geometric motif derived from the product itself, reused across logo, packaging, and site as one coherent visual system.

name: Storybook Showcase
one_line: Storybook's own Showcase is a curated card-grid gallery of public component libraries and design systems — a live trend index for docs-as-product sites.
design_notes: Card-grid gallery: project thumbnail, org avatar/name, and a star-count metric per card; filter-by-name search bar; curated 'Popular' section; 'Load more' progressive pagination instead of full pages.
take_what: Card-grid gallery pattern (thumbnail + org identity + popularity metric) — relevant if Astryx builds a 'built with Astryx' component showcase.

name: Nicelydone — Waitlist Page Design gallery
one_line: Curated screenshot gallery of real SaaS waitlist/coming-soon pages incl. OpenAI, Framer, Replit, Descript, Remote — for benchmarking current conventions.
design_notes: Mixed approaches: minimalist form-only (Bird), modal signup over live product (Replit), gallery-style with localization (Framer), accordion feature previews (Descript) — mechanic matters more than a single aesthetic.
take_what: Reference set to benchmark an Astryx 'request access' template against current real SaaS conventions.

name: Codrops — "Inside Metalab: Silicon Valley's Best-Kept Design Secret"
one_line: Codrops profile of Metalab (160-person Victoria, Canada agency) on how it builds startup product/brand design at scale.
design_notes: Agency-retrospective format per the beat brief: Codrops covering a design shop's process/philosophy rather than one site. Source for how a professional studio structures startup visual-identity systems end to end.
take_what: Agency process pieces show how studios structure a component-driven visual system, relevant to how Astryx documents design rationale.

name: Best of Show HN — July 2026
one_line: Monthly curated Hacker News Show HN list; the July 2026 batch skews toward plain-text, content-first tools (markdown editors, RSS readers, terminal apps).
design_notes: N/A, a link-list resource not a single site. Listed projects (Flashtype, Strata, Newsprint, Inkwell, DevTUI) lean toward functional simplicity over graphical flourish.
take_what: A recurring, live feed of freshly launched small startups to spot-check for the text-first pattern before it hits mainstream design-trend press.

name: Rebrand Gallery — OpenAI entry
one_line: Curated rebrand-catalog entry tagging OpenAI's identity: monochrome + halftone patterning, black/white/blue-family palette, lavender accent.
design_notes: Tags OpenAI's system as Monochromatic + Halftone pattern styles; palette = black, white, blue/sky-blue/electric-blue/navy family, plus a lavender accent. Filed under in-house 'Pro' production tier in the gallery's taxonomy.

name: Gemini app redesign — feature breakdown

name: Chert (YC P26)
one_line: API/workflow layer for sending and routing real iMessage conversations at scale — 'Twilio for iMessage.'
design_notes: Light background, dark text, blue accents mirroring iMessage's blue-bubble branding; hero shows an animated live iMessage thread mockup (read receipts, reactions, typing); scrolling client-logo row (Whop, Vela); iOS-style rounded elements and subtle shadows throughout.
take_what: Using the platform's own native chrome (iOS message bubble) as the literal hero visual instead of abstract illustration — 'show don't render' pattern.

name: 11 Web Design Trends in 2026, With Live Demos (Gezar)
one_line: Interactive 2026 trend guide letting you try kinetic typography and glassmorphism live in-browser instead of just reading about them.
design_notes: Hero uses kinetic type where words rotate through values (growth, leads, meetings, results) on scroll; ships runnable glassmorphism (blur+transparency+border) demo blocks beside each trend writeup so visitors toggle/interact instead of viewing static screenshots.
take_what: The format itself — a trend explainer shipping a live, toggleable demo next to each writeup — beats prose-only trend posts for a docs site.

name: SitesPlaced — 13 Best SaaS Website Designs of 2026
one_line: No-code builder's own demo-template gallery of 13 archetypal 2026 SaaS designs — synthetic templates, not real launches, but a signal.
design_notes: Repeating pattern across all 13: near-black canvases, liquid-glass card surfaces, italic-serif or gradient-text headlines, some char-by-char kinetic entrances, uppercase type, glass email-capture pills, radial/node-cluster decoration (e.g. 'PowerAI', 'Cosmos', 'CodeNest').
take_what: Even as vendor demos not real launches, the near-black + liquid-glass-card + italic-serif-headline formula is what's sold as 'premium SaaS' now.

name: Corner

take_what: Narrative curated-list layout (vs. tabular data) as an alternative to dense data tables

take_what: A dense, scannable ranked-list/leaderboard layout — useful if Astryx needs a plain data table or changelog page that gets out of its own way.

name: Top 10 Minimalist Web Design Trends For 2026 (Digitalsilk)
one_line: Trend roundup arguing clean geometric typography now signals innovation/trust for tech and startup brands, part of a broader 2026 minimalist push.

name: Muzli — Dark Mode Inspiration
one_line: 60+ curated dark-mode UI screens for 2026 spanning SaaS analytics, fintech, and ML-monitoring dashboards with neon accents on near-black backgrounds.

take_what: Model for organizing Astryx's own component docs by real usage pattern/flow (pricing tables, onboarding, settings), not only by component name.

one_line: Directory aggregating crowd-extracted DESIGN.md files (incl. Cursor's, Stripe's) as reusable design-language references for AI coding agents.
design_notes: Each entry distills a company site into a portable style dossier (palette, type scale, spacing, component patterns) meant to be dropped into an AI coding agent's context — evidence that "extract this brand's visual DNA" is itself a mid-2026 tooling trend.
take_what: Suggests Astryx's own token system could ship as a portable "DESIGN.md" for AI-agent consumption — closes the loop with the AGENTS.md vibe-test work.

name: Andera
one_line: AI-native SOX/internal-audit automation platform raised a $37M Series A led by Lightspeed (June 17, 2026).
design_notes: Clean corporate-B2B palette, neutral white/gray, one accent CTA ('Book a demo'); bold hero 'Automate your controls testing'; real product screenshots (spreadsheets, email) embedded in marketing sections; dual-audience hero split; the $37M raise used as an on-page trust badge.
take_what: Surfacing the funding round as an on-page trust badge, and splitting the hero into two explicit audience paths instead of one CTA.

name: Architect Labs
one_line: AI system for custom chip design/verification; $24M seed led by Kindred Ventures, backed by Jeff Dean and OpenAI/Nvidia execs, announced June 18 2026.
design_notes: Minimalist Next.js B2B site; simple top nav (About, Blog, Careers), left-aligned body copy, large hero banner image, asterisk section dividers; content-over-ornamentation, no visible decorative motion — sober frontier-lab positioning.
take_what: A restrained, text-dense 'serious lab' look — proof credibility-first engineer audiences sometimes prefer sober type over bento/gradient maximalism.

design_notes: Part of a broad animation/motion component catalog (700+ items) aimed at React/Next.js builders; positions magnetic-cursor hover as a standard, drop-in interaction rather than a bespoke agency build.
name: Uilora — Magnetic Cursor UI Components
one_line: Next.js library ships 'Magnetic Cursor' as one of 700+ production-ready components — magnetism normalized as installable UI.
take_what: Confirms magnetic-cursor is now an expected off-the-shelf component category in React libraries, not a bespoke build.

name: Stan Store
one_line: All-in-one link-in-bio creator storefront (checkout, bundling, upsells) built for traffic arriving from Instagram/TikTok bios.
design_notes: Per comparison coverage (site is a heavy client-rendered SPA, little static content observable directly): positioned as sales-focused vs. Beacons' design-first approach — mobile checkout, bundling, and upsell screens are the featured UI, not lifestyle photography.
take_what: For a mobile-social-to-purchase funnel, foreground the transaction UI itself as hero content instead of lifestyle photography.

name: Bland
one_line: Enterprise voice-AI-for-calls launch video hit 7.4M X views, headlined by a live '530,807,128 calls resolved' counter.
design_notes: Conventional enterprise B2B vertical scroll. Hero: 'Built for high-stakes phone calls where security and trust actually matter,' huge live call-counter above fold. Animated Build/Test/Deploy cards, tabbed deployment timeline, security-badge wall, light mode.
take_what: A single enormous live usage counter as the trust-building hero stat, placed ahead of any feature copy.

name: Win the First 5 Seconds: The YC Landing Page Formula
one_line: A 2026 YC-landing-page playbook argues the opposite of visual flourish: single-column static layouts and 'mom-readable' headlines, minimal motion.
design_notes: Prescribes dropping carousels/gifs/decorative video, the headline formula 'Outcome for [ICP] without [pain]', cites that hard words cut conversion ~25%, and that only short 10-60s embedded product demos (not decorative animation) earn their keep.
take_what: A useful check against over-designing Astryx's site — if the goal is adoption not award-bait, a demo-first plain-language hero can beat WebGL flourish.

name: Robert Scoble live-thread from HF0 demo day
one_line: On-the-ground account of HF0's June 2026 demo day (14 companies, several still stealth) from a repeat attendee who rates this batch highly.
design_notes: N/A — social post.
take_what: The 'insider live-tweet from the room' distribution pattern accelerators now lean on instead of formal press releases.

name: Boardy on HF0 batch demand and results
one_line: 500+ founders reached out within days of HF0's next batch opening; cites 5/10 prior teams past $10M and the top team at $200M ARR.
design_notes: N/A — social post.
take_what: Stat-flex tweet reinforcing exclusivity aura — a distribution technique relevant to framing 'what's hot' claims.

name: HF0 Facts page
one_line: HF0's own numbers-only page: batch-by-batch demo-day results back to F21, confirming batch size (10 teams) and season+year naming (S25, W25...).
design_notes: Dense, terse stat list per batch (e.g. S25: $82M avg post-demo valuation; W25: 4/10 teams over $3M revenue) — a distinct content type from narrative marketing pages.
take_what: A dedicated, dense 'facts/proof' page as its own content type, separate from narrative marketing — a pattern for a docs/credibility page.

name: web.dev: Well-controlled scrolling with CSS Scroll Snap
one_line: Google's canonical technical reference for CSS scroll-snap, the no-JS mechanism behind most 2026 mobile-first vertical landing pages.
design_notes: Covers scroll-snap-type/align/stop, 96%+ browser support since 2019, use cases spanning full-screen storytelling, onboarding carousels, and swipeable dashboards.
take_what: Direct implementation reference if Astryx ships a scroll-snap layout primitive — standard CSS, no JS workaround needed per project's StyleX rules.

name: Sidebar.io
one_line: Long-running (since 2012) daily design-link newsletter, now curated by Fabricio Teixeira of UX Collective, ~40k subscribers, 5 hand-picked links/weekday.
design_notes: Not a visual style — a curation/distribution mechanism. Relevant as the beat's primary discovery surface for what's currently circulating in design conversation.
take_what: The 'five tight links a day, zero noise' format is a content-voice model Astryx's own changelog could imitate instead of long-form posts.

name: Ciao Energy
one_line: Energy-drink CPG launch site (French market) using Three.js/scroll-triggered flavor reveals — the 3D trend spreading beyond SaaS.
design_notes: 'Scroller pour découvrir' scroll-to-reveal flavor carousel keyed to product-can photography; white space + black type with flavor-derived accent colors; motion budget concentrated on the hero/carousel only, rest of page stays flat.
take_what: Confirms the trend isn't SaaS-only — even a CPG brand spends its entire 3D/motion budget on one hero moment, keeps the rest flat.

name: Filteroff / Spark (video speed dating)
one_line: Video speed-dating app (rebranded 'Spark' on app stores); landing page is built around live/virtual events rather than static swipe profiles.
design_notes: Per coverage: vibrant, event-driven landing page with dynamic visual layout and trust-first storytelling around real-time video connection; event-centric CTA structure ('join tonight's event') rather than a generic 'download the app' button.
take_what: Time-bound, event-framed CTAs read more TikTok-native than evergreen 'Sign up' buttons; worth testing for launch-style pages.

name: "Content is the new storefront" — TikTok Shop 2026 design shift
one_line: 2026 analysis: TikTok Shop storefronts fail when designed like Shopify PDPs instead of scrollable feed content; thumbnails must read at 80x80px.
design_notes: Hard constraint distinctive to vertical-feed commerce: hero imagery must read at thumbnail scale in-feed, not just full-bleed; recommends 1-3 SKUs over full-catalog grids to avoid mid-scroll confusion; creators/content replace product pages as storefront.
take_what: Test any shareable component-preview image at thumbnail scale too, not just full-page — that's how it's actually seen once shared into feeds.

name: Awwwards — AI-Powered Web Projects
one_line: Awwwards' own 'AI-powered' collection skews toward older interactive ML demos (Quick Draw, Khroma) rather than 2026 dark-mode startup marketing sites.
design_notes: Mostly experimental single-purpose demos (deepfake, drawing-recognition games, color-palette generators) rather than cohesive dark-mode marketing sites — a reminder that 'AI on the web' and 'AI-startup marketing-site aesthetic' are different categories that get conflated.
take_what: A cautionary reference — don't let 'AI-powered demo' gimmicks substitute for a coherent marketing-site design language.

name: Baseline Type Scale Generator
one_line: Type-scale tool embedded inside a broader design-tool product (Baseline), pairing scale controls with an educational live preview and code export.
design_notes: Full marketing chrome (product/solutions/resources nav dropdowns) wraps the utility instead of a bare tool page; live preview grid shows every step with em+px labels (0.833em caption to 2.488em h1); "Grab Code" CTA; long-form copy explains type-scale theory inline.
take_what: Wrapping a narrow utility (type scale) inside full product marketing chrome plus educational copy — turns a docs tool into a lead-gen page.

name: Cursor DESIGN.md (unofficial dossier)
one_line: Crowd-extracted DESIGN.md dossier for cursor.com — off-white/dark-brown palette, 4px spacing scale, monospace-for-code type system.
design_notes: Palette: #f7f7f4 primary off-white, #26251e secondary dark-brown, #e6e5e0 accent, #050503 deep black. Type: Display 2.8rem/700, H1 2rem/700, body 1rem/400, monospace for code. Spacing 4px base (4-32px). Radius 0-24px, 6 shadow levels.
take_what: Ready-made token scaffold (spacing, radius, elevation) for a "keyboard-centric devtool" look — useful for an Astryx docs/dev-audience theme variant.

name: Stripe DESIGN.md (unofficial dossier)
one_line: Crowd-extracted DESIGN.md dossier tagging Stripe's identity as "signature purple gradients" + "weight-300 elegance" for premium fintech UI.
design_notes: Positions Stripe pattern for "payment platforms, gradient-heavy designs, premium fintech UIs." Emphasizes light font weights (300) as the sophistication signal, purple-led gradient system as differentiator.
take_what: The "weight-300 elegance" tag is a useful shorthand for a light type treatment that reads premium/fintech — worth testing as an alt heading weight.

name: Endex
one_line: 'AI Built For Excel' launch video pulled 10.8M X views — beating Google AI's and Manus AI's clips despite a narrow finance-analyst niche.
design_notes: Minimal light-mode hero 'AI Built For Excel,' Microsoft Partner badge as trust anchor, compliance badge row (SOC2/ISO/CCPA/GDPR), customer quote, plain feature cards ('Trace References'). No animation — clarity-over-spectacle enterprise pattern.
take_what: Proof a plain, animation-free, badge-driven layout can still carry a top-15 viral launch — spectacle isn't required.

name: Dribbble — Waitlist UI / Leaderboard UI tags
one_line: Dribbble's waitlist-ui and leaderboard-ui tags (200+ / 53 shots) are the default concept-mockup source for queue-position and referral-rank visuals.
design_notes: Aggregator tag page, not one design — concept shots typically favor numeric rank badges, progress bars toward next reward tier, avatar-stack social proof; palette/type vary shot to shot.
take_what: Mood-board source for queue/leaderboard component visuals before building an Astryx primitive.

name: Codrops — Comfort Websites
one_line: Emerging niche: 'comfort websites' as personalized emotional-support spaces, documented via 3 named case studies.
design_notes: Named: Mr. Panda's Portfolio (mascot changes outfits), Aimee's Papercraft World (nostalgic paper/craft aesthetic), a couple's 'Comfort Space' (uses the Pixar 'Up' house as metaphor). Devices: multi-dimensional style, nostalgic textures, fantasy imagery.
take_what: Genuinely fresh but low-relatedness trend (therapeutic micro-sites) — little direct transfer to a B2B design-system marketing site.

name: Awwwards — Fintech Design Inspiration
one_line: Awwwards' fintech-specific inspiration collection, aggregating award-nominated fintech site designs (Contiant Open Banking, Hub Fintech Europe).
design_notes: Aggregator grouping award-recognized fintech sites; sibling collection at awwwards.com/websites/startups/ covers startups generally. Award-circuit sample skews toward higher production value / more experimental than typical funding-press sites.
take_what: Standing bookmark for periodic spot-checks of fintech design specifically, complementing funding-press exemplars that skew more conservative.

name: Gency AI
one_line: AI+blockchain 'sovereign advertising network' raised $20M with TikTok and HF0 as backers; residency-cohort membership itself is unconfirmed.
design_notes: Could not confirm visual design directly (fetch returned text only); branded around 'AI-Driven Verifiable Advertising' with Web3-inflected language ('sovereign', 'verifiable', 'on-chain').
take_what: Crypto/AI crossover vocabulary ('sovereign', 'verifiable coordination') as a 2026 enterprise-copy trend worth tracking.

name: Design Systems Surf
one_line: A maintained, searchable database of public design systems (Adobe Spectrum, Apple HIG, Material, Atlassian...) rather than a dated listicle.
design_notes: Sections for Products, Libraries, Articles, Blueprints, and a 'Popular Systems' gallery; each system entry is tagged with which resources exist (Docs/Components) and linked platforms (Figma, Storybook, Repository) for quick cross-comparison.
take_what: A living, tag-filterable index (docs/components available, which platforms) beats a one-off blog roundup as a docs-presentation reference.

name: Modular Scale
one_line: The original 2010 ratio-based type-scale calculator, still live; musical-interval presets, Web/Sass/JS code export.
design_notes: Utilitarian high-contrast black-on-white; serif/sans pairing (JAF Bernini Sans headers, Freight Text Pro body); tabbed interface (Calculator/Output/About) instead of scroll; ratio buttons labeled with both math (1.618) and music terms (Golden Ratio, Perfect Fifth).
take_what: A design-token tool that has stayed legible for 15+ years on plain undecorated HTML — a sober baseline against flashier newcomers.

name: Hang Ten Systems
one_line: Ex-Infosys CEO Vishal Sikka's enterprise AI services startup; $32M seed led by Mayfield, announced June 24 2026 (TechCrunch).
design_notes: Stark single-column layout, black type on light bg, near-zero navigation (just Press/Blog), one hero product image, investor-logo strip (Mayfield, Aramco); no visible animation, bento grid, or motion flourish anywhere.
take_what: A $32M-round enterprise brand shipping near-zero ornamentation and still reading credible — a sober floor against over-designing.

name: Slate Medicines
one_line: Raleigh biotech launched with a $130M Series A (Feb 2026, RA Capital/Forbion/Foresite) for an in-licensed migraine therapy.
design_notes: Restrained clinical-minimalist aesthetic typical of a fresh biotech launch: modular Focus/Science/Pipeline/Team/Board/News sections, pipeline data as a table, placeholder-style team photos, no visible motion or illustration flourish.
take_what: Counter-example: a well-funded launch that skips visual flourish for stark clinical credibility — the sober baseline other 'trendy' sites read against.

name: YC Application Day (S26) on Product Hunt
axis: launch mechanism: PH x YC crossover
one_line: Product Hunt ran a dedicated 'YC Application Day S26' contest: launch and tag 'YC application' for a guaranteed YC partner review.
design_notes: Not a designed site — a contest/launch page. Evidence that Product Hunt launch pages remain the default proving ground new-founder sites optimize their above-the-fold pitch for.
take_what: Worth checking how an Astryx-adjacent product would frame itself for a PH launch card — tight headline + one GIF/screenshot + single CTA.

name: Bloomy
one_line: YC S26 K-12 AI-tutoring startup splits its hero: gradient headline text beside a floating node-diagram product card.
design_notes: Split two-column hero, blue-to-teal gradient applied to headline text and CTA button (not the bg), rounded bubble-letter logotype, mint-white dotted gradient bg, floating card with a node-diagram illustration, tabbed feature switcher below.
take_what: Gradient-on-text (not full-bleed) is a lighter 'friendly SaaS' touch, useful for differentiating feature callouts without full color blocks.

name: QOSMIC
one_line: SPC/Accel/Prosus-backed Bengaluru deep-tech startup building laser optical ground stations for satellites, $3.33M seed June 2026.
design_notes: Heavily client-rendered SPA (React); initial HTML only ~2.6KB, visuals JS-injected, not inspectable via fetch. Only verified point: near-black bg #0A0A0F, matching dark-mode-default norm for deep-tech/space sites. Thin/limited observation.
take_what: Weak signal only: near-black base confirms space/deep-tech dark-mode-first convention; not enough directly observed for a specific technique.

name: Muzli - best designed landing pages
one_line: Muzli's 60+ pick 2026 landing-page roundup, cross-cited across multiple 2026 trend write-ups as shorthand for 'what's hot.'
design_notes: Aggregator frequently cited alongside bento grids, bold oversized type, and AI-personalization as this season's defining traits.
take_what: A scan tool for spotting repeated motifs (bento grids, oversized type, dark-mode AI tools) across many startups at once.

name: Butterflies AI
one_line: Social platform where AI-generated characters and humans coexist and post in the same feed; $4.8M seed led by Coatue.
design_notes: Interface is reported to closely mirror Instagram's feed/grid/profile conventions — familiar photo-grid and card layout repurposed to host both human and AI-generated personas, rather than inventing a new visual language.
take_what: Using a familiar, proven feed/card layout as a trust anchor when the underlying content model is novel

name: Motion Spring Visualizer
one_line: Indie lab tool for tweaking spring stiffness/damping/mass with a live GIF preview, framed as a personal blog post, not a product.
design_notes: Minimal single-column layout under a personal site's "Home / Lab" nav; conversational first-person copy ("I have been using... quite fiddly"); central animated GIF captioned "Tweak the spring props!" is the sole visual proof; light bg, no dark mode, no branding chrome.
take_what: Framing a niche technical tool as a personal lab note (informal voice + one demo GIF) instead of a full product page — lightweight docs-cookbook pattern.

name: Godly.design gallery
one_line: Daily-updated curated gallery of real startup/SaaS marketing and landing pages, filterable for layout, motion, and storytelling references.
design_notes: Not a single design but a filterable index of live sites — organized by category (landing page, SaaS, ecommerce) so designers can study current layout, motion, and storytelling patterns across many funded startups at once rather than one-off inspiration.
take_what: Use as an ongoing reference index to track live startup-site patterns over time rather than a one-time trend snapshot

name: Best of Product Hunt: June 2026 (monthly leaderboard)
one_line: Product Hunt's own monthly ranked leaderboard, primary source for which startups won attention in June 2026.
design_notes: Not a design showcase itself; used as discovery index (Fundraisly, Goldfish, Upstream, Bond, Tencent EdgeOne Makers, Mailwarm 2.0, Publora, Bluerails Discovery, Elentaria, ElevenAgents all ranked here).
take_what: Sourcing resource, not a design reference.

name: Awwwards — Japan websites directory
one_line: Live feed of Japan's 2026 Awwwards-recognized sites (IVRESS, sakazuki, Penguin Capital) — quick way to sample the current Japanese web-craft aesthetic.
design_notes: n/a — index/gallery, not a single design; useful as a continuously refreshed sampling tool for Japan's 3D/WebGPU + restrained-typography house style.
take_what: Bookmark as a recurring design-scan source before any Astryx marketing-site refresh, specifically filtered to Japan's engineering-led aesthetic.

name: Awwwards — South Korea websites directory
one_line: Live feed of Korea's 2026 Awwwards sites (K-beauty, coffee, fashion brands) — shows Korean consumer-brand web craft distinct from AI-startup design.
design_notes: n/a — index/gallery; mix skews toward polished lifestyle/D2C brand sites (Torriden, Blue Bottle Coffee Korea, Andersson Bell, Dongwon) over SaaS/AI dashboards, showing Korea's current web energy concentrated in brand storytelling.
take_what: Cross-check for "brand storytelling" hero/motion patterns from D2C/lifestyle sites as a counterpoint to SaaS-dashboard-style marketing pages.

name: YC Startup Directory — Summer 2026 filter
one_line: YC's own directory filtered to Summer 2026 shows 56 companies live as of July 2, 2026 (of an eventual ~150-200); batch just started, Demo Day is Sept 10.
design_notes: Not a designed marketing page — the authoritative live roster used to verify which companies are genuinely S26, since third-party AI summaries frequently conflated S26 with the prior Spring 2026 ('P26') batch.
take_what: Canonical source for who's in the current batch; a reminder that even YC's own batch-letter scheme changed in 2026 and needs re-verifying each cycle.

name: YC S26 Companies (Summer 2026): Full Startup List
one_line: A startup-data aggregator maintains a live, categorized roster (name, tagline, URL) of YC S26 companies pulled as they launch.
design_notes: Not a designed site — a data-room aggregator page, useful for tracking the rest of the ~150-200-company batch as more sites go live through the July-September program.
take_what: Good source to re-check periodically as more of the batch ships marketing sites over the summer, rather than treating this scout as a one-time snapshot.

name: Product Hunt top-products dashboard (hunted.space)
one_line: Third-party PH tracking dashboard aggregating highest-voted products by category for June-July 2026.
design_notes: Utility dashboard, not itself a design showcase; used to cross-verify vote counts and category rankings beyond PH's own leaderboard pages.
take_what: Sourcing/verification resource, not a design reference.
